title: fix(bin): make Devin config and zellij pane checks work on jq 1.6
body:
## Intent Captain approved via main (corr ae3fc80b33d0b7d7): offer the two extra jq 1.6 fixes (fm-devin-config.sh end keyword; zellij empty-output pane check) upstream as one small PR from firstmate-contrib, no-mistakes, yolo off. Context: review of the jq 1.6 compatibility PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/5406 found these two and skipped them as out of scope there. (1) `bin/fm-devin-config.sh` binds `--arg end` and references `$end`; `end` is a jq keyword, so jq 1.6 rejects the program and Devin config generation fails. (2) `fm_backend_zellij_pane_exists` in `bin/backends/zellij.sh` pipes CLI output straight into `jq -e`; on jq 1.6 empty input exits 0, so a missing pane reads as present. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-devin-config.sh`: renamed the session-end hook variable from `end` to `end_cmd`. The jq program now binds `--arg end_cmd` and uses `$end_cmd`. jq 1.6 rejects `$end` because `end` is a jq keyword, so Devin config generation failed on that jq version. - `bin/backends/zellij.sh`: `fm_backend_zellij_pane_exists` now captures the `list-panes --json` output first. It returns failure if the CLI call fails or prints nothing, and only then passes the output to `jq -e`. On jq 1.6, `jq -e` exits 0 on empty input, so a missing pane read as present. `fm_backend_zellij_tab_matches_label` gets the same exit-status and empty-output guard for `list-tabs`. - `tests/fm-backend-zellij.test.sh`: added a regression test. It checks that `fm_backend_zellij_pane_exists` fails when `list-panes` succeeds with empty stdout. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is small and well-bounded. It renames a jq variable so that jq 1.6 accepts the program; the jq `end` keywords that remain are real syntax. It also adds empty-output and exit-status guards to two zellij predicates. On jq 1.7 and later, both guards give the same result as before. On jq 1.6, they close a false positive that could otherwise let kill close a tab that was not verified. ## Testing I got a real jq 1.6 binary so the tests could show the difference between old and fixed code. The local jq is 1.8.2, which cannot show it. - **Devin config:** I ran fm-devin-config.sh from start to end. Under jq 1.6 the base script fails at compile time on `$end`. The fixed script writes the merged config, mode 600, with all three hooks. It also still works on jq 1.8. - **Zellij checks:** Zellij is not installed on this host, so I sourced the zellij backend functions from the base and fixed commits and gave them a fake zellij CLI. This is not a live test, so the zellij scenarios are marked untested. With the fake CLI on jq 1.6, the base code reports a missing pane or tab as present, for both empty and failing CLI output. The fixed code reports it as absent. Results for valid output are the same. - **Test files:** I ran fm-devin-harness.test.sh under jq 1.6 and it passed. I ran fm-backend-zellij.test.sh under jq 1.6. It shows the new empty-output test passing, but the file exits 1 on one failure: an fm-teardown scout test. That test fails the same way under jq 1.8.2. Its gate refuses with "compatible tasks-axi is required", so the failure seems to come from this host setup and not from this change. I did not run it on the base commit. - **Not done:** I did not do a live Zellij session test because zellij is not installed. No Herdr lab was needed, because this change does not touch Herdr. This change has no UI, so there are no screenshots. - Live validation: ✅ go - 2 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Operator on jq 1.6 generates a Devin worker config: fm-devin-config.sh exits 0 and writes the merged config (mode 600, user settings kept, SessionEnd/Stop/UserPromptSubmit hooks added) | ✅ pass | live | devin-config-jq16.txt: base exits 3 with 'syntax error, unexpected end'; fixed exits 0 and writes the full JSON | | Operator on jq 1.8 still gets the same Devin config (no regression from the end_cmd rename) | ✅ pass | live | devin-config-jq16.txt 'FIXED with jq 1.8' section; fm-devin-harness.test.sh passes | | On jq 1.6, a zellij list-panes call that prints nothing or fails makes pane_exists report the pane as absent, not present | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: zellij is not installed on this host, so only a fake zellij CLI was used (zellij-jq16-matrix.txt). Install zellij to run a live session check. | | On jq 1.6, empty or failed list-tabs output makes tab_matches_label report no match, which closes the target_ready/kill fallback-tab false positive | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: zellij is not installed on this host, so only a fake zellij CLI was used. Install zellij to run a live session check. | | Valid zellij output still gives correct present/absent and match/mismatch results on jq 1.6 and 1.8 | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: zellij is not installed on this host, so only a fake zellij CLI was used. title: fix(bin): correct Claude busy state after fm-control interrupt
body:
## Intent

"Handle blocking worker questions with queued answers. During a merge-request close-out, a worker opened a blocking Ask prompt (a modal question in its own UI) to request merge confirmation, while the answer already waited in its durable instruction inbox. Ordinary fm-send queued another record, but the worker could not read either record while the modal owned the UI. Firstmate recovered by interrupting the prompt through fm-control and resending one corrective line. Update the shared recovery guidance or delivery mechanism so an already-answered blocking prompt is dismissed safely and the queued answer is consumed without repeated stale notifications."

The incident's dismissal step is fixed here: `fm-control.sh <id> interrupt`, the canonical control-plane verb, never corrected Claude's busy ledger after dismissing a blocking prompt, unlike `fm-send.sh`'s legacy `--key Escape` path, which already did. Both now share one correction, `fm_busy_record_manual_interrupt` in `bin/fm-busy-lib.sh`.

Scope was narrowed during review (captain decision, recorded in task status): the escalation-ladder reset needed to also auto-deliver the queued answer and suppress a stale re-notification is real follow-up work, tracked separately, and is not part of this PR. See "Known limitation" below.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-busy-lib.sh`: new `fm_busy_record_manual_interrupt` is the single owner of "what a manual interrupt does to Claude's busy ledger" (idle/`fm-interrupt`, generation-bound, a no-op for every non-hook-based harness).
- `bin/fm-control.sh`: `do_interrupt()` now calls it after a verified interrupt, so `fm-control <id> interrupt` and `fm-send --key Escape` apply the same correction.
- `bin/fm-send.sh`: `fm_send_record_interrupt()` now calls the shared helper instead of a duplicated inline copy of the same logic (one-owner rule).
- `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/references/harness/claude.md`: the busy operating-fact table no longer implies the ledger is left stuck busy after an `fm-control` interrupt.
- `.agents/skills/stuck-crewmate-recovery/SKILL.md`: a new step tells a recovering firstmate to dismiss a blocking harness-owned prompt with `fm-control.sh <id> interrupt` (never answer it by key), then resend only if the queued record needs it.
- `docs/agent-control.md`: updated to state that an interrupt now corrects Claude's busy record, distinguishing that from the pre-existing "does not confirm cancellation" contract, which is unchanged.
- `tests/fm-control.test.sh`: new `test_claude_interrupt_records_interrupt_idle` proves a Claude interrupt classifies `idle fm-interrupt`, the same lifecycle edge `fm-send --key Escape` already covered. The existing unconfirmed-cancel test was moved from `claude` to `codex` so it keeps testing "an unconfirmed cancel must not fabricate a busy-state change" without the new Claude-specific correction changing its meaning.

## Known limitation

The escalation-ladder side of the incident (re-arming an already-escalated inbox notification, and suppressing a stale re-notification for an already-dismissed prompt) is not in this PR. Several review rounds converged on a real residual race between when the watcher durably queues a stale wake and when it later calls its own notification path, which an interrupt landing in that narrow gap can still leave stale. Closing it fully needs the durable wake row and the ladder lock to be invalidated as one atomic step, which is scoped follow-up work rather than a fix folded into this PR's dismissal-only scope.

## Risk Assessment

🟡 Low: the change is a shared, generation-bound, additive correction confined to Claude's busy ledger. It is a no-op for every harness whose busy source is not hook-based, and the existing unconfirmed-cancel guarantee is preserved (now proven on `codex` instead of `claude` so the two lifecycle edges do not conflate).

## Testing

- `tests/fm-control.test.sh`, `tests/fm-send-settle.test.sh` pass.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh`: ShellCheck 0.11.0 passes clean on every changed file. `fm-lint-workflows.sh` reports `actionlint not found` in this environment (the tool is not installed here); this diff touches no `.github/workflows/` file, so there is nothing for it to check.
- Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive by the pipeline's own live-Herdr gate - this worker process is not Herdr-managed (`HERDR_ENV` unset), and Herdr policy prohibits controlling even an isolated lab from outside Herdr, so the pipeline's own live-product step could not run.
- Closest representative path used instead (per the brief's allowance for this exact situation): before opening this PR, I reproduced the incident's dismissal step live, end to end, in an isolated tmux server against a real Claude Code 2.1.280 session - a blocking `AskUserQuestion`-style prompt open, a durable steer already queued in the inbox, `fm-control.sh <id> interrupt` dismissing the prompt without answering it, and Claude's busy ledger left stuck busy before this fix and corrected to `idle`/`fm-interrupt` after it. That reproduction is what the shipped fix and `test_claude_interrupt_records_interrupt_idle` are built from.
- Push, PR, and CI ran outside the no-mistakes pipeline: the pipeline's own account cannot write to `kunchenguid/firstmate` (`git push` returned 403), so I brought the pipeline's fully-reviewed final commit into my worktree, pushed it to my fork, and opened this PR from there. CI on this PR is the first real run of that head against the target repository's checks.

title: fix(bin): stop settled backlog lanes re-escalating an unchanged idle pane
body:
## Intent

Idle alert supression authorised.
This authorizes the existing queued repair that stops correctly held, deliberately parked, or finished child panes from repeatedly re-escalating while preserving alerts for genuinely stalled or newly actionable work.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-watch.sh` gains a `wedge_settled_evidence` consult, run last inside the at-threshold wedge branch (after the wait, worktree-write, and dead-record probes): when a quiet pane's own backlog row is `done` or carries a live hold (captain, external, or parked) and the crew shows no positive working evidence, the pane is deferred to the bounded `FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS` recheck naming whom the wait is on and the action that clears it, instead of re-escalating as a possible wedge every `FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS`; a released or lapsed timed hold, a reopened or absent row, or working evidence drops the marker and restores the unchanged escalation ladder.
- `wait_record`/`wedge_defer_wait` now carry a sixth optional cadence field, separating recheck pacing from the published wait age: the new `.waiting-since-<key>` marker (keyed on settlement, captain-call identity, busy gen, and status signature - deliberately not the pane hash) paces the recheck, while the published age comes only from the age anchor, which now also accepts an `@<epoch>` stamp read from a captain hold's set time; a captain-facing settled wait is absorbed silently while the away-posture record exists and restarts the idle timer. Field-contract validation and `.waiting-since-<key>` cleanup were extended in `clear_stale_hash_tracking` and in `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh`'s pause-tracking reset.
- `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/configuration.md` document the settlement contract, its pacing/publication split and hash-exclusion rationale, and the probe ordering; `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` adds coverage for non-repeating settled absorbs, away-mode captain silence, working/lapsed-hold/released/changed-pane escalation, a busy over-age settled lane, published wait age, agent-incarnation window restart, and the six-field record guard, with `tests/fm-daemon.test.sh` asserting the new anchor is cleared on a terminal signal.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The change is internally correct, fails toward alarming on every failure mode I could construct, and pins both directions with discriminating behavioral tests, but it is a 245-line change to the fleet's stall-detection ladder that deliberately widens detection latency on held/parked/finished lanes (authorized by intent, and already accepted as a no-op in an earlier round), and it leaves one mechanical follow-up: the new backlog read depends on a library fm-watch.sh does not declare, guarded only by tests that skip when tasks-axi is absent.

## Testing

No baseline commands were handed to this phase, so I started by reading the diff, then exercised the change three ways: the six new settled-lane cases plus the extended daemon reset contract (all pass at 0ffc881, each selector run individually rather than running the whole 6,700-line suite); a fails-before/passes-after pass that swapped in the older copy of each implementation file and reproduced exactly the reported symptoms ("possible wedge, escalation 1" on a captain-held lane, a recheck publishing 2s instead of the hold's 172806s, a busy over-age lane that never surfaced at all, and a retained `.waiting-since` anchor after a terminal signal); and thirteen pre-existing wedge-path cases to confirm the shared wait-record and timer paths still behave. Because the end-user surface here is supervisor wake noise rather than a UI, the reviewer-visible evidence is CLI transcripts of the real bin/fm-watch.sh against a hermetic home with a real tasks-axi backlog and a real captain hold: before the fix three rounds of one unchanged held pane produce three escalating wedge wakes ending in demand-deep-inspection, after the fix the same rounds produce zero wakes and no escalation count, followed by a single bounded recheck naming the hold, the captain, the clearing action and the hold's true 172835s age - while an unheld row, a working crew, a released hold and a changed pane each still wake the supervisor. One setup problem was fixed rather than worked around in the product: this host's default PATH carries tasks-axi 0.2.4, below the repo's declared 0.2.6 floor, which made the captain-hold fixtures fail at build; running with a compatible 0.2.6 on PATH made every case pass. The worktree is clean at the target commit with no transient files left behind, and there are no test failures.

<details>
<summary>Evidence: BEFORE - base bin/fm-watch.sh: a captain-held unchanged idle pane escalates on every supervision round</summary>

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Product-level demonstration of the change under test (branch
# fm/fix-held-idle-pane-reescalation): what a supervising turn actually SEES for
# a crewmate pane that is quiet because its own backlog row is held for the
# captain.
#
# The scenario is one real bin/fm-watch.sh process per "supervision round",
# driven against a hermetic firstmate home:
#   - one tmux-backed crew window whose pane content never changes (already
#     surfaced once, the suppressor holds its hash), so every poll goes straight
#     to the wedge timer;
#   - a worker status log whose last line ("working: still tidying the branch")
#     explains nothing;
#   - the crew's current state showing no positive working evidence;
#   - the task's own backlog row held for the captain, written by the real
#     bin/fm-captain-hold.sh.
# FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=1 puts every round at the escalation threshold at once;
# the shipped default only changes how long that takes (240s).
#
# What each round prints is the watcher's own supervisor-facing output: the wake
# reason it emits, plus the durable wake queue a supervising turn drains.
#
# Usage: FM_DEMO_REPO=<worktree> held-lane-noise-demo.sh "<label>"
set -u

REPO=${FM_DEMO_REPO:?set FM_DEMO_REPO to the firstmate worktree}
LABEL=${1:-run}

# shellcheck source=/dev/null
. "$REPO/tests/wake-helpers.sh"
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
. "$REPO/bin/fm-classify-lib.sh"

TMP_ROOT=$(fm_test_tmproot fm-held-lane-demo)
WATCH="$REPO/bin/fm-watch.sh"
DRAIN="$REPO/bin/fm-wake-drain.sh"
WINDOW='crew:ship-docs'
TASK='ship-docs'
KEY=$(printf '%s' "$WINDOW" | tr ':/.' '___')
PANE_TEXT='waiting at the gate'

size_of() { LC_ALL=C wc -c < "$1" | tr -d '[:space:]'; }
file_mtime() { stat -c %Y "$1" 2>/dev/null; }
set_mtime() { touch -t "$(date -d "@$1" +%Y%m%d%H%M.%S)" "$2"; }
seen_sig() {
  printf 'v2\t%s\t%s@%s' "$(status_observed_signature "$1")" "$(size_of "$1")" \
    "$(_fm_open_decisions_file_ident "$1")"
}
wait_poll_cycle() {  # <state> <pid> [limit]
  local state=$1 pid=$2 limit=${3:-300} beat first now i=0
  beat="$state/.last-watcher-beat"
  rm -f "$beat"
  first=''
  while [ "$i" -lt "$limit" ]; do
    kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || return 1
    first=$(file_mtime "$beat"); [ -n "$first" ] && break
    sleep 0.1; i=$((i + 1))
  done
  while [ "$i" -lt "$limit" ]; do
    kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || return 1
    now=$(file_mtime "$beat")
    [ -n "$now" ] && [ "$now" != "$first" ] && return 0
    sleep 0.1; i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}
reap() { kill "$1" 2>/dev/null || true; wait_for_exit "$1" 100 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }

stale_wakes() { awk -F '\t' -v w="$WINDOW" '$3 == "stale" && $4 == w { n++ } END { print n + 0 }' \
  "$STATE/.wake-queue" 2>/dev/null || echo 0; }

# --- the home -----------------------------------------------------------------
DIR=$(make_case held-lane); STATE="$DIR/state"; OUT="$DIR/watch.out"
mkdir -p "$DIR/config" "$DIR/data"
printf '%s' "$PANE_TEXT" > "$DIR/pane.txt"
printf 'window=%s\nkind=ship\nharness=grok\nbackend=tmux\n' "$WINDOW" > "$STATE/$TASK.meta"
printf 'working: still tidying the branch\n' > "$STATE/$TASK.status"
printf '%s' "$(seen_sig "$STATE/$TASK.status")" > "$STATE/.seen-${TASK}_status"
printf '%s' "$(hash_text "$PANE_TEXT")" > "$STATE/.hash-$KEY"
printf '1\n' > "$STATE/.count-$KEY"
printf '%s' "$(hash_text "$PANE_TEXT")" > "$STATE/.stale-$KEY"

cp "$REPO/.tasks.toml" "$DIR/.tasks.toml"
printf '## In flight\n\n## Queued\n\n## Done\n' > "$DIR/data/backlog.md"
( cd "$DIR" && tasks-axi add "$TASK" 'refresh the architecture docs' --file data/backlog.md ) >/dev/null
( cd "$DIR" && tasks-axi start "$TASK" --file data/backlog.md ) >/dev/null
FM_HOME="$DIR" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$STATE" FM_DATA_OVERRIDE="$DIR/data" FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$DIR/config" \
  "$REPO/bin/fm-captain-hold.sh" hold "$TASK" \
  --reason 'awaiting the captain on whether to land the docs rewrite' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || { echo "FATAL: could not record the captain hold"; exit 1; }

# Backdate the hold's own recorded set time by two days, so the transcript shows
# the age a recheck publishes for a hold the captain has really been sitting on.
HELD_SINCE=$(( $(date +%s) - 172800 ))
HELD_STAMP=$(date -u -d "@$HELD_SINCE" +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
sed -i "s/^  Captain hold set: .*Z\$/  Captain hold set: $HELD_STAMP/" "$DIR/data/backlog.md"

echo "================================================================"
echo "$LABEL"
echo "================================================================"
echo "crew window        : $WINDOW  (pane content unchanged every poll)"
echo "worker status line : $(cat "$STATE/$TASK.status")"
echo "crew current state : state: working - source: status-log - still tidying the branch"
echo "backlog row        : $(grep -A 3 -F "$TASK" "$DIR/data/backlog.md" | sed -n '1,4p' | tr '\n' '|')"
echo

OFFSET=0
round() {  # <label> <pause-resurface-secs>
  local label=$1 resurface=$2 pid cycles=0 exited=0 before after new
  before=$(stale_wakes)
  PATH="$DIR/fakebin:$PATH" FM_FAKE_TMUX_WINDOW="$WINDOW" FM_FAKE_TMUX_CAPTURE="$DIR/pane.txt" \
    FM_FAKE_TMUX_CURRENT_COMMAND=grok \
    FM_FAKE_CREW_STATE='state: working · source: status-log · still tidying the branch' \
    FM_WATCH_HANDLING_SUCCESSOR=1 \
    FM_HOME="$DIR" FM_DATA_OVERRIDE="$DIR/data" FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$DIR/config" \
    FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$STATE" FM_CREW_STATE_BIN="$DIR/fakebin/fm-crew-state.sh" \
    FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=1 FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS="$resurface" \
    FM_POLL=1 FM_SIGNAL_GRACE=1 FM_CHECK_INTERVAL=999999 FM_HEARTBEAT=999999 \
    "$WATCH" >> "$OUT" 2>&1 &
  pid=$!
  while [ "$cycles" -lt 3 ]; do
    if ! wait_poll_cycle "$STATE" "$pid" 300; then exited=1; break; fi
    cycles=$((cycles + 1))
  done
  [ "$exited" -eq 1 ] || reap "$pid"
  new=$(tail -c "+$((OFFSET + 1))" "$OUT" 2>/dev/null | sed '/^$/d')
  OFFSET=$(size_of "$OUT")
  after=$(stale_wakes)
  printf -- '--- %s\n' "$label"
  if [ -n "$new" ]; then
    printf 'watcher surfaced and exited, waking the supervisor with:\n'
    printf '    %s\n' "$new"
  else
    printf 'watcher stayed running: nothing surfaced, no supervising turn spent\n'
  fi
  printf 'wake queue entries for this window: %s (was %s)\n' "$after" "$before"
  printf 'wedge escalation count on record   : %s\n' \
    "$(cat "$STATE/.wedge-escalations-$KEY" 2>/dev/null || echo '(none)')"
  if [ "$after" -gt "$before" ]; then
    printf 'what the supervising turn drains  :\n'
    FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$STATE" "$DRAIN" 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1,12p' | sed 's/^/    /'
    ack_cycle
  fi
  echo
}

ack_cycle() {
  local err sequence generation
  err="$STATE/.demo-drain.err"
  FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$STATE" "$DRAIN" >/dev/null 2> "$err" || true
  sequence=$(sed -n 's/.*--ack-through \([0-9][0-9]*\) --recovery-generation \([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\)$/\1/p' "$err")
  generation=$(sed -n 's/.*--ack-through [0-9][0-9]* --recovery-generation \([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\)$/\1/p' "$err")
  rm -f "$err"
  [ -n "$sequence" ] && [ -n "$generation" ] || return 0
  FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$STATE" "$DRAIN" --ack-through "$sequence" \
    --recovery-generation "$generation" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

round 'supervision round 1 (idle threshold reached)' 999
round 'supervision round 2 (same unchanged pane)' 999
round 'supervision round 3 (same unchanged pane)' 999

echo '--- and then the long bounded recheck the absorb still owes'
if [ -e "$STATE/.waiting-since-$KEY" ]; then
  echo "settled-wait record on disk: state/.waiting-since-$KEY"
  echo "  identity: $(cat "$STATE/.waiting-since-$KEY")"
  echo "aging it past FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS (240s here, 14400s shipped default)"
  set_mtime "$(( $(date +%s) - 5000 ))" "$STATE/.waiting-since-$KEY"
  round 'supervision round 4 (recheck cadence elapsed)' 240
else
  echo 'no settled-wait record exists: this watcher has no bounded recheck for a'
  echo 'held lane at all, which is why the rounds above keep escalating instead.'
fi

echo '=== end of transcript ==='
```

  printf '%s' "$(hash_text "$PANE_TEXT")" > "$STATE/.hash-$KEY"
  printf '1\n' > "$STATE/.count-$KEY"
  printf '%s' "$(hash_text "$PANE_TEXT")" > "$STATE/.stale-$KEY"
  cp "$REPO/.tasks.toml" "$DIR/.tasks.toml"
  printf '## In flight\n\n## Queued\n\n## Done\n' > "$DIR/data/backlog.md"
  ( cd "$DIR" && tasks-axi add "$TASK" 'refresh the architecture docs' --file data/backlog.md ) >/dev/null
  ( cd "$DIR" && tasks-axi start "$TASK" --file data/backlog.md ) >/dev/null
}

hold_for_captain() {
  FM_HOME="$DIR" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$STATE" FM_DATA_OVERRIDE="$DIR/data" \
    FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$DIR/config" "$REPO/bin/fm-captain-hold.sh" hold "$TASK" \
    --reason 'awaiting the captain on whether to land the docs rewrite' >/dev/null 2>&1
}

answer_and_release() {
  printf 'go ahead and land it\n' > "$DIR/decision.txt"
  FM_HOME="$DIR" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$STATE" FM_DATA_OVERRIDE="$DIR/data" \
    FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$DIR/config" "$REPO/bin/fm-captain-hold.sh" answer "$TASK" \
    --decision-file "$DIR/decision.txt" --release >/dev/null 2>&1
}

ack_cycle() {
  local err sequence generation
  err="$STATE/.demo-drain.err"
  FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$STATE" "$DRAIN" >/dev/null 2> "$err" || true
  sequence=$(sed -n 's/.*--ack-through \([0-9][0-9]*\) --recovery-generation \([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\)$/\1/p' "$err")
  generation=$(sed -n 's/.*--ack-through [0-9][0-9]* --recovery-generation \([A-Za-z0-9._-]*\)$/\1/p' "$err")
  rm -f "$err"
  [ -n "$sequence" ] && [ -n "$generation" ] || return 0
  FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$STATE" "$DRAIN" --ack-through "$sequence" \
    --recovery-generation "$generation" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

round() {  # <crew-state> -> prints what the watcher surfaced, or nothing
  local verdict=$1 pid cycles=0 exited=0 new
  PATH="$DIR/fakebin:$PATH" FM_FAKE_TMUX_WINDOW="$WINDOW" FM_FAKE_TMUX_CAPTURE="$DIR/pane.txt" \
    FM_FAKE_TMUX_CURRENT_COMMAND=grok FM_FAKE_CREW_STATE="$verdict" \
    FM_WATCH_HANDLING_SUCCESSOR=1 \
    FM_HOME="$DIR" FM_DATA_OVERRIDE="$DIR/data" FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$DIR/config" \
    FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$STATE" FM_CREW_STATE_BIN="$DIR/fakebin/fm-crew-state.sh" \
    FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=1 FM_PAUSE_RESURFACE_SECS=999 \
    FM_POLL=1 FM_SIGNAL_GRACE=1 FM_CHECK_INTERVAL=999999 FM_HEARTBEAT=999999 \
    "$WATCH" >> "$OUT" 2>&1 &
  pid=$!
  while [ "$cycles" -lt 3 ]; do
    if ! wait_poll_cycle "$STATE" "$pid" 300; then exited=1; break; fi
    cycles=$((cycles + 1))
  done
  [ "$exited" -eq 1 ] || reap "$pid"
  new=$(tail -c "+$((OFFSET + 1))" "$OUT" 2>/dev/null | sed '/^$/d')
  OFFSET=$(size_of "$OUT")
  if [ -n "$new" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$new"; fi
  ack_cycle
}

report() {  # <variant> <expectation> <surfaced-text>
  printf -- '--- %s\n' "$1"
  printf '    must still alert: %s\n' "$2"
  if [ -n "$3" ]; then
    printf '    supervisor woken: %s\n' "$3"
  else
    printf '    supervisor woken: (nothing surfaced)\n'
  fi
  printf '    wedge escalations on record: %s\n\n' \
    "$(cat "$STATE/.wedge-escalations-$KEY" 2>/dev/null || echo '(none)')"
}

echo '================================================================'
echo 'STILL ALERTS - lanes the authorised suppression must not swallow'
echo '================================================================'
echo "same unchanged idle pane and same real bin/fm-watch.sh as the held-lane"
echo "transcript; one supervision round each, FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS=1"
echo

build_home open-row
report 'backlog row In flight, not held (nothing explains the quiet)' \
  'possible wedge' "$(round "$IDLE_STATE")"

build_home held-but-working
hold_for_captain
report 'row held for the captain, but the crew IS working (run-step)' \
  'possible wedge - a working task that stops responding is the real wedge' \
  "$(round "$WORKING_STATE")"

build_home released-hold
hold_for_captain
printf '    (first round with the hold live, expected silent: "%s")\n' "$(round "$IDLE_STATE")"
answer_and_release
report 'the captain answered and released the hold: newly actionable' \
  'possible wedge again, within one FM_STALE_ESCALATE_SECS' \
  "$(round "$IDLE_STATE")"

build_home changed-pane
hold_for_captain
printf '    (first round with the hold live, expected silent: "%s")\n' "$(round "$IDLE_STATE")"
printf 'the worker printed something new' > "$DIR/pane.txt"
report 'held lane whose pane changed: a new sighting' \
  'the plain first-sight stale wake' "$(round "$IDLE_STATE")"

echo '=== end of transcript ==='
```

title: fix(bin): preserve the allowlisted launcher environment across secondmate relaunch
body:
## Intent The developer wanted to resubmit an upstream Firstmate fix to kunchenguid/firstmate, raised as a PR from the public fork Thoughts-One/firstmate-contrib: keep the allowlisted launcher environment when a secondmate relaunches. For local secondmate launches and relaunches only, allowlisted variable names other than TRACEPARENT should be captured fresh from the launching process's own environment, not from stale destination-pane values. Every other launch kind, including remote secondmates, keeps its existing behavior. The fix was to be ported from the more complete private branch onto current upstream main, and the PR had to state that it supersedes the closed PR #4850, whose author closed it unmerged after incomplete live validation. That validation gap had to be closed first, only in isolated labs and never against a real session: an ordinary worker launch, the interaction between a dedicated TRACEPARENT carrier and an allowlisted TRACEPARENT, and a Herdr-backed secondmate restart. Constraints included following upstream CONTRIBUTING.md (fm-lint must pass, the change must work on macOS Bash 3.2 and Linux, one Markdown sentence per line, accurate usage headers), shipping only through no-mistakes and never with --yes, and keeping fleet-specific host names, private repos, runner labels, and local paths out of the commits and the PR. ## What Changed - When `config/launch-env-allowlist` is enabled, `fm-spawn.sh` now handles local secondmate spawns and relaunches differently. It captures each allowlisted name that is set in the launching process into a private, mode-0600 one-launch file at `$STATE/.launch-env`. The fixed operational names and `TRACEPARENT` are excluded, so the dedicated `TRACEPARENT` launch path stays authoritative. The pane sources this file, deletes it, and then starts the worker, so values never appear in the launch text. Ordinary launches and remote secondmates keep the previous behavior: values expand in the destination pane. - The snapshot is cleaned up on abort in `fm-spawn.sh` and on teardown in `fm-teardown.sh`. A capture that finds no values also removes an old snapshot. The operational-floor name list moved into a shared helper. - `docs/configuration.md` now documents the local-secondmate exception, how `TRACEPARENT` is handled, and why remote secondmates are excluded. Regression tests cover the secondmate relaunch boundary, the `TRACEPARENT` guard, and snapshot cleanup on teardown. This PR replaces the closed PR #4850. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is limited to local secondmate launches when an allowlist exists: remote secondmates, ordinary launches, and TRACEPARENT keep their existing paths, a failed or interrupted delivery leaves no worker without its environment, and the fix-round edits (a TRACEPARENT-guard test that runs the emitted launch and fails without the guard, stale-snapshot removal on empty capture, and a revert of the unrelated trace-context test edit) are minimal and correct. ## Testing I drove the real fm-spawn.sh against a throwaway Herdr lab session and tore it down in the same run; the default session's tripwire stayed unchanged. The lab server was started with different, stale values for the allowlisted names, so each result shows which source a worker actually used. I read each worker's real environment from a probe it wrote at startup, and captured the pane text to check for leaks. What the lab showed: - **Local secondmate:** receives the launcher's values exactly, including an empty value, an unset name, and a value containing shell-injection text that did not run. The one-launch snapshot is private and gone once the worker starts, and the value never appears in the pane text. - **Secondmate restart:** picks up fresh launcher values. A restart that captures nothing deletes a leftover credential snapshot instead of loading it. - **Ordinary workers:** still take values from the destination pane and get no snapshot. - **TRACEPARENT:** with it allowlisted and set in the launcher, both a secondmate and an ordinary worker receive the carrier recorded in their meta, not the launcher's value. **Not driven live:** - **Remote secondmate:** needs a second host. The new unit test covers it and passes. - **`fm-control relaunch` against a live agent in Herdr:** needs a Herdr-registered claude harness to prove the old agent exited. The restart path ran live instead, and the relaunch unit tests pass. **Host problems worked around:** 353 `/tmp/fm-*` directories owned by another local user, `gha-runner`, block spawn's hardcoded `/tmp/fm-<id>` path, so I re-ran the unit tests with a private tmpfs `/tmp`. A tasks-axi 0.2.5 < 0.2.6 version gate fails older backlog-transition tests this change doesn't touch. This is a CLI/terminal change with no graphical UI, so the evidence is text: the worker environment files, the pane captures and the lab logs. - Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Ordinary worker launch in a Herdr lab keeps expanding allowlisted names from the destination pane, with no snapshot file and no launcher value in the pane text | ✅ pass | live | herdr-lab-final.log (A: 4 PASS), A-worker-env.txt, A-pane-capture.txt | | Local secondmate spawn in a Herdr lab receives the launcher's allowlisted values (verbatim value, empty stays empty, unset stays unset) instead of stale pane values; non-allowlisted names filtered; in… | ✅ pass | live | herdr-lab-final.log (B: 7 PASS), B-secondmate-env.txt, B-pane-capture.txt | | Herdr-backed secondmate restart (pane killed, then recovery respawn) captures fresh launcher values and drops a name the launcher no longer sets | ✅ pass | live | herdr-lab-final.log (C: 2 PASS), C-secondmate-restart-env.txt | | Adversarial: a secondmate restart that captures nothing deletes a leftover launch-env snapshot holding an old credential and does not load it | ✅ pass | live | herdr-lab-final.log (E: 2 PASS), E-secondmate-env.txt | | Adversarial: with trace context on and TRACEPARENT allowlisted, a launcher TRACEPARENT never overrides the recorded carrier, for a local secondmate or an ordinary worker, and other allowlisted values… | ✅ pass | live | herdr-lab-final.log (D: 4 PASS), D-secondmate-env.txt, D-ordinary-env.txt | | `fm-control relaunch` of a local secondmate uses launcher values, not the reused pane's | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: only the unit tests in tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh ran, and they passed. title: feat(harness): add Mirasim Claude wrapper alongside Devin
body:
## Why

Add `mirasim` as a selectable Claude-wrapper harness for workers and scouts, preserving the current Devin adapter and launch-prompt behavior.
This replaces the Mirasim proposal at https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/5272 and includes its locally retained nested owner-path correction.
The earlier proposal and the separate skill/quiet proposal at https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/5273 remain untouched.

## Scope

- Resolve and quote the Mirasim executable and model, preserve its route identity, and reuse Claude trust, permission mode, lifecycle hooks, steering, interrupt, exit, and recovery wiring.
- Keep Mirasim limited to workers and scouts, validate its supported effort range, and preserve Devin's separate control and hook contracts.
- Add adapter, coexistence, live-guard inventory, and owner-path regressions. Quiet and AFK behavior is unchanged.

## Verification

- Passed 10 focused portable scripts through `bin/fm-test-run.sh`: Mirasim, Devin, Claude trust, bootstrap, dispatch resolution, adapter references, documentation audiences, control, composer ghosts, and busy-adapter wiring.
- Passed `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`, `bin/fm-lint.sh` with pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0/actionlint 1.7.12, and the 226-script coverage inventory guard.
- Passed `FM_MIRASIM_LIVE_E2E=1 bin/fm-test-run.sh --per-script-timeout-secs 120 tests/fm-mirasim-live-e2e.test.sh` with Mirasim 0.0.303 and Claude Code 2.1.278. One synthetic request completed through the authenticated relay with both required hook events.
- Initial fixture-layout failures were retained as evidence, then resolved by rerunning against the real worktree with a task-owned temporary directory outside the source root.

## Limitations

The live check covers one authenticated headless turn and real UserPromptSubmit/Stop hooks. Interactive terminal steering, interrupt, exit, and relaunch were not refreshed, and served-model identity and quota coverage remain unproven.
This is direct-PR delivery by explicit operator instruction. No no-mistakes pipeline or attestation was produced; the upstream no-mistakes requirement remains unmet.

title: feat(bin): read the TypeSafe dispatch key from the macOS Keychain
body:
## Intent Make firstmate read the TypeSafe (Jev) API key from the macOS Keychain. Context: bin/fm-dispatch-resolve.sh enables typed dispatch resolution only when TYPESAFE_API_KEY is set in the process environment or as a TYPESAFE_API_KEY= line in the home's .env. The operator's standing policy is that this key never lives in .env or any plain file; it is stored in the macOS login Keychain as a generic password with service name `typesafe-api-key`. Today that means the resolver stays off on this machine even though the key is available. Run the pipeline on this branch through to a PR. In the PR description, state plainly that the Keychain fallback only activates when an operator has stored a key under that Keychain service, so it is opt-in exactly like the existing .env line and does not change the default for anyone who has not done so. ## What Changed - Added `fm_typesafe_key` to `bin/fm-env-lib.sh`. It looks for the typed dispatch key in the process environment first, then in the `TYPESAFE_API_KEY=` line of `$FM_HOME/.env`, and last in the macOS Keychain generic password for service `typesafe-api-key` (via `security find-generic-password -s typesafe-api-key -w`). If `security` is missing, the Keychain has no such item, or the secret can't be read, that source counts as absent. `bin/fm-dispatch-resolve.sh` and `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` now both use this helper, so the resolver's opt-in gate and bootstrap's resolver-field validation and harness routing always agree. The "off" message on stderr now names the Keychain service as a third source. `bin/fm-test-run.sh` now also maps `bin/fm-env-lib.sh` changes to the `session-bootstrap` test family. - **The Keychain fallback is opt-in, just like the existing `.env` line.** It only takes effect when an operator has stored a key under the `typesafe-api-key` Keychain service. If nobody has, the resolver stays off and dispatch works exactly as before. The environment and `.env` still take precedence over the Keychain. - Tests in `tests/fm-dispatch-resolve.test.sh` and `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` use a stubbed `security`, so they never touch the real Keychain. They cover: a Keychain-only key turns the resolver and bootstrap validation on; a missing `security` command, a missing item, or an unreadable secret leaves them off; the environment and `.env` win without querying the Keychain; and the key reaches `curl` only as the header read from a file descriptor, never on `security`'s argv. `docs/configuration.md` documents the source order and the `security add-generic-password` command for storing the key. Its heading is renamed to "Typed dispatch resolution", and the anchor links in `AGENTS.md`, the quota-array-dispatch skill, and the verification docs are updated to match. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change adds an opt-in Keychain fallback through one shared helper (fm_typesafe_key), used by both the resolver and bootstrap. It keeps env → .env → Keychain precedence, keeps the secret off argv, logs and child environments, and turns nothing on for anyone without a stored `typesafe-api-key` item. The two findings from earlier rounds are verifiably resolved and covered by hermetic tests that use a fake `security`. ## Testing I ran the real resolver and bootstrap from a throwaway FM_HOME, using the operator's real Keychain item (read-only), real curl to api.typesafe.ai and real quota-axi. I also ran the resolver test script and the bootstrap crew-dispatch test case on their own. - **Keychain-only key:** the resolver returned `status: clear` from jev-1.13.0 (rule_1, confidence 1.0, `--harness claude --model claude-sonnet-5 --effort low`). The only resolver `security` call was `find-generic-password -s typesafe-api-key -w`. - **Precedence:** bogus keys in the environment and in `.env` each drew an HTTP 401 from the real API, and `security` was never called. So those sources win and the Keychain is not consulted. - **Default off:** with an empty HOME (the real `security` finds no item, exit 44) and with no `security` binary at all, the resolver printed only `dispatch-resolve: off (...Keychain service typesafe-api-key)` on stderr, exited 0 and made no network call. - **Bootstrap:** it reported `approval must be "captain"` and accepted `gemini` only when the Keychain key was reachable. Without it, it stayed silent on approval and reported `unverified harness: gemini`, same as before this change. - **Secret handling:** the key never showed up in stdout, stderr, the curl or security argv logs, bootstrap output, or any evidence file. - **Automated tests:** both passed. The noisy `fatal: not a git repository` lines in the bootstrap log come from its non-git temp homes, not from a test failure. Not tested live: a Keychain item whose metadata can be read but whose secret cannot. Producing it would mean changing the operator's login Keychain. The bootstrap test covers it with a fake `security`. No Herdr lab was needed; the change does not touch Herdr lifecycle. It has no UI, so there are no screenshots; the CLI transcript is the user-facing evidence. The PR-description requirement in the intent belongs to the later PR phase and was not exercised here. - Live validation: ✅ go - 7 of 8 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | With the key only in the macOS Keychain (no env var, no .env), the operator runs fm-dispatch-resolve.sh and gets a typed dispatch answer instead of 'off' | ✅ pass | live | live-keychain-transcript.txt S1: status clear from jev-1.13.0 via one real call to https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone. When the item's metadata is readable but its secret is not, bootstrap reports typed resolution active every session, but the resolver either stops at an access prompt or turns itself off. Firstmate runs the resolver unattended on every dispatch (AGENTS.md:238). Each run of `security -w` then opens a macOS dialog asking permission to use the stored secret, and the resolver waits for someone to answer it. This does not happen on your machine: jev.py already reads the item with the same `security -w` command. title: fix(bin): support jq 1.6 in fm-contributions and the cmux backend
body:
## Intent The captain chose A: proceed with a. All 13 upstream PRs in the triage report are approved, opened from Thoughts-One/firstmate-contrib. This PR: Upstream: jq 1.6 compatibility in fm-contributions and the cmux backend. From the triage report's item 2: bin/fm-contributions.sh binds a jq --arg as $label and then references $label as a jq variable; jq 1.6 refuses a reserved word as a bound $-name, so observing an issue's ready-for-pr label fails outright on that jq version, and this is confirmed still present on current upstream. Separately, fm_backend_cmux_surface_exists in bin/backends/cmux.sh pipes a possibly-empty CLI call straight into jq -e; jq's --exit-status only started reporting wholly empty stdin as a distinct nonzero exit from jq 1.7 onward, while jq 1.6 exits 0 on empty input, so a failed or targetless call would read a genuinely absent surface as present on jq 1.6. This is runtime code shipped to every cmux-backend user, not just CI, and is also confirmed still unfixed on current upstream. Both fixes are fully general, not specific to the private fork or its fleet. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-contributions.sh`: The ready-for-pr label in `observe()` now goes to jq as `--arg ready_label`, not `--arg label`. `label` is a reserved word in jq, so jq 1.6 refused `$label` as a variable name and the ready-for-pr label check failed. - `bin/backends/cmux.sh`: `fm_backend_cmux_surface_exists` now stores the `list-panes` output before it runs `jq -e`. It returns failure if the CLI call fails or prints nothing. Before, jq 1.6 exited 0 on empty input, so a failed call reported a missing surface as present. - `tests/fm-backend-cmux.test.sh`: A new regression test checks that `fm_backend_cmux_surface_exists` fails when `list-panes` succeeds with empty stdout. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is small: it renames one jq variable to avoid the reserved `$label` name, and it checks the cmux list-panes result for failure or empty output before running `jq -e`. Both fixes match the stated intent. The only behavior change is that a failed CLI call now returns early. ## Testing I drove both changed runtime paths under the real jq 1.6 release binary, on the base commit and on the target commit. Before the fix, `fm-contributions.sh` issue observation failed with `unexpected label` compile errors. After the fix, the ready-for-pr label becomes one durable wake, and ack and replay work on both jq 1.6 and jq 1.8. Before the fix, `fm_backend_cmux_surface_exists` read an empty or failed cmux CLI call as a live surface under jq 1.6. After the fix, it reports absent in both cases, and the real present and absent answers still hold. The whole cmux adapter test file passes under jq 1.6. The new regression test fails on the base code and passes on the target code. I did not run a Herdr lab because the change does not touch Herdr. I used no real cmux binary: the fake CLI covers the exact empty and failure outputs that the fix guards. Temporary jq binaries and the base-tree copy were deleted, and the worktree is clean. - Live validation: ✅ go - 4 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | On jq 1.6, polling a filed GitHub issue that has the ready-for-pr label records a ready-for-pr pending event and one durable wake. The new test fails on base and passes on target under jq 1.6. | | cmux surface_exists still returns true for a live surface and false for a different surface on jq 1.6 and 1.8. The whole cmux adapter test file passes under jq 1.6. | ✅ pass | live | cmux-surface-exists-matrix.txt (present exit=0, absent exit=1 for both jq versions); `tests/fm-backend-cmux.test.sh` exit 0 under jq 1.6 | | surface_exists against a real running cmux application on a jq 1.6 host | ⏸️ untested | no | This Linux host has no cmux binary or session. The empty-output and failure paths were driven through the adapter with a fake CLI. To run it against the real app, use a macOS host that has cmux instal… |

title: fix(bin): wait for the Herdr presentation lock on exact resume
body:
## Intent The captain chose A: "proceed with a". All 13 upstream PRs in the triage report are approved, opened from Thoughts-One/firstmate-contrib. This PR: Upstream: Herdr exact-resume presentation-order lock waits instead of failing. The exact-resume path in bin/fm-spawn.sh's spawn_herdr_presentation_order_lock_acquire shares the same bounded, give-up-after-50-attempts lock acquire as the new-task-create path. On lock contention this hard-fails the resume instead of waiting, even though a concurrent recovery may legitimately be holding that lock, and the create path's flat-layout fallback is not a safe response for a resume that is recovering one specific existing identity rather than starting fresh. Give the exact-resume call site a wait mode that waits for the lock instead of giving up after a bounded number of attempts, while leaving the create call site's existing bounded-then-flat-fallback behavior unchanged. ## What Changed - `spawn_herdr_presentation_order_lock_acquire` in `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now accepts an optional `wait` mode. This mode calls `fm_lock_acquire_wait` and does not stop after 50 attempts. The exact-resume (presentation recovery) call site uses `wait`, so lock contention no longer fails the resume. The new-task create path keeps its bounded attempt and its fallback to the flat layout. Dead-owner reclaim still stops the wait when a lock holder has crashed. - The header comments in `bin/fm-spawn.sh` and the operational compromises in `docs/herdr-backend.md` now say that recovery waits for the shared presentation lock. It does not refuse the spawn. The docs also note that a recovery spawn can block while another process holds the lock. - `tests/fm-backend-herdr-presentation-e2e.test.sh` has a new real-Herdr lab case. A separate process holds the session lock for 30 seconds. The case then checks that the resume waits for the lock and succeeds. It also checks that the resume keeps the same workspace, replaces the old husk pane, and does not change focus. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change adds a narrow `wait` mode used only at the exact-resume call site, reuses the repo's existing `fm_lock_acquire_wait` idiom, and leaves the create path's bounded attempt and flat-fallback behavior (plus the abort-cleanup call) unchanged. Every other presentation-lock holder (teardown, kill, session cleanup, create spawns) uses try or bounded acquisition and takes the per-task meta lock before the presentation lock, so the unbounded wait cannot form a deadlock cycle. ## Testing I ran the real-Herdr presentation E2E twice in isolated fm-lab-* sessions through bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh. title: fix: preserve answers from list-form Lavish results

## Intent Contribute the upstream fix for kunchenguid/firstmate issue #4726 as a pull request from the fork. Issue #4726: when a Lavish result is emitted in list form (`prompts[N]:` followed by `- uid: ...` entries) instead of the table form (`prompts[N]{uid,prompt,selector,tag,text}:`), `bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh read` prints declared_items 0, presented_items 0, complete: yes, and `answers` closes nothing, so the captain's board answers are silently dropped. Expected: `read` and `answers` parse both emission forms, or refuse loudly with malformed_items > 0 rather than reporting a complete empty result; a feedback result whose raw prompts[N] header declares N > 0 while the parser finds 0 must never print complete: yes. Reproduced on 2026-09-23 with lavish-axi 0.1.68 without any attachment: 6 of 19 prompt rows carried an extra `target` field, the rows were no longer uniform, and lavish-axi used the list form. A real captured example is at ~/fm-homes/primary/data/fm-lavish-list-form/sample-list-form.result (private board content; use it to understand the shape, but build any committed test fixture from synthetic text, never from this file). ## What Changed - Share parsing across `read`, `answers`, and `reconciles` to support both table-form and list-form Lavish results, preserving item fields while skipping nested targets and attachments. - Mark malformed or count-mismatched results incomplete and make answer extraction fail explicitly; recognize list-form blocks as queued content. - Add synthetic regression coverage for list-form presentation, choice extraction, nested content, and declared-but-unparsed results. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The bounded parser change supports both emission forms, flags incomplete results, and preserves existing answer-intake controls. ## Testing Focused synthetic-capture checks passed, and base-versus-target CLI transcripts demonstrate the regression and fix. title: fix(bin): surface suspected worker loops at parked gates
body:
## Intent

Upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/4795 (maintainer triage 2026-09-18: ready-for-pr, class restore): a no-mistakes ship worker whose run parked at its `fix-review` gate did not idle. While it waited for the supervisor's gate decision it re-ran `no-mistakes axi status` and similar read-only commands in a tight loop, about 900 tool commands, and reached about 79% of its context window before the decision landed. Because the harness showed activity every few seconds, the watcher read it as a healthy busy pane, so the park never surfaced as parked or stale and the supervisor had no signal that the worker was spinning.

This task delivers only the watcher-side remedy the issue proposes: many identical read-only commands with no run-step change become a distinct looping classification that wakes the supervisor, instead of reading as a healthy busy pane.

The brief-side remedy (a parked worker appends one status line and ends its turn, no status polling) is left to https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/4859, which is open and already carries it. The classification must be correct whether or not 4859 has landed, and must not restate or contradict its brief-side rules.

Boundaries that matter more than the fix: a worker genuinely making progress must keep reading as working, and a parked worker must stay resumable by an ordinary steer.

Out of scope: rate-limiting or refusing repeated status calls inside no-mistakes itself; that is the no-mistakes repository and separate work.

## What Changed

- Add configurable, inspection-only `looping` alarms for busy no-mistakes workers at unchanged parked gates without detected worktree writes; document that distinct read-only work can also trigger this proxy.
- Reset tracking on gate changes, worktree writes, observed idle states, or worker replacement while preserving ordinary steering and tracking through notification churn.
- Preserve looping alarms through daemon triage and retain unread status events and diagnostics in enriched escalations; add watcher and daemon regression coverage.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: No new material defects found; the inspection-only behavior preserves status delivery and steering, while the previously accepted proxy retains false-positive risk.

## Testing

Eleven watcher regressions, five daemon regressions, and a repeated-alarm probe passed with fixtures; both pre-fix reproductions failed as expected. Queue and escalation evidence was captured, temporary files were removed, and live validation remained blocked by the unavailable initialized gate and this phase's authority boundary.

- Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 0 of 8 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A worker repeatedly reads an unchanged parked gate; the supervisor receives a durable looping alarm, with subsequent alarms incrementing the escalation count. | ⏸️ untested | no | No real parked run is accessible from this uninitialized worktree. The outer executor must provide an authorized disposable parked run. |
| A worker advances its run step or writes its worktree and remains working without a looping alarm. | ⏸️ untested | no | A controllable live parked run is unavailable; creating or advancing one is outside this phase's authority. Provide that isolated setup for live validation. |
| An observed non-busy transition or a new busy generation clears the previous looping episode. | ⏸️ untested | no | No live worker bound to a parked gate was available. Provide an authorized disposable worker and gate to exercise its lifecycle. |
| Pi-family notifications and OpenCode retry updates cannot hide a continuing loop, including in away or quiet mode. | ⏸️ untested | no | These checks used fixture harness events. Live proof requires authorized isolated harnesses, a parked run, and a supervisor endpoint. |
| A busy worker without a stored busy record still qualifies through its existing transcript, rendered, or native backend state. | ⏸️ untested | no | Actual harness sessions at a parked gate were unavailable; the test supplied fixture busy sources. Provide authorized isolated sessions for live verification. |
| An ordinary steer reaches a looping worker, which resumes without automatic interruption or restart. | ⏸️ untested | no | The steering test used a terminal stub. A real parked worker and authorized supervisor endpoint are required to demonstrate resumption. |
| The daemon delivers unread questions and unreadable-status diagnostics alongside looping or wedge alarms, without losing or duplicating acknowledged events. | ⏸️ untested | no | Daemon handlers passed with fixture inputs, but no isolated live worker/supervisor flow was provisioned. Provide that environment to verify actual delivery. |
| Default, zero, and invalid settings retain the 900-second window, while repeated watcher starts respect the gate-probe interval. | ⏸️ untested | no | Timing checks used fixture state and adjusted timestamps. A real parked run must be provided for live timing validation. |

<details>
<summary>Evidence: Fixture-based watcher output: durable looping alarms and escalation 2</summary>

Source: [Fixture-based watcher output: durable looping alarms and escalation 2](https://github.com/mremond/firstmate/blob/92bbe740b6f47c982ef998c471b204c11e49ba11/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-4795-parked-worker-polls-its-gate/watcher-loop-output.txt)

title: fix(bin): stagger repeated same-host SSH launches during bootstrap fan-out
body:
## Intent

The captain approved proceeding with all 13 upstream PRs recommended in the private-fork triage report (chose option "a").

This PR is item 11 from that report: stagger repeated same-host SSH launches during bootstrap fan-out.

The underlying bug: during Firstmate's concurrent bootstrap fan-out (the secondmate liveness sweep and the remote convergence loop), simultaneous cold SSH connections from one home to the same remote secondmate host can hit that host's SSH connection-rate limit and drop connections. This was evidenced by 3 of 18 same-instant connections dropping with no spacing, while the same 6 connections all succeeded once spaced by 0.4 seconds apart.

The fix: space the Nth launch bound for one configured remote host within a single concurrent bootstrap batch by a fixed 0.4 seconds per repeat, inside that launch's own worker after it has already been forked, so the parent dispatch loop never blocks. Every other host, and every local launch, still fires immediately and runs exactly as before; no SSH command is retried.

Which host gets this spacing is named by an optional, one-line, local setting naming the remote host (matching the literal value that host's secondmates are registered under). When that setting is absent, there is no staggering at all, unchanged from today's upstream default for every installation that does not create it.

## What Changed
- `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh`: `bootstrap_parallel_spawn` now takes the item's remote host as its first argument. The secondmate liveness sweep and the remote sync loop pass `remote_host` to it. The Nth launch in one concurrent batch that goes to the host named in the new optional `config/ssh-launch-stagger-host` waits `0.4s * (N-1)` inside its own forked worker, so the parent dispatch loop never blocks. Launches to other hosts and local launches still start immediately. Nothing is retried.
- The setting is file-only and is not inherited. Bootstrap reads it only when a network phase runs, before any network sweep starts, including the background `fleet_sync` fork. If the file is not a readable regular file, or it is empty or contains whitespace or control characters, bootstrap exits with an error. When the file is absent, launches are not staggered, which is the same as the current behavior.
- The setting is documented in `docs/configuration.md` ("SSH launch stagger host"), `docs/remote-secondmates.md` and the config layout in `AGENTS.md`. `tests/fm-bootstrap-network-parallel.test.sh` has new tests for the stagger behavior.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is small and opt-in. With no config file, BOOTSTRAP_STAGGER_HOST stays empty and every launch forks exactly as before. With the file present, only workers bound for that exact host sleep 0.4s*(N-1), inside the worker after the fork, with no retry. Both fix-round findings are now resolved: validation runs only in network runs that are not detect-only, and it runs before the fleet_sync fork.

## Testing

I ran the shipped network-parallel suite and a separate adversarial driver against the real `fm-bootstrap.sh` CLI, with a fake SSH binary that timestamps each call. Configured-host repeats were spaced about 0.4s apart in both the liveness batch and the convergence batch (gaps 0.36–0.58s). Other hosts and the no-config case were not spaced. There were no retries. Malformed configs stop only network runs, before any SSH call or fetch, leave no orphan background job, and do not affect the lavish-compatible, network-skip or detect-only modes. Herdr was not involved because this change does not touch the Herdr lifecycle. I did not test against a real rate-limited sshd because no remote host was available.

title: fix(bin): wait on a sibling fresh spawn for the home task-set lock
body:
## Intent The captain chose A: "proceed with a". All 13 upstream PRs in the triage report are approved, opened from Thoughts-One/firstmate-contrib. This PR: Upstream: wait on a sibling fresh spawn for the home task-set lock. The bug: bin/fm-bootstrap.sh's secondmate liveness sweep forks every local secondmate relaunch concurrently with no stagger, so two or more dead local secondmates can spawn fresh fm-spawn.sh processes that all compete for the same per-home task-set lock. Whichever process loses that race currently refuses outright, even when the lock's actual holder is a harmless sibling relaunch rather than a forced teardown, and the refusal message always blames "a forced teardown" regardless of the real holder. This is a real, currently-unfixed, general concurrency bug: any firstmate home with two or more dead local secondmates relaunched in the same liveness sweep can hit it, independent of remote host, and it has a real same-day reproduction in this fleet's own session-start liveness sweep. The fix should distinguish the two possible lock holders, still refuse immediately when a forced teardown holds the lock (since the home may be moments from removal), but have a sibling fresh spawn wait instead of racing to failure, and name the actual holder in the refusal message rather than always blaming a forced teardown. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: When a fresh spawn cannot take the per-home task-set lock, it now checks which process holds the lock. If the holder is a live sibling `fm-spawn.sh`, the spawn polls until it gets the lock, with a limit of 90s for each holder. If the holder is a forced teardown, the spawn still refuses immediately. The spawn checks the holder again on each poll, so a teardown that takes the lock during the wait also causes an immediate refusal. - The refusal message now names the actual holder (a forced teardown, another spawn, an operation that has since exited, or another operation). Before this change, the message always named "a forced teardown". The header comment also describes the new wait behavior. - `tests/fm-secondmate-liveness.test.sh`: Adds a regression test in which one `fm-bootstrap.sh` liveness sweep relaunches three dead local secondmates at the same time, with a slow fake tmux launch. The test checks that all three relaunch and that none of them fails on the task-set lock. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix round removed the env override and replaced the single bounded wait with a per-poll loop. That loop re-reads the holder on every pass and resets the 90s bound only when the holder pid changes. A spawn that waits holds no other lock, and forced-teardown and non-spawn holders still refuse at once. The refusal message now names the real holder, and the existing refusal tests still match the unchanged 'task set is locked' text. ## Testing I ran the new three-sibling regression test on the change (pass) and on the base commit (fails with the old refusal that blames a forced teardown). Then I drove five lock-holder scenarios through the real bootstrap sweep and fm-spawn.sh. In each one, a stand-in process held the real task-set lock through the library's own lock function. Every scenario passed, and the tests used no wait override. When the full test file runs in this gate worktree, one earlier test fails. title: fix(bin): read every prompt from Lavish YAML-style frames
body:
## Intent

During a visual review, six freeform comments left on a Lavish board were captured durably, but `bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh read` reported zero items and no annotations, so the review was wrongly treated as empty. The cause found: `cmd_read` parses only a CSV-shaped frame whose header must match `prompts[N]{fields}:` followed by indented CSV rows, while the Lavish 0.1.45 capture uses a YAML-style `prompts[6]:` list of `- uid:` mappings, so every freeform prompt was silently dropped, contrary to the script's own header promise that typed words are never dropped. Firstmate offered to fix the tool and asked whether to deliver it as a public PR upstream from a fork under the captain's GitHub account or as a local-only change. The answers:

yes, please, fix the tool

go with your recommendation, please

## What Changed

- Unified the `read` and `answers`/`reconciles` frame parsing in `bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh` into a single `lavish_prompt_frame` reader that accepts both published poll shapes - the flat `prompts[N]{fields}:` CSV frame and the YAML-style `prompts[N]:` list of `- key: value` mappings - so freeform comments and keyed choice rows are no longer silently dropped when Lavish renders a batch containing nested structures (e.g. quoted text-range `target` blocks, now surfaced as `target_type`/`target_text`).
- A prompts frame that matches neither published shape, or declares queued items but parses to none, now fails loudly instead of printing an empty review.
- Added a sanitized lavish-axi 0.1.45 YAML-frame capture fixture with regression tests in `tests/fm-procevent.test.sh` covering both frame shapes, keyed rows, and the loud-failure paths, and classified the new capture README in `docs/documentation-audiences.json`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is well-bounded to one adapter script plus tests and a recorded fixture, both prior findings were fixed minimally and correctly with no siblings left behind, and a fresh adversarial pass over the unified frame reader, its callers, and every new test fixture surfaced no reachable defect.

## Testing

Drove the real bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh CLI end-to-end on the recorded six-comment Lavish 0.1.45 YAML capture and on hand-built flat-CSV, mixed-choice, garbled, alien-header, feedback-framed, and empty captures, proving the reported silent-drop is fixed, both frame shapes and all guard boundaries behave as documented, and the two review fixes took effect; the targeted fm-procevent suite (which also arms the real adapter through the real runner) passed in full. Worktree left clean; before/after and guard transcripts saved as evidence artifacts.

- ⚠️ `tests/fm-procevent.test.sh:3287` - Vacuous regression assertion: `assert_not_contains` (tests/lib.sh:565) is a fixed-substring case-glob, so the needle `malformed_items: [1-9]` is matched literally and can never appear in real output — the guard 'a clean YAML frame reported malformed items' cannot fail even if malformed_items is nonzero, giving false confidence on exactly the regression this change pins. title: fix(bin): refuse to spawn into a pool slot another live task still claims
body:
## Intent

Pool-slot fix: both approved (offer publicly after satisfying all contributor requirements)

Context: an investigation found that `bin/fm-spawn.sh` accepts whatever pooled worktree `treehouse get` returns and then unconditionally overwrites its `.fm-slot-owner` claim through `fm_treehouse_slot_owner_claim`, without calling `fm_treehouse_slot_owner_state`. So a slot still recorded for another live, parked task can be handed to a new task. Only teardown checks ownership today, through `require_owned_worktree_slot_record` and `require_exclusive_worktree_slot_record` in `bin/fm-teardown.sh`. The recommendation is a spawn-time refusal that mirrors the teardown guard.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now reads the pool slot's existing `.fm-slot-owner` claim with `fm_treehouse_slot_owner_state` before it overwrites the claim. Spawn stops with an error that names the slot and the task in two cases: the claim names a different task whose `.meta` record still exists in the home that the claim names, or the claim cannot be read. This mirrors the teardown guard in `bin/fm-teardown.sh`. Spawn still overwrites a claim that names the spawning task itself, and a stale claim whose task has no record.
- When a spawn aborts after it has already released the Treehouse project lock, `spawn_abort_cleanup` now acquires the lock again to release its own slot claim. Before this change, it printed a warning and left the claim on the slot.
- `tests/fm-spawn-pool-base-freshen.test.sh` adds tests for the new spawn behavior. Spawn refuses a claim from a live conflicting task and does not change that claim, the slot HEAD, or the task records. Spawn takes back a stale claim, takes back a claim that already names the spawning task, and refuses a claim it cannot read.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The spawn-time guard refuses only an `other` claim whose task still has a regular state/<id>.meta record in the home the claim names, as the user asked in round 2. It treats a claim with no record as stale and overwrites it, and it still refuses an `unsafe` claim. The abort path takes the project lock again. Every other user of that lock only tries it and refuses when it is taken, so the new wait cannot deadlock. The new tests run spawn itself and cover the refusal, the stale claim and a claim that names the same task.

## Testing

I ran the targeted pool-slot spawn test file, and it passed, including the new refusal, stale-reclaim, and self-reclaim cases. I then drove the change live in an isolated fm-lab-* Herdr session with a real Treehouse pool. The steps were: (1) spawn task A and confirm it claims its slot; (2) close A's pane but keep A's record, spawn task B, and confirm Treehouse returns A's slot and spawn refuses (exit 1). The refusal names task A, the slot, and the leftover window, leaves A's claim unchanged, and publishes no record for B. (3) Close B's leftover window, remove A's record, spawn task C, and confirm that spawn takes the same slot and rewrites the claim to task=C. All three live scenarios passed. The self-reclaim and unreadable-claim cases were covered only by the test file (fake terminal), not live, so they are reported as untested live. Spawn refuses by default inside the no-mistakes gate, so the live script sets the repo's documented test-harness bypass (FM_GATE_REFUSE_BYPASS=1), which the repo's own sandbox tests also set. The first live run's S3 failed because of a bug in my script: it passed a session-qualified pane id to `pane close`, so slot 1 stayed busy. I fixed the script and re-ran it, and all three scenarios passed. I kept both logs. The lab was torn down cleanly, and nothing is left in the worktree.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 3 of 6 scenarios driven live against the product

| Adversarial: Treehouse returns a slot whose claim names another task that still has a record; spawn refuses, keeps that claim, publishes no record, and names the leftover window | ✅ pass | live | live-pool-slot-guard.log S2: slotA's pane is closed (Treehouse reports the slot as available), slotB's spawn exits 1 on the same slot, the claim still reads task=slotA, there is no slotB.meta, and the… |
| A stale claim (the named task has no record) does not block the slot: spawn proceeds and rewrites the claim for itself | ✅ pass | live | live-pool-slot-guard.log S3: slotA.meta is removed, slotC's spawn exits 0 on the same slot 1, and the claim rewrites to task=slotC |
| A retried spawn whose slot claim already names the same task proceeds | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: this case was exercised only by tests/fm-spawn-pool-base-freshen.test.sh (test_pool_slot_claim_reclaims_its_own_prior_marker) with a fake terminal, n… |
| An unreadable slot claim makes spawn refuse and name the claim file | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: this case was exercised only by tests/fm-spawn-pool-base-freshen.test.sh (test_pool_slot_claim_follows_the_spawn_outcome) with a fake terminal, not a… |
| An abort after metadata publication takes the project lock again and releases the task's own slot claim | ⏸️ untested | no | Driving this path needs launch delivery to fail after metadata publication but before the backlog commit. The lab gives no way to inject that failure into the real product, and the user declined addin… |

Source: [Live scenario driver script](https://github.com/Thoughts-One/firstmate-contrib/blob/c89d16cda86184d378585392f46836b4270bb1a7/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/pool-slot-spawn-guard-upstream/live-pool-slot-guard.sh)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Live proof of the spawn-time Treehouse pool-slot owner guard, driven through
# the real bin/fm-spawn.sh, a real Treehouse pool (in-project, under a temp
# dir), and an isolated fm-lab-* Herdr session via bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh.
set -u
ROOT=${ROOT:?set ROOT to the checkout}
HELPER="$ROOT/bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh"
SESSION=$("$HELPER" name fm-slot-guard) || exit 1
export HERDR_SESSION="$SESSION"
TMP=$(mktemp -d "$(cd /tmp && pwd -P)/fm-slot-guard-live.XXXXXX")
SLOTS=()
say() { printf '\n=== %s\n' "$*"; }
cleanup() {
  local wt
  for wt in ${SLOTS[@]+"${SLOTS[@]}"}; do treehouse return --force "$wt" >/dev/null 2>&1; done
  "$HELPER" teardown "$SESSION"; echo "teardown rc=$?"
  rm -rf "$TMP"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
unset HERDR_ENV HERDR_PANE_ID HERDR_SOCKET_PATH
"$HELPER" provision "$SESSION" || { echo "provision failed"; exit 1; }
echo "lab session: $SESSION"
lab() { "$HELPER" run "$SESSION" "$@"; }

PROJ="$TMP/project"
mkdir -p "$PROJ"; git -C "$PROJ" init -q -b main
printf '# scratch\n' > "$PROJ/README.md"
printf '.treehouse/\n' > "$PROJ/.gitignore"
printf 'max_trees = 4\nroot = "."\n' > "$PROJ/treehouse.toml"
git -C "$PROJ" add -A
git -C "$PROJ" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.invalid commit -qm initial
git clone -q --bare "$PROJ" "$PROJ.origin.git"
git -C "$PROJ" remote add origin "file://$PROJ.origin.git"
git -C "$PROJ" fetch -q origin

HOME_DIR="$TMP/home"
mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR/state" "$HOME_DIR/config"
printf 'off\n' > "$HOME_DIR/config/herdr-presentation-spaces"
for id in slotA slotB slotC; do
  mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR/data/$id"
  printf '# Task\n## Captain'"'"'s intent\nLive slot guard %s.\n\n## Firstmate spec\nNothing.\n' "$id" > "$HOME_DIR/data/$id/brief.md"
done

spawn() { # <id>
  env FM_GATE_REFUSE_BYPASS=1 HERDR_SESSION="$SESSION" FM_SPAWN_NO_GUARD=1 FM_HOME="$HOME_DIR" FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$ROOT" \
    "$ROOT/bin/fm-spawn.sh" "$1" "$PROJ" "sh -c 'echo slot-guard-ok'" \
    --mode no-mistakes --yolo off --backend herdr > "$TMP/$1.out" 2>&1
  local rc=$?
  echo "\$ fm-spawn.sh $1 ... --backend herdr  -> exit $rc"
  sed 's/^/  | /' "$TMP/$1.out" | grep -E 'spawned|error|warning' | head -5
  return $rc
}
meta_field() { grep "^$2=" "$HOME_DIR/state/$1.meta" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | cut -d= -f2-; }
claim_of() { cat "$(dirname "$1")/.fm-slot-owner" 2>/dev/null || echo '<no claim file>'; }

say "S1: fresh spawn of slotA claims its pool slot"
spawn slotA; RC_A=$?
WT_A=$(meta_field slotA worktree); PANE_A=$(meta_field slotA herdr_pane_id)
[ -n "$WT_A" ] && SLOTS+=("$WT_A")
echo "slotA worktree=$WT_A pane=$PANE_A"
echo "claim on slot:"; claim_of "$WT_A" | sed 's/^/  /'
[ "$RC_A" = 0 ] && grep -qx "task=slotA" "$(dirname "$WT_A")/.fm-slot-owner" && echo "S1 RESULT: PASS" || echo "S1 RESULT: FAIL"

say "Park slotA: close its pane so Treehouse sees the slot free, but keep state/slotA.meta"
lab pane close "$PANE_A" >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "pane close rc=$?"
sleep 2
(cd "$PROJ" && treehouse status 2>&1 | sed "s/^/  /")
ls "$HOME_DIR/state/slotA.meta"

say "S2 (adversarial): spawn slotB; Treehouse hands back slotA's slot; spawn must refuse"
CLAIM_BEFORE=$(claim_of "$WT_A")
spawn slotB; RC_B=$?
WT_B_GUESS=$(grep -o "pool slot [^,]*" "$TMP/slotB.out" | head -1 | sed 's/^pool slot //')
echo "refused slot: $WT_B_GUESS"
echo "claim after:"; claim_of "$WT_A" | sed 's/^/  /'
echo "state/slotB.meta exists? $( [ -e "$HOME_DIR/state/slotB.meta" ] && echo yes || echo no)"
if [ "$RC_B" -ne 0 ] && [ "$WT_B_GUESS" = "$WT_A" ] && [ "$(claim_of "$WT_A")" = "$CLAIM_BEFORE" ] \
   && [ ! -e "$HOME_DIR/state/slotB.meta" ] && grep -q "still names task slotA" "$TMP/slotB.out"; then
  echo "S2 RESULT: PASS"
else echo "S2 RESULT: FAIL"; cat "$TMP/slotB.out"; fi

say "Close slotB's leftover refusal pane (named in the error) and drop slotA's record (claim now stale)"
PANE_B=$(grep -o 'inspect window [^ ]*' "$TMP/slotB.out" | tail -1 | awk '{print $3}')
PANE_B=${PANE_B#"$SESSION:"}
echo "leftover pane named by refusal: $PANE_B"
[ -n "$PANE_B" ] && { lab pane close "$PANE_B" >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "pane close rc=$?"; }
rm -f "$HOME_DIR/state/slotA.meta"
(cd "$PROJ" && treehouse status 2>&1 | sed "s/^/  /")
sleep 2

say "S3: spawn slotC; slot claim names recordless slotA -> stale, spawn proceeds and overwrites"
spawn slotC; RC_C=$?
WT_C=$(meta_field slotC worktree); [ -n "$WT_C" ] && SLOTS+=("$WT_C")
echo "slotC worktree=$WT_C"
echo "claim after:"; claim_of "$WT_C" | sed 's/^/  /'
if [ "$RC_C" = 0 ] && [ "$WT_C" = "$WT_A" ] && grep -qx "task=slotC" "$(dirname "$WT_C")/.fm-slot-owner"; then
  echo "S3 RESULT: PASS"
else echo "S3 RESULT: FAIL"; cat "$TMP/slotC.out"; fi

PANE_C=$(meta_field slotC herdr_pane_id)
[ -n "$PANE_C" ] && lab pane close "$PANE_C" >/dev/null 2>&1
```
