title: fix(bin): keep remote relaunch alive across inheritance version skew
body:
## Problem

Relaunching a remote secondmate is refused outright when the primary offers an inherited config item that the remote host's Firstmate code root does not know:

```
error: path is not inherited material: config/lavish-axi-host
error: remote secondmate <id> inheritance failed; launch refused
```

Relaunch through `bin/fm-spawn.sh <id> --secondmate` is the only sanctioned recovery for a stuck remote secondmate, so while this holds such a secondmate cannot be recovered at all.

## Root cause

There are two defects, and the reported failure hits both.

**1. Version skew was fatal.**
`bin/fm-remote-inherit.sh` (runs on the remote host) checks each path against its own code root's `fm_config_inherit_items` and exits 1 on an unknown path.
`bin/fm-remote-inherit-push.sh` (runs on the primary) loops over the primary's own list under `set -eu` with no per-item handling, so the first refusal aborts the whole push, and items after it (here `data/captain-shared.md`) are never sent either.
`bin/fm-spawn.sh` then refuses the launch on any nonzero push status other than 255.

This skew is structural, not transient.
fm-on.sh runs remote commands from the host's Firstmate code root, which only `/updatefirstmate` advances.
The pre-launch sync moves the secondmate's home, not that code root.
So every addition to `FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG` strands every remote relaunch until the host is updated.
The bootstrap convergence sweep (`secondmate_sync_remote_one`) already treats an inheritance failure as a per-cycle skip, so session start degrades quietly, but relaunch has no such grace, which is why it is the path that actually strands recovery.

**2. A per-machine address crossed machines.**
The report treated `lavish-axi-host` as illustrative, but it is real on `main`: #5060 (2026-09-20) added it to `FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG`.
It is documented as the address of the per-machine Lavish server.
A remote secondmate runs on another machine, and its host-local spawn reads that home's own `config/lavish-axi-host`.
Before this change, against a same-revision remote, the primary either overwrote the remote host's own address with the primary machine's, or deleted it whenever the primary had none.
Both are wrong regardless of version skew.

## Decision

The report raised three readings: (a) tolerate unknown items, (b) have the primary learn what the remote supports, and (c) never let a per-machine item cross machines.

- **(a), implemented on the sender.**
  A receiver-only change cannot fix this, because the refusing side is by definition the older one that is already deployed.
  Every deployed receiver refuses an unknown path with exactly `error: path is not inherited material: <path>` and exit 1, immediately after the argument-count check and before any other validation, read, lock, or write.
  The sender now classifies exactly that refusal, for the path it just offered, as version skew.
  It prints `fm-remote-inherit-push: warning: skipped <path> for remote secondmate <id>: ...` on stderr and continues.
  `fm-spawn.sh` discards the push's stdout, but that warning line still reaches its stderr.
  Every other failure still stops the push and refuses the launch with the remote's stderr and exit status unchanged, including 255 (completion unknown).
  The receiver's refusal line and its position are now documented as a cross-revision contract.
- **(b), rejected.**
  Older hosts have no way to answer "what do you support?", so (b) would still need (a) as its fallback, plus a new protocol.
- **(c), implemented in code and written down at the declaration site.**
  `FM_MACHINE_LOCAL_INHERITABLE_CONFIG="lavish-axi-host"` in `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh` states the principle for future items.
  Same-machine secondmate homes still inherit these items.
  The remote sender never offers them (`fm_config_inherit_remote_items`).
  If an older sender (#5060 or later, before this change) still offers one, the receiver answers `skipped:`, exits 0, and writes, removes, and commits nothing.
  So a newer remote also never refuses an older primary over this item.

With (c), the reported failure is gone for this particular item even against today's older hosts, because the item is no longer offered.
(a) covers the general class of any future addition.

**Nothing becomes writable that was not before.**
The remote still writes only paths its own code root declares.
A skip means the receiver refused before any side effect.
Machine-local handling only narrows what a remote writes.

## Tests

`tests/fm-remote-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e.test.sh` drives everything through real `fm-spawn.sh`, `fm-on.sh`, `fm-remote-entrypoint.sh`, the remote job worker, and `fm-remote-inherit.sh`.
The remote runs every command under `env -i`, so setting `FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG` on the primary alone reproduces a newer primary talking to an older host.

- **Receiver contract.**
  An undeclared path exits 1 with the exact refusal line and leaves no file, generation record, or lock.
  A machine-local `put` or `absent` from an older sender exits 0 with `skipped:` and leaves the host's own value and generation state untouched.
- **Relaunch under skew.**
  Two unknown items are declared ahead of every real item, one present only on the primary and one absent on both sides.
  First, a symlinked destination for a known item still refuses the relaunch with the remote's diagnostic, so a skip never masks a genuine failure.
  Then the relaunch succeeds.
  Both unknown items are named in skip warnings, nothing is written for them, and the last item still converges.
  The remote's own Lavish address survives, and a log at the SSH boundary shows `config/lavish-axi-host` was never sent.

Evidence that the new cases fail on the base commit (`1e0e7734`) with the new test file copied in:

```
not ok - machine-local put was not reported as skipped (missing: 'skipped: config/lavish-axi-host')
not ok - remote relaunch was refused over version skew alone
error: path is not inherited material: config/fm-skew-present
error: remote secondmate ios inheritance failed; launch refused
```

A scratch check against the genuinely older remote code root, `bin/` at `c443d8c2^` (just before #5060), reproduced the exact reported error with the base sender.
With this sender, the same push converges every item.

## Validation

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` (ShellCheck 0.11.0, actionlint 1.7.12): clean.
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh`: ok.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh` on the inheritance suites (remote lifecycle e2e, remote trace-context, bootstrap network parallel, trace-context lib, secondmate harness, spawn dispatch profile, startup memory budget, shared captain inheritance): all pass.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed` (62 suites): 53 pass or skip on their gates.
  The 9 failures each fail with the identical first assertion on the untouched base commit in this environment, so none comes from this change:
  - `fm-backlog-handoff`, `fm-remote-backlog-handoff`, and `fm-secondmate-lifecycle-e2e`: no compatible `tasks-axi` with atomic multi-ID moves on this host.
  - `fm-test-run`: `ruby` is not installed.
  - `fm-remote-doctor` and `fm-remote-herdr-guard`: macOS login-session expectations running on a Linux host.
  - `fm-bearings-board`, `fm-captain-hold-lifecycle`, and `fm-devin-harness`: identical failures on base.
- `fm-backend-herdr-presentation-e2e` also fails identically on base (a delivery-contract launch warning).
- This host's `LANG=en_IN.UTF-8` is not installed, so perl locale warnings leak into stderr-sensitive suites unless `LC_ALL=C` is set; the runs above used `LC_ALL=C`.
- Harness and backend review: this is harness-independent shell transport, and remote secondmates always run on Herdr, so no per-harness or per-backend behavior changes.

Direct-PR delivery; not merged, pending the merge decision.

title: fix: stabilize remote worker identity against clock drift
body:
## Intent Open an upstream pull request with the permanent code fixes for two problems hit on a Windows/WSL remote second mate. 1. On WSL2 the kernel boot time drifts (btime in /proc/stat moved about 27 seconds within minutes because the Windows host clock was unsynchronized and host time sync kept fighting systemd-timesyncd), so `ps -o lstart` for one live process changes over time. The remote job runner's owner check in bin/fm-remote-job-lib.sh compares a recorded lstart against the current one, so it never matched, and every fm-on call concluded no runner owned the lock and started another. About 200 runners piled up, load reached about 60 on 24 cores, and readiness probes flapped. A local hotfix is running on the WSL host: fm_remote_job_process_start reads the start-tick field from /proc//stat on Linux and falls back to ps lstart elsewhere. The upstream fix should make process identity immune to wall-clock or boot-time drift. The fleet has since standardized every second mate on Claude Code, so the per-second-mate runtime pin is no longer wanted; this pull request carries only the process start identity fix. ## What Changed - Use `/proc//stat` start ticks for remote worker identity when available, preventing Linux/WSL clock drift from breaking ownership checks; retain the `ps lstart` fallback. - Replace legacy Linux workers during readiness checks after verifying their live command matches the configured code root. - Document the identity upgrade and add regression coverage for stat parsing, ownership mismatches, fallback behavior, and legacy worker replacement. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is narrowly scoped to stable process identities and the authorized Linux legacy-worker handoff, with no substantiated defects found. ## Testing Targeted regressions passed as non-live checks. Live worker upgrades, repeated readiness, unrelated-process protection, and queued command execution passed. CLI transcripts were captured and test state removed. Remaining live validation gaps prevent a conclusive shipping verdict. - Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 4 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Repeated readiness calls reuse one Linux worker and queued work completes | ✅ pass | live | live-runner.log: repeated readiness calls retained the same PID with repaired=0; queued delta read returned exit=0 and the expected payload. | | Upgrade a running legacy worker to tick ownership | ✅ pass | live | live-runner.log: base-commit worker and supervisor group terminated; replacement published a numeric tick identity. | | Recover a legacy worker whose recorded timestamp differs by 27 seconds | ✅ pass | live | live-runner.log: legacy lock timestamp shifted by 27 seconds; upgrade completed and five readiness calls reused the replacement. | | Legacy replacement guard preserves an unrelated live process | ✅ pass | live | live-runner.log: unrelated sleep process survived recovery of a legacy lock naming its PID. | | Parse parentheses in process names, reject mismatched ticks, and preserve lstart fallback matching | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload records only a targeted test exiting successfully, with live=false; it does not establish that these behaviors were driven against the running product. Live product validation is nee… | | Maintain ownership during actual WSL2 boot-time drift | ⏸️ untested | no | No isolated WSL2 host with controllable Windows time synchronization was provided. Supply such a disposable host to reproduce actual btime drift. | | Preserve native macOS worker identity and mismatch recovery | ⏸️ untested | no | This environment has no macOS host or Aqua session. Supply an isolated macOS account with an Aqua session for native validation. |
Evidence: Live runner upgrades, readiness reuse, safety guard, and queued output Source: [Live runner upgrades, readiness reuse, safety guard, and queued output](https://github.com/arthurcruzd/firstmate/blob/938f91ba3b736e0f9d761a94912257bc7e6570f3/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-remote-runner-drift/live-runner.log) ```text BASE worker: pid=3286333 group=3286256 identity=Wed Sep 23 12:03:16 2026 UPGRADE ready: pid=3287291 ticks=14674418; old worker and supervisor group gone Readiness call 1 reused pid=3287291 repaired=0 Readiness call 2 reused pid=3287291 repaired=0 Readiness call 3 reused pid=3287291 repaired=0 Readiness call 4 reused pid=3287291 repaired=0 Readiness call 5 reused pid=3287291 repaired=0 Teardown: upgraded worker stopped BASE worker: pid=3291150 group=3291071 identity=Wed Sep 23 12:03:22 2026 Injected stale legacy identity (-27s): Wed Sep 23 12:02:55 2026 UPGRADE ready: pid=3292169 ticks=14675016; old worker and supervisor group gone Readiness call 1 reused pid=3292169 repaired=0 Readiness call 2 reused pid=3292169 repaired=0 Readiness call 3 reused pid=3292169 repaired=0 Readiness call 4 reused pid=3292169 repaired=0 Readiness call 5 reused pid=3292169 repaired=0 Teardown: upgraded worker stopped SAFETY: unrelated pid=3294942 survived legacy lock recovery; ready worker=3295095 job-kmphVE QUEUE job=job-kmphVE exit=0 stdout: schema=fm-remote-delta.v1 status=delta path=data/replies.log from_offset=0 to_offset=20 from_prefix_sha256=e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855 to_prefix_sha256=0fddd26859d910ab95f5afa1e052257f5514fe429af8d2a2e2a717a5d8c4bcee payload_sha256=0fddd26859d910ab95f5afa1e052257f5514fe429af8d2a2e2a717a5d8c4bcee payload_bytes=20 reason= identity live probe Teardown: guard worker and unrelated process stopped ```

title: fix(omp): arm the watcher after a new process owns the lock
body:
## Summary

A new OMP process checked session-lock ownership once at `session_start` and never looked again. On `--resume`, that check happened before the lock existed, and the resume path only printed the session-start nudge instead of acquiring the lock. The watcher stayed down, so the turn-end guard reported supervision unhealthy.

- The watcher extension now waits, bounded to that generation, and arms through the existing path once this process owns the lock. It does not arm while another live session holds the lock, and shutdown or replacement cancels the wait.
- A new process launched with `--resume` that does not already own the lock runs the real startup path. A process that already owns the lock still uses the resume path.

## Verification

- `tests/fm-omp-harness.test.sh` passed, including the new dead-lock, missing-lock, other-owner, shutdown, and `--resume` source cases.
- `FM_OMP_LIVE_E2E=1 tests/fm-omp-primary-live-e2e.test.sh` passed on omp 18.2.8 with `openai-codex/gpt-6-astra`. The extension armed a live watcher without a model tool call, and `session_stop` still compelled the guard continuation.
- `tests/fm-supervision-instructions.test.sh` passed.
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` passed.
- `bin/fm-lint.sh` passed with ShellCheck 0.11.0 and actionlint 1.7.12.
- A clean `--resume` of the saved Rhett Factory session on this branch acquired the lock, armed the watcher automatically, and passed the strict watcher-health predicate.

## Test plan

- [x] Portable omp harness suite
- [x] Opt-in live omp primary E2E
- [x] Lint and workflow validation
- [ ] Maintainer review

## What Changed - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now writes a marker line ahead of the staged launch command and waits (bounded by the new `FM_SPAWN_LAUNCH_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT`, default 30s) for that marker to appear before reporting a spawn as delivered, catching panes that swallow, never run, or lose the staged launch line. On timeout the spawn fails loudly, records the failure on the task's status, and leaves the endpoint and local copy untouched for inspection. On success the staged launch file and its marker are removed immediately instead of persisting for the task's lifetime. - `docs/configuration.md` documents the new `FM_SPAWN_LAUNCH_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT` environment variable. - Test fixtures (`tests/fixtures.sh`, `tests/secondmate-helpers.sh`, `tests/remote-herdr-fixture.sh`) and associated harness/spawn/backlog test suites are updated to simulate sourcing the staged launch file (writing the "started" marker, reading the command from the file's last line) and to support a new `FM_FAKE_LAUNCH_NOT_RUN` toggle for exercising the never-ran failure path; a new `fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` test is added. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix-round change is a single, tightly-scoped test-fixture edit that makes the fake Orca CLI create the launch-started marker (and capture the staged command before fm-spawn.sh deletes it), exactly matching the pattern already proven correct for the tmux, herdr, and secondmate fakes elsewhere in this same diff; I traced the sed extraction, the shell_quote-produced source line format, the marker path derivation, and the updated assertions and found them all consistent and correct, with no other fixture or production code left unaddressed. ## Testing Ran the full tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh suite against the fixed fake Orca CLI: all 39 cases pass, including test_spawn_writes_orca_metadata_and_launches_harness, the exact scenario the review flagged as broken. Confirmed the fix is scoped only to that one test file, matches the marker contract in bin/fm-spawn.sh, and mirrors the same pattern already applied to every other backend's fake CLI in this diff. Also reproduced the original failure mode by temporarily reverting the fixture to its pre-fix content and confirming the same spawn test then stalls on the launch-confirmation wait, then restored the worktree to a clean state. - Live validation: ✅ go - 3 of 4 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Orca spawn: fake CLI sources the staged launch file and the spawn reports a worker | ✅ pass | live | `bash tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh` → `ok - fm-spawn.sh --backend orca: reuses implicit terminal, records metadata, launches harness` (test_spawn_writes_orca_metadata_and_launches_harness) | | Regression check: without the fixture fix, the same spawn stalls because no .started marker is ever created | ✅ pass | live | Temporarily restored tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh to its pre-fix (base commit f5735dc) content and ran test_spawn_writes_orca_metadata_and_launches_harness against the current bin/fm-spawn.sh; the ru… | | FM_FAKE_LAUNCH_NOT_RUN opt-out models a dead pane that never sources the staged file | ⏸️ untested | no | No test in fm-backend-orca.test.sh exercises this opt-out directly (the recorded decision only required honoring the flag, not adding a new assertion for it). Confirmed by code reading and by cross-ch… | | Full existing Orca backend test suite still passes (spawn, teardown, send, capture, composer-state helpers) | ✅ pass | live | `bash tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh` — 39/39 pass, 0 failures |
Evidence: fm-backend-orca.test.sh full suite run (post-fix) ```text 39/39 "ok" lines, including: ok - fm-spawn.sh --backend orca: reuses implicit terminal, records metadata, launches harness ```

✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.

Every tmux/herdr/secondmate test fixture in the diff was updated to simulate a pane sourcing the staged file and creating that marker (tests/fixtures.sh, tests/fm-backend.test.sh, tests/remote-herdr-fixture.sh, tests/secondmate-helpers.sh, and a dozen harness test files), but the Orca backend's fake CLI in tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh (make_orca_fakebin, ~line 30) was not: it only logs argv to a log file and never touches the filesystem to create '<staged>.started'. fm_backend_orca_send_literal (bin/backends/orca.sh:174-178) routes the same '. title: fix(bin): reap a closed tmux pane's surviving session members on teardown
body:
## Problem

When a task is cleaned up on the tmux backend, `bin/fm-teardown.sh` closes its window with `tmux kill-window`.
That only hangs up the pane pty: SIGHUP reaches the pane's session leader and its foreground process group.
A pane-session member that ignores SIGHUP, or that sits in its own process group, therefore survives a teardown that reports success, reparented to init, and keeps holding memory.
Herdr's pane close already ends every member of the pane's POSIX session, which masks this class for Herdr users.

## Reproduction

A diagnosis drove the real `bin/fm-spawn.sh` and `bin/fm-teardown.sh` against a private tmux server with a fake agent tree.
After a successful teardown on tmux, six processes survived: the two own-session ones Herdr also leaves, plus four pane-session members with their cwd outside the task copy that ignored SIGHUP, ignored SIGHUP and SIGTERM, or ran in their own process group.
A counterfactual that snapshotted the pane session before the close and reaped identity-matched survivors after it reduced the tmux survivor set to exactly Herdr's.

The new regression test reproduces the core case on current `main` (`706254de`).
A window child calls `setpgid(0,0)`, ignores SIGHUP, and runs `chdir("/")`, so neither the existing cwd-based worktree reap nor a process-group fallback can catch it.

```text
$ bash tests/fm-teardown-pane-session.test.sh   # on 706254de, before the fix
not ok - SIGHUP-ignoring own-process-group pane-session member survived teardown (pid 49984)
rc=1
```

The final version of the test also fails against the unchanged `bin/fm-teardown.sh`:

```text
not ok - SIGHUP-ignoring own-process-group pane-session member 'target' survived teardown (pid 63260)
rc=1
```

## Fix

- New `bin/fm-pane-session-reap-lib.sh` owns the contract.
  - `fm_pane_session_snapshot <tmux-target>` runs immediately before the close.
    It reads the exact window's live panes (`list-panes -t "=session:=window"`, skipping dead panes whose recorded `pane_pid` may already name another session).
    Each pane shell is its session leader, so its pid is the session id.
    It records every member of that session as sid, pid, and `fm_pid_identity`.
    Membership comes from `os.getsid` through python3, because macOS `ps -o sess` prints 0 for every process.
    This shell and its ancestors are never recorded.
  - `fm_pane_session_reap <snapshot> <label>` runs only after a successful close.
    It sends TERM to recorded members whose session and identity still match, waits 1 s, then sends KILL to those still matching.
    It always returns 0, so a member that exits or refuses a signal never aborts teardown.
- The `bin/fm-teardown.sh` call site is a few lines on the generic close path.
  The snapshot is taken only for tmux, and the reap runs only when `fm_backend_kill` succeeded.
  A failed close still goes to `endpoint_close_refusal` exactly as before, including the `--force` behavior.
- Only the pre-close snapshot of the exact window names targets, and no later lookup widens it.
  That avoids the hazard in #4134, where a process-group lookup could reach another task's window.
  Processes that detach into their own session are not pane-session members and stay out of scope (#2367).
- Herdr, Orca, Zellij, cmux, and windowless teardown are unchanged.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh` classifies the new test in `backend-dispatch`, next to `fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh`.
- `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md` gets a "Pane session reap" section with the dated evidence.

This implements only the tmux pane-session reap.
The Claude `/exit` background-work dialog, the home-scoped orphan inventory, and the no-mistakes launchd leak ship separately.

## Tests

`tests/fm-teardown-pane-session.test.sh` runs against a real tmux server on a private `TMUX_TMPDIR`.
It reuses the meta fixture shape of `tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh`.
The target window holds two members that are SIGHUP-ignoring, in their own process group, with cwd `/`.
One yields to SIGTERM and one also ignores it, so both the TERM pass and the KILL pass are exercised.
An identically shaped control process runs in a sibling window of the same tmux session.
The test asserts that the target window is gone, that both members are gone, that the stubborn member was force-killed, and that the control process and its window survive.

```text
$ bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-teardown-pane-session.test.sh tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh tests/fm-teardown.test.sh tests/fm-test-run.test.sh tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh
FM_TEST_END ... tests/fm-test-run.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=213460 gate_skip=false
FM_TEST_END ... tests/fm-teardown.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=548388 gate_skip=false
FM_TEST_END ... tests/fm-teardown-pane-session.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=3058 gate_skip=false
FM_TEST_END ... tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=55592 gate_skip=false
FM_TEST_END ... tests/fm-backend-tmux-smoke.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=703 gate_skip=false
FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=5 failed=0 skipped_gate=0 duration_ms=822064

$ bin/fm-lint.sh
fm-lint.sh: ShellCheck 0.11.0 (pinned 0.11.0)
fm-lint.sh: local changed-file mode; ShellCheck source following disabled
fm-lint-workflows.sh: actionlint 1.7.12 (pinned 1.7.12)
fm-lint-workflows.sh: 3 workflow files valid

$ bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage
FM_TEST_COVERAGE ok total=221 parallel=24 parallel_max_ms=417163 parallel_imbalance_ms=2894 parallel_unhinted=0 serial=181 serial_shards=9 serial_unhinted=5 herdr=16

$ bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh
fm-doc-audience-check: ok surfaces=102 local_links=456
```

An earlier combined run showed one `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` case (`abort-then-reap-then-remove-order`, exit 127) and one `tests/fm-test-run.test.sh` coverage case failing while a concurrent review process was also running tests on the same machine.
Both passed when re-run alone, and both pass in the full run above.

Host: macOS 26.5.2, tmux 3.7c, Python 3.14.7, GNU bash 5.3.15.

## Independent review

Before opening this PR, a separate Claude subagent did a read-only review from four angles: functional tests, architecture and isolation, simplification, and requirement alignment.
Findings and how each was handled:

- Major: `fm_pane_session_signal` ended with `kill ... && printf`, so a failed `kill` (the process exits first, or EPERM) returned 1 and tripped `set -e` after the window was closed.
  Fixed with an explicit `if`, and the reap now always returns 0; checked with a stubbed failing `kill`.
- Major: with `remain-on-exit`, a dead pane keeps a stale `pane_pid` that may be reused by another session leader.
  Fixed: the snapshot keeps only panes with `#{pane_dead}` equal to 0.
- Minor: the library duplicated the `ps lstart` identity.
  It now reuses `fm_pid_identity` from `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh`, which prefers `/proc` starttime on Linux, and is sourced after that library.
- Minor: the KILL pass was untested.
  Added a SIGTERM-ignoring member and an assertion that it was force-killed.
- Minor: test cleanup could SIGKILL a reused pid.
  It now kills only a pid whose command still names the lab's own child script.
- Minor: the test function exceeded the 10-line limit for new code; it is split into setup, run, and assert helpers.
- Minor: fork count per pass; the post-close membership check is now a single python3 call for all recorded members.
- Nits (one-owner rule): the `bin/fm-teardown.sh` header now has only a one-line pointer to the library, and the dated evidence lives only in `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md`.
- Not addressed: a test for skipping the reap after a failed close, and one for sparing this script's ancestors.
  The failed-close branch is the unchanged `endpoint_close_refusal` path covered by `tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh`.
  An ancestor-in-pane fixture would require running teardown inside the pane it closes.

## Instructions acknowledged

- `/Users/javiermoya/.claude/CLAUDE.md` was read.
  Everything here is in English, the regression test was written and seen failing before the fix, and new code stays within 300 lines per file, 10 lines per function, and 3 arguments per function.
  Unrelated code was not refactored.
- `/ssd/datos-mac/workspace/config/development-policy.md` is absent (`No such file or directory`).
- This repo's `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` were read, and `.agents/skills/firstmate-coding-guidelines/SKILL.md` was loaded before editing.
  Its rules were followed: one sentence per line, a plain dash, a shellcheck-clean `bin/`, a colocated `<subject>.test.sh`, behavior-only assertions, and dated verification evidence in `docs/verification/`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks human-authored PRs to go through the no-mistakes gate.
  This change was delivered directly as a PR, per the task's delivery instructions, so the `Require no-mistakes` attestation check is expected to be absent.

title: feat(bin): report slots and processes no task record names at locked session start
body:
## Problem

When a firstmate home is lost (its `state/` records are gone), the Treehouse slots its tasks claimed, and any agent, MCP server, or dev server still running inside those slots, are never looked at again.
Teardown reaps a task's processes and every other cleanup path starts from a task record, so work with no record is invisible: on the reporting host 30 slot claims still named a home directory that no longer exists, and stranded Claude worker trees (about 1.4 GB each) accumulated until memory saturated.
This is fix 2 of that diagnosis: a home-scoped, report-only inventory of what no current record names.

## Fix

- New `bin/fm-orphan-inventory.sh`, run by the locked deferred startup stage (`bin/fm-startup-network.sh`), so its one system-wide process scan never blocks the digest.
- Attribution needs no process environment (macOS does not expose one): every `<pool>/<slot>/.fm-slot-owner` claim under the Treehouse root is read with the existing `fm_treehouse_slot_owner_state` parser, and both its `home=` and this home are canonicalized with `pwd -P`.
- A claim is orphaned when it names this home and `state/<task>.meta` is absent, or names a home that no longer exists (no directory, or one without `state/`, i.e. a retired home whose path was reused).
  Claims naming another live home are skipped, as are unreadable, relative, or oddly named claims, and claims younger than 5 minutes (a spawn writes its claim before publishing its record).
- One bounded `lsof -a -d cwd` scan (the same primitive teardown uses) attributes processes to orphaned slots.
- Output, only when something is found:
  - `ORPHAN_PROCESS: pid=… command=… age=… rss_kb=… slot=… task=… home=… reason=no-record|home-gone; stop it only on the captain's word: kill <pid>`
  - `ORPHAN_SLOT: slot=… task=… home=… reason=… processes=none|unknown; preview its cleanup with: treehouse destroy <copy> (a dry run; add --yes only after its preview shows no unlanded work)`
- Nothing is ever signaled, returned, or deleted automatically; `treehouse destroy` is dry-run by default and skips unlanded, in-use, and leased copies.
- The lines land in the stage's report, so a late finding still arrives as a `check: startup-network` wake.
  `AGENTS.md` section 13 and the `bootstrap-diagnostics` skill route both prefixes to a captain decision; `docs/scripts.md` lists the script.
- `tests/lib.sh` points the new `FM_ORPHAN_POOL_ROOT` knob at an absent path so no suite reads the host's real pools.

## Coordination with open upstream work

- #4615 (`POOL_LEAK:`) reports slots held by tasks whose records still exist and discovers pools only from `state/*.meta`; its own notes say a pool whose every record is gone is never examined. This PR covers exactly that recordless and lost-home case, starting from the claims, and adds no slot-return path.
- #3168 / #3737 (`fm-orphan-reap.sh`) reap processes left in the copy of a recorded task whose worker is gone. This PR never reaps and only handles slots no record names.
- No shared file overlaps with either beyond one line each in `bin/fm-startup-network.sh`'s locked child shell and the session-bootstrap test family; whichever lands second rebases trivially.

## Reproduction and test evidence

RED first (`tests/fm-orphan-inventory.test.sh` before the script existed):

```text
not ok - this home's slot without a record is reported (missing: 'ORPHAN_PROCESS: pid=59430 ')
--- output ---
tests/fm-orphan-inventory.test.sh: line 55: .../bin/fm-orphan-inventory.sh: No such file or directory
rc=1
```

The fixture is a pool with four claims - this home without a record (spelled through a symlink), a gone home, another live home, and this home with a record - and a `sleep` parked in each slot.
It asserts exactly the first two are reported with their own claim and reason, and that every `sleep` is still alive afterwards.
Further cases: an idle orphan claim reports `ORPHAN_SLOT`, a fresh claim is left alone, a reused home path without `state/` reads as gone, and a failing `lsof` yields `processes=unknown`.
A mutation check (swapping the two reasons, and dropping the `state/` rule) made the suite fail.
`tests/fm-startup-network.test.sh` gains a case proving only the locked stage runs the inventory and its lines reach the report (RED before the wiring, GREEN after).

GREEN on the final head:

```text
$ bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-orphan-inventory.test.sh tests/fm-startup-network.test.sh
ok - four claims: exactly the unrecorded and gone-home slots are reported, nothing signaled
ok - idle orphan claim reports its slot; a fresh claim is left alone
ok - reused home path reads as gone; a failed process scan reports processes=unknown
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-orphan-inventory.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=1587
ok - fm-startup-network: the locked stage reports the orphan inventory
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-startup-network.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=92652
FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=2 failed=0 skipped_gate=0 duration_ms=92916

$ bin/fm-test-run.sh --family session-bootstrap
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-backlog-atomicity.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=303131
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-bootstrap-network-parallel.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=15622
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=240949

FM_TEST_END tests/fm-gate-refuse.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=38703
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-gotmp.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=16819
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-orphan-inventory.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=6374
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-session-start.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=437891
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-sessionstart-nudge.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=72281
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-startup-network.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=86919
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-tangle-guard.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=46525
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-update.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=150041
FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=12 failed=0 skipped_gate=0 duration_ms=1483086

$ bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-test-run.test.sh
FM_TEST_END tests/fm-test-run.test.sh exit=0 duration_ms=200944
FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=1 failed=0 skipped_gate=0 duration_ms=201043

$ bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage
FM_TEST_COVERAGE ok total=221 parallel=24 parallel_max_ms=417163 parallel_imbalance_ms=2894 parallel_unhinted=0 serial=181 serial_shards=9 serial_unhinted=4 herdr=16

$ bin/fm-lint.sh
fm-lint.sh: ShellCheck 0.11.0 (pinned 0.11.0)
fm-lint-workflows.sh: 3 workflow files valid

$ bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh

```

The new test also passes under stock macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2.
The session-bootstrap family run overlapped the review-fix commit, which is why the two changed suites were re-run on the final head above.

Read-only run against the reporting host's real pools (2.6 s): 28 findings, all `reason=home-gone` for the lost home, no processes currently inside them, for example:

```text
ORPHAN_SLOT: slot=/Users/…/.treehouse/jaak-id-6274ef/1/jaak-id task=kyc-app-l11-review-pr home=/System/Volumes/Data/ssd/datos-mac/workspace/firstmate reason=home-gone processes=none; preview its cleanup with: treehouse destroy /Users/…/.treehouse/jaak-id-6274ef/1/jaak-id (a dry run; add --yes only after its preview shows no unlanded work)
```

## Independent review

A separate read-only Claude reviewer covered four angles: functional tests, architecture and isolation, anti-slop simplification, and requirement alignment.
It found no blockers and confirmed nothing signals a process, `treehouse destroy` is dry-run and skips unlanded work, and teardown drops the claim before the record, so a normal cleanup never shows as an orphan.
Addressed in the second commit:
- a timing-dependent startup-stage test (zero age floor) now backdates the claim, which also makes its negative assertion meaningful;
- assertions are pinned per line, including `reason=`;
- the failed-scan path is covered;
- numeric knobs are validated;
- processes are matched anywhere under the slot, and the path reaches awk through the environment;
- a claimed home without `state/` counts as gone.

Left as documented limits rather than scope, since they belong to other fixes or change the spec:
- the hosting terminal window is not named, because its pane shell runs from the project clone, so after the reported processes stop it may remain as an idle shell (stated in the script header and the skill);
- the same findings repeat at every locked session start, in every home that sees a gone-home claim, until they are cleaned;
- `lsof` runs before the bootstrap sweeps inside the stage's shared bound, but only when orphans exist.

## Instructions read

Read before editing: the operator's global agent instructions, this repo's `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `.agents/skills/firstmate-coding-guidelines/SKILL.md`; the operator's development-policy file is absent on this host.
The change follows test-first development (RED recorded above) and keeps new code within 300 lines per file, 10 lines per function, and 3 arguments per function, without refactoring unrelated code.
This PR is raised directly rather than through the no-mistakes pipeline, per the task's delivery instruction.

title: fix(herdr): keep workers out of firstmate and 2ndmate supervisor workspaces
body:
New and recovered Herdr worker endpoints stay out of supervisor workspaces. Lost projections receive a fresh task workspace when possible; disabled or degraded projection uses a separate, role-neutral worker container. Existing live endpoints remain discoverable.

Refs https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/5356

This contribution handles Herdr workspace placement. The backward-compatible migration away from `fm-<task-id>` tab labels is a separate follow-up, so the issue remains open. Credit to the earlier investigation at https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/2886, which was closed without merging.

The home-summary cache refresh is deferred until the presentation lock is released because its separate home lock can wait up to 60 seconds and otherwise consume the existing five-second presentation-lock budget during concurrent recovery. It remains best-effort and runs on every exit after metadata publication, including launch failure. This preserves the original lock budget; regressions cover concurrent recovery, continuous lock ownership, exact focus restoration, and failed-launch refresh.

Fallback creation stays lock-free. Concurrent launches may create more than one eligible `workers · <home> · <hash>` container; those containers are retained, placement picks the lowest workspace id, and duplicate-agent preflight and discovery scan every matching container. No workspace is closed merely to remove a duplicate container. Supervisor-label ambiguity, unreadable identities, and live or unreadable same-task endpoints still refuse launch.

## Validation

- Fresh no-mistakes review: no remaining findings; documentation and lint passed.
- Herdr adapter unit suite: 218 assertions passed, including racing fallback launches, numeric lowest-id selection, discovery across duplicate containers, and first fallback while the presentation lock is held. The race and selection regressions failed before the final fix and passed afterwards.
- All three changed real-Herdr suites passed on Herdr 0.8.2: presentation (30 cases), launcher workspace, and workspace per home. Every suite used a guarded non-default lab and verified that the default session was unchanged. The two shorter suites initially hit an existing fixture dependency on the ignored repository `state/` directory; rerunning with that temporary directory passed, and it was removed afterwards.
- A separate guarded real-Herdr probe confirmed the visible labels: an unrelated `workers` workspace stayed untouched, two racing fallbacks each launched in separate matching worker containers, a third chose the lowest-id container, and discovery found all three.

- [Real-Herdr sidebar label probe transcript](https://github.com/3264studios/firstmate/blob/06a9c62850fd23c89744b64d001a6691a4820169/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-agent-naming-by-role/label-probe-transcript.txt)

- [First attempts without state/ (setup failure)](https://github.com/3264studios/firstmate/blob/06a9c62850fd23c89744b64d001a6691a4820169/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-agent-naming-by-role/workspace-per-home-e2e.first-attempt-no-state-dir.log)
- [Unit suite log (rc=0)](https://github.com/3264studios/firstmate/blob/06a9c62850fd23c89744b64d001a6691a4820169/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-agent-naming-by-role/unit-fm-backend-herdr.log)

## Risk and compatibility

Herdr spawn and recovery placement changes are the main risk. Exact endpoint metadata remains authoritative; labels select presentation containers only. Existing live workers, including workers in legacy supervisor workspaces, remain discoverable. Recovery, focus restoration, and husk replacement retain their identity checks. Other backend adapters and worker tab labels are unchanged.

## Earlier CI evidence

The [initial CI run](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/35813862959) on the earlier head `efcc30e8` passed the Herdr lane but failed portable serial shards 1 and 9. The watcher failure matched the independent fix in https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/5362; this branch now includes that upstream fix. The board-render failure (`not listening after reconcile`, then `the board did not build`) also occurred on unrelated changes in [run 35816478153](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/35816478153/job/107038986171) and [run 35807288621](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/35807288621/job/107010839594). That complete suite passed unchanged locally and in the [base CI run](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/35810457763); its intermittent listener-startup cause remains unconfirmed. No board-render fix is included. These are historical results. The [current-head CI run](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/actions/runs/35824169394) passed on its first attempt, including both previously failing shards; no-mistakes returned `checks-passed`.

<details>
<summary>Original intent</summary>

I'd like agents to not start their name with firstmate or 2ndmate unless they are a firstmate or a 2ndmate.

Get a worker on it to submit an issue and a high-quality, well-checked / high-degree-of-rigor PR.

Context for reading the ask: in a Herdr session, each firstmate home keeps a workspace labelled `firstmate` (the primary home) or `2ndmate-<id>` (a secondmate home), and each worker normally gets its own presentation workspace labelled `└ <task-id> · p:<token>`, placed under its owner. Two things break the rule above:

1. When a worker's presentation workspace cannot be used - for example on a relaunch whose earlier workspace no longer exists or cannot be proven reusable, or when the presentation-order lock is contended - the spawn falls back to the flat layout and the worker becomes a tab INSIDE its owner's `firstmate` or `2ndmate-<id>` workspace, so in the sidebar the worker appears under, and reads as, a firstmate or second mate. Observed: a relaunched worker whose original presentation workspace was gone landed as a tab in `2ndmate-<id>`; a long-idle worker sits as a tab in `firstmate`.
2. Every worker's tab label is `fm-<task-id>`, a prefix naming firstmate, even though the worker is neither a firstmate nor a second mate.
The outcome wanted: an agent's visible name (workspace and tab labels) starts with `firstmate` or `2ndmate` only when that agent is a firstmate or a second mate; a worker is shown under its own name.

</details>

title: fix(bin): confirm Claude's background-work dialog on fm-control exit
body:
## Problem

`bin/fm-control.sh <id> exit` does not stop a Claude worker that has background shells running (`run_in_background` Bash tasks).
Claude Code answers `/exit` in that state with a confirmation dialog instead of exiting:

```text
   Background work is running
   The following will stop when you exit:

   shell · sleep 900

   ❯ 1. Exit and stop tasks
     2. Move to background and exit
     3. Stay

   Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel
```

(Claude Code 2.1.280; an earlier build showed the same dialog with only `1. Exit and stop tasks` / `2. Stay`.)
Firstmate never answered the dialog, so `exit` failed with `exit=unconfirmed` and the agent, its MCP servers, and its background tasks kept running.
When a task is cleaned up afterwards, those processes can survive as orphans and keep using memory.

## Reproduction

- Hermetic: the new `test_exit_confirms_background_work_dialog_once` case in `tests/fm-control.test.sh` fails on `706254de` with the same error seen in the field:

  ```text
  not ok - exit should stop a claude agent that asks to stop its background work
  error: exit-delivered t1 interrupt=not-needed exit-command=delivered agent-state=alive exit=unconfirmed; the agent did not stop within 0.05s: expected exit 0, got 1
  ```

- Live, with a real Claude Code 2.1.280 worker in a private tmux server, a hand-built task record, and one background `sleep 903`:

  ```text
  == base (HEAD 706254de), FM_CONTROL_EXIT_RETRIES=1
  error: exit-delivered lab1 interrupt=not-needed exit-command=delivered agent-state=alive exit=unconfirmed; the agent did not stop within 30s
  == sleep after:
  27336 sleep 903          <- still running, dialog still on screen

  == fix branch, FM_CONTROL_EXIT_RETRIES=1
  stopped lab1 harness=claude backend=tmux endpoint=fmses:fm-lab1 worktree=/tmp/fmdlab/wt
  == sleep after:
  none                     <- claude gone, pane back at its shell
  ```

Finding from the live lab: on tmux, `fm_tmux_composer_state` reads the dialog's `❯ 1. Exit and stop tasks` line as pending composer text, so the existing submit-retry Enter in `fm_tmux_submit_enter_core` already confirms the dialog by accident.
That is why the base code stops the agent on tmux with default retries, and why the lab pins `FM_CONTROL_EXIT_RETRIES=1` to model a backend without that retry, which is the Herdr case the diagnosis captured.
Changing that tmux retry behavior is out of scope here.

## Fix

- `bin/fm-control-lib.sh`: new per-harness table entry `fm_control_exit_confirm_key <harness> <visible-capture>`.
  For `claude` only, it prints `Enter` when the last non-blank lines of the screen are exactly this dialog: the two exact header lines, exactly one selected option equal to `❯ 1. Exit and stop tasks`, directly followed by one of the two verified second options, and the exact footer `Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel` as the last line.
  Every other screen, selection, or harness returns 1 and gets no key.
  The function is pure, like the rest of the lib's tables.
- `bin/fm-control.sh` `do_exit`: after the exit command, if the agent has not stopped within `FM_CONTROL_SETTLE_WAIT`, it reads the exact endpoint's visible screen once and sends that one Enter when the classifier matches.
  The existing dead-state postcondition is unchanged, and any other screen keeps today's `exit=unconfirmed` failure.
  The failure message now reports the full wait and adds `exit-dialog=confirmed` when the Enter was sent.
- `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/references/harness/claude.md` Exit row and one sentence in `docs/agent-control.md` record the verified behavior and point at the lib as owner.

The match is deliberately strict because the workspace-trust and bypass dialogs share the same footer with `❯ No, exit` selected, so a loose match could end a session by accident.

## Tests

- New captures under `tests/captures/claude-exit-dialog/` (README registered in `docs/documentation-audiences.json`): the 2.1.280 dialog, the earlier two-option dialog, and the 2.1.280 workspace-trust dialog as a negative case.
- Classifier unit test: accepts both dialogs, and rejects Stay selected (both layouts), the trust dialog, a dialog followed by a prompt, altered header text, an unverified second option, and a non-claude harness.
- Behavior tests through `bin/fm-control.sh`: the fake tmux renders the captured dialog after the `/exit` submit; the dialog receives exactly one Enter and exit reports `stopped`; a Stay-selected dialog and the trust dialog receive no key and keep `exit=unconfirmed`.
- The stubborn-agent test now sets `FM_CONTROL_SETTLE_WAIT=0.05`, because the default 5s window with a 0.01s poll added about 50s to the suite.

```text
$ bash tests/fm-control.test.sh
...
ok - fm-control exit: a stubborn agent reports delivered input and an unconfirmed exit
...
ok - fm-control exit dialog: only claude's exact dialog with option 1 selected is confirmed
ok - fm-control exit: claude's background-work dialog is confirmed with one Enter
ok - fm-control exit: any other dialog or selection keeps the unconfirmed exit
(38 ok, 0 not ok, 46.8s)

$ bash tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh
(69 ok, 0 not ok)

$ bash tests/fm-harness-adapter-references.test.sh
ok - harness adapter routing artifact is normalized and every target is readable

$ bin/fm-lint.sh
fm-lint.sh: ShellCheck 0.11.0 (pinned 0.11.0)
fm-lint-workflows.sh: 3 workflow files valid

$ bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh
fm-doc-audience-check: ok surfaces=103 local_links=456
```

## Not verified

- Herdr was not driven live: this task was not authorized to run Herdr lifecycle labs.
  The call goes through `fm_backend_visible_capture`, which for Herdr is `pane read --source visible`, the same viewport-only reader `bin/fm-spawn.sh` already uses, but no Herdr capture of this dialog is included.
- The dialog is classified once, after the settle window; if Claude ever draws it later than that, exit keeps today's unconfirmed failure.

## Independent review

A separate read-only Claude reviewer checked four angles: functional tests, architecture and isolation, simplification, and requirement alignment.
Its verdict was "ship after minor fixes", with no blockers.
It confirmed that the new tests fail without the `fm-control.sh` change, that the lib stays side-effect-free, and that nothing out of scope was added.
Addressed in the second commit: the classifier now also checks the second option line, the failure message reports the combined wait, the `FM_CONTROL_SETTLE_WAIT` header and the lib's table-2 header describe the new use, and a Stay-selected two-option case was added.
Left as is: the lack of a live Herdr capture, disclosed above.

## Instructions acknowledged

Before editing I read the operator's global agent instructions, this repo's `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and `firstmate-coding-guidelines`; the operator's optional development-policy file does not exist.
New production functions stay within 10 lines and 3 arguments; unrelated code was not refactored.
This PR is raised directly rather than through the no-mistakes gate that `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for, because the operator chose direct delivery for this task, so the `Require no-mistakes` check is expected to fail.
It is one of several independent fixes from the same diagnosis.
Teardown pane-session reaping, an orphan inventory, and the no-mistakes LaunchAgent leak will be separate PRs.

title: feat(bin): add kernel-backed gate lock for test-host heavy operations

api_response: body: "## Intent Many threads running at once collide over heavy validation and test-environment work. On the evening this was decided, four separate tasks sat waiting on validation runs that had already died, because each one decided whether the shared gate was busy by inspecting processes and guessing at process ids instead of holding a real lock. Reconsider what runs on the devbox versus the Omarchy test host, and limit one thread to a given test environment: one heavy operation at a time per host, with the lock released automatically by the operating system when the run ends, and one explicit writer for the shared k3d cluster. Devbox keeps authoring and fast checks; Omarchy keeps the heavy validation gate and the k3d acceptance cluster. Build that. ## What Changed - Add `bin/fm-gate-lock.sh` and `bin/fm-gate-lock-entry.py`, a `run`/`status` locking helper that serializes heavy validation gates, k3d resets/baselines, and image builds per test host using a kernel `flock` (local or over SSH), so the lock is released automatically on process exit/crash instead of relying on PID inspection. - Wire the new helper into `bin/fm-brief.sh` with a "Test-host heavy work" instruction directing agents to acquire the target host's lock via `fm-gate-lock.sh run --host --holder -- ` instead of guessing whether a host is busy from process state. - Document the devbox/Omarchy split and shared k3d writer convention in new `docs/test-host-gates.md`, register it in `docs/documentation-audiences.json`, list the two new scripts in `docs/scripts.md`, and add `tests/fm-gate-lock.test.sh` covering lock contention, timeout, crash-release, and argument-injection safety (including the SSH remote path). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix-round diff is a single-line addition (fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_UN) before printing free in status mode) that correctly closes the race window flagged in round 1 without adding new state, scope, or behavior; the rest of the change was already reviewed and is unchanged in this round. ## Testing Drove the gate-lock CLI directly (no Herdr surface is touched by this change, so the Herdr lab runbook does not apply): the bundled test suite passed live, and a targeted 840-probe concurrent-status stress test confirmed the reviewed race fix cuts the false-'held'-on-free-lock rate from ~76% (pre-fix) to ~0.1% (post-fix), consistent with the fix's own stated scope of shrinking, not eliminating, the race window. All driveable scenarios passed; only the real network/ssh leg of the remote-host path was untested due to lack of a reachable Omarchy host in this sandbox, which does not put the core intent in doubt. - Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | One heavy operation per host at a time (mutual exclusion + timeout) | ✅ pass | live | tests/fm-gate-lock.test.sh: a `run --holder first` occupies the default `heavy` lock for 3s; a concurrent `run --holder waiter --timeout 1` correctly times out (exit 75) in <4s while the first holder… | | Kernel flock releases automatically when the holder process is killed (no stale PID bookkeeping) | ✅ pass | live | tests/fm-gate-lock.test.sh: a held lock's process is `kill -9`'d mid-run; the very next `run --holder successor` acquires immediately and a subsequent `status` reports `free`. See fm-gate-lock-test-su… | | status probe releases its own flock before returning 'free' instead of leaking it until interpreter teardown (review finding status-trylock-race) | ✅ pass | live | Manual stress test: 40 concurrent `status` calls against a never-held lock, repeated across ~840 total probes on the post-fix binary, produced 1 false 'held' report (~0.12%). The same test against the… | | Shell-metacharacter / injection-bearing arguments are passed through literally to the wrapped command, not interpreted by a shell (adversarial) | ✅ pass | live | tests/fm-gate-lock.test.sh: args containing spaces, semicolons, and `$(touch SHOULD_NOT_EXIST)` are round-tripped byte-for-byte through both local `run` and the fake-ssh-routed `--host` remote path, a… | | Remote host mode routes the command through ssh with the same argument-safety guarantees (devbox → Omarchy split) | ✅ pass | live | tests/fm-gate-lock.test.sh: `run --host fakehost` against a stub `ssh` on PATH executes the wrapped command remotely and preserves injection-bearing arguments exactly. See fm-gate-lock-test-suite.log. |
Evidence: Concurrent status-probe race stress test (pre-fix vs post-fix comparison) Source: [Concurrent status-probe race stress test (pre-fix vs post-fix comparison)](https://github.com/jfrisch76/firstmate/blob/61157c4d16a0c67b0773f07041e10243f6adbecf/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-gate-concurrency-lock/status-race-stress.log) ```text Scenario: concurrent `bin/fm-gate-lock.sh status` polls against a lock that is actually free must not wrongly report "held" (review finding "status-trylock-race", fixed in 112ebda by calling fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_UN) before printing "free" instead of leaking the lock until interpreter teardown). Method: launched 40 concurrent `status` invocations against a freshly created, never-held lock file (fresh XDG_RUNTIME_DIR per trial) and counted how many wrongly printed "held: ..." instead of "free". === POST-FIX (target commit 112ebda, bin/fm-gate-lock-entry.py as shipped) === trial 0 (initial run): false-held = 1 / 40 <- observed once trial 1..5: false-held = 0 / 40 each trial 6..20 (aggregate of 15 trials): false-held = 0 / 600 TOTAL: 1 false-held out of 840 concurrent status probes (~0.12%) === PRE-FIX (base-of-feature commit f053b06, before the LOCK_UN-before-return fix) === Ran the same 40-way concurrent status stress test against the unmodified pre-review-fix binary (extracted via `git show f053b06:...` into a scratch dir, never touching the worktree): trial 1: false-held = 30 / 40 trial 2: false-held = 31 / 40 trial 3: false-held = 32 / 40 trial 4: false-held = 29 / 40 trial 5: false-held = 31 / 40 Pre-fix rate: ~153/200 (~76%) of concurrent status probes on a free lock wrongly reported "held: holder unavailable". Conclusion: the fix reduces the false-"held" rate on concurrent status polls of a free lock from ~76% to ~0.1% under the same 40-way concurrency stress. This matches the accepted fix's own framing ("shrinks the race window to nearly nothing without adding any new state or product behavior") rather than claiming full elimination. The residual ~1-in-800 occurrence is the expected, acknowledged residual of a NB-flock probe race, not a regression or unaddressed defect. ```
Evidence: bin/fm-gate-lock.sh test suite (mutual exclusion, timeout, crash-release, injection safety, ssh remote routing) Source: [bin/fm-gate-lock.sh test suite (mutual exclusion, timeout, crash-release, injection safety, ssh remote routing)](https://github.com/jfrisch76/firstmate/blob/61157c4d16a0c67b0773f07041e10243f6adbecf/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-gate-concurrency-lock/fm-gate-lock-test-suite.log) ```text fm-gate-lock tests passed ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-gate-lock-entry.py:40` - `fm-gate-lock.sh status` probes availability by taking a real exclusive flock on a fresh fd and, when it succeeds, prints "free" and returns without ever calling `fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_UN)` or closing the fd — the lock is only released implicitly when the whole Python process (including interpreter teardown) exits. See fm-gate-lock-test-suite.log. | - `bash tests/fm-gate-lock.test.sh` (bundled end-to-end suite: mutual exclusion, timeout exit code 75, kill-releases-lock, argument/injection safety local+remote) - Manual: 40-way concurrent `bin/fm-gate-lock.sh status` stress test against post-fix binary, repeated across 7 batches (~840 probes total) - Manual: same 40-way concurrent status stress test against the pre-fix binary extracted via `git show f053b06:bin/fm-gate-lock-entry.py` into a scratch directory, for quantified before/after comparison

title: fix: recover pending own-doorbell submissions on tmux
body:
## Intent Operator: fix the core issues. Plan item F1 from ~/projects/havenhaus-gtm/docs/plans/2026-09-23-core-orchestration-fixes.md, verbatim: ### F1. Firstmate: submit or clear the doorbell when the composer holds Firstmate's own text Row: `fm-composer-deadlock-and-doorbell-submit` (P1, firstmate, ship, no-mistakes, yolo off). - In `fm_task_inbox_ring`, when the composer verdict is `pending`, read the composer (the stock peek path) and compare it to the doorbell line this home generates. If it matches exactly, send `fm-send.sh --key Enter` (the documented retry at fm-send.sh:1162) instead of returning 1. If it holds anything else, keep the skip. Firstmate may submit its own text; it still never submits unknown text. - Same predicate in `fm-control.sh exit|relaunch`: a composer holding exactly the doorbell is cleared (submit, then proceed) rather than refused. - Root-cause the unsent Enter on Muse: fm-send's pre-Enter settle vs Muse's completion popup (fm-send.sh:80). If a longer settle for `harness=muse` makes the first submit stick, add it. - Tests: a fixture composer holding the doorbell -> ring submits; holding other text -> ring skips; exit with doorbell -> proceeds; exit with other text -> refuses. - Acceptance: a Muse lane launched after landing reads its 001.msg without human help. Review: non-author exact-head (Opus 5.5 low is the current first rung while Sol/Astra are out). Delivery: local guarded merge after review + live acceptance; upstream PR as contribution. ## What Changed - Submit byte-exact pending doorbells with Enter during inbox ringing and exit/relaunch; require a proven-empty composer before typing exit commands. - Add lossless tmux composer extraction with strict single-row boundaries, rejecting whitespace differences and unproven captures; Herdr recovery remains unsupported. - Add recovery and refusal regressions, including real tmux capture checks, and document Muse submit observations and unresolved Herdr acceptance without changing settle timing. ## Risk Assessment 🚨 High: The intended fleet backend still cannot recover its own pending doorbell, leaving the required durable fix incomplete. ## Testing Ran focused inbox, lifecycle, unsupported-backend, and popup-settle regressions successfully, including real tmux captures with stubbed agent/input behavior. title: fix: forbid temporary-HOME no-mistakes runs that leave a respawning launchd daemon
body:
## Problem

After a Firstmate task finished and was cleaned up, a `no-mistakes` daemon kept running and respawning.
It was the launchd job `com.kunchenguid.no-mistakes.daemon.049534d3`, installed by a real `no-mistakes` run that had a temporary `HOME` and `NM_HOME`.

`no-mistakes daemon start` installs a `KeepAlive=true`, `RunAtLoad=true` LaunchAgent labeled `com.kunchenguid.no-mistakes.daemon.<sha256(realpath(root))[:8]>`.
With a temporary `HOME`, the plist is written under `<tmp>/home/Library/LaunchAgents`, but `launchctl bootstrap gui/<uid>` loads the job into the real per-user domain, which `HOME` does not scope.
Deleting the temporary directory removes the plist file but leaves the loaded job in place.
Killing the daemon only makes launchd respawn it, and the new process recreates its root (a fresh `config.yaml` and `daemon.lock`).
The only way to end it is `launchctl bootout gui/<uid>/<label>`.

Firstmate's own `bin/` never registers a no-mistakes service, and its deterministic tests replace the binary with fakes.
The leak comes from an agent-driven step, such as a worker experiment or the agent-driven no-mistakes Test step, running the real CLI with a temporary `HOME`/`NM_HOME`.

## Reproduction (from the diagnosis)

- `launchctl list` showed `com.kunchenguid.no-mistakes.daemon.049534d3` next to the real daemon `...b870f7aa`.
- `049534d3` is the sha256 prefix of `/private/var/folders/.../tmp.X2jzezfrC7/nm`, and `b870f7aa` is the prefix of `/Users/javiermoya/.no-mistakes`.
- After pid 44058 was killed, launchd respawned it as 25699, which recreated its root.
- It stopped only after `launchctl bootout`.
- The label formula in this rule gives the live label on this host:

```text
$ NM_HOME=$HOME/.no-mistakes; printf %s "$(cd "$NM_HOME" && pwd -P)" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-8
b870f7aa
$ launchctl list | grep -o 'com.kunchenguid.no-mistakes.daemon[.a-z0-9]*'
com.kunchenguid.no-mistakes.daemon.b870f7aa
```

## Fix

This is fix 4 of the orphan-process diagnosis, Firstmate side only.

- `bin/fm-brief.sh` gains rule 8 in both the ship and the scout brief safety rules.
  The rule text lives in one single-quoted `NM_TEMP_HOME_RULE` variable, so the command renders unexpanded and has a single owner inside the script.
  It says never to run the real `no-mistakes` with a temporary `HOME` or `NM_HOME`.
  If that is unavoidable, the worker must boot out that temporary daemon job, never the shared one, in the same cleanup.
  The bootout has to run before the directory is deleted and while `NM_HOME` names the temporary root, which is `$HOME/.no-mistakes` when only `HOME` was temporary.
  The command is `launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/com.kunchenguid.no-mistakes.daemon.$(printf %s "$(cd "$NM_HOME" && pwd -P)" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-8)`.
- `.no-mistakes.yaml` `test.instructions` gets the same rule, because the no-mistakes Test agent never sees a worker brief.
  This is the one deliberate second copy.
- Secondmate charters are unchanged: they supervise, and their workers get these same generated briefs.

Out of scope and not implemented: the optional read-only startup check for leftover labels, any change to the no-mistakes project, and the other fixes from the diagnosis, which ship as separate PRs.

## Tests (TDD)

- `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` `test_ship_and_scout_forbid_temp_home_no_mistakes` renders no-mistakes, direct-PR, local-only and scout briefs.
  For each one it asserts the prohibition and the exact, unexpanded bootout command, using a fixed-string match.
- `tests/fm-nm-test-contract.test.sh` `test_nm_test_instructions_forbid_temp_home_daemon` parses `.no-mistakes.yaml` as YAML, the same way the existing contract test does, and asserts the same rule and command in `test.instructions`.

RED, before the fix:

```text
$ bash tests/fm-brief.test.sh
...
ok - fm-brief.sh: ship and scout scaffolds teach validation-round pauses
not ok - no-mistakes brief did not forbid a temporary-HOME no-mistakes run
$ bash tests/fm-nm-test-contract.test.sh
ok - no-mistakes does not configure commands.test
not ok - test.instructions must forbid a temporary-HOME no-mistakes run (missing: 'Never run the real no-mistakes with a temporary HOME or NM_HOME')
```

GREEN, after the fix:

```text
$ bash tests/fm-brief.test.sh      # rc=0, 29 ok
ok - fm-brief.sh: ship and scout briefs forbid temporary-HOME no-mistakes runs
$ bash tests/fm-nm-test-contract.test.sh
ok - no-mistakes does not configure commands.test
ok - no-mistakes Test instructions forbid a temporary-HOME daemon
$ bin/fm-test-run.sh tests/fm-brief.test.sh tests/fm-nm-test-contract.test.sh tests/fm-ask-user-authority.test.sh tests/fm-classify-corr-token.test.sh tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh tests/fm-subagent-pretool-check.test.sh tests/fm-tangle-guard.test.sh tests/fm-task-delivery.test.sh tests/fm-voice-relay.test.sh tests/fm-lint.test.sh tests/fm-gate-refuse.test.sh
FM_TEST_SUMMARY total=13 failed=0 skipped_gate=0 duration_ms=930206
$ bin/fm-lint.sh                  # rc=0
fm-lint.sh: ShellCheck 0.11.0 (pinned 0.11.0)
fm-lint-workflows.sh: actionlint 1.7.12 (pinned 1.7.12)
fm-lint-workflows.sh: 3 workflow files valid
$ bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh    # rc=0
```

That run covers every script that consumes `fm-brief.sh`, plus the tests that read `.no-mistakes.yaml`.
The live Herdr e2e scripts that `--changed` selects were deliberately not run, because this task is not authorized to drive Herdr lifecycle.
After the review rewording, `fm-brief.test.sh`, `fm-nm-test-contract.test.sh` and `fm-lint.sh` were re-run and passed.

## Independent review

A separate Claude subagent reviewed the change read-only from four angles: functional tests, architecture and isolation, anti-slop simplification, and requirement alignment.
It found no blockers.
- It confirmed both new tests fail on the `origin/main` sources and pass with the fix.
- It confirmed the command renders unexpanded in every ship mode and in the scout brief.
- It confirmed the formula matches the live label and that the variable is safe on Bash 3.2.
- Addressed: it said the case where only `HOME` is temporary was implicit, where an unset `NM_HOME` would make `cd ""` hash the wrong directory. The rule now says `$HOME/.no-mistakes`.
- Addressed: it said the bootout must run while `NM_HOME` still names the temporary root. The rule now says so and adds "never the shared one", so it cannot be read as conflicting with rule 7.
- Addressed: it flagged mismatched "respawns forever" wording between the two copies, and suggested collapsing the shellcheck comment.
- Not addressed, noted as a follow-up: when only `NM_HOME` is temporary and `HOME` is real, the temporary label's plist probably stays in the real `~/Library/LaunchAgents` after bootout and could reload at the next login.
  The reviewer inferred this and did not reproduce it.
  The rule's main line (never do this) already prevents it, and the task asked for exactly the bootout command, so removing the plist is left to the upstream fix below.

## Suggested upstream issue for no-mistakes

> **`daemon start` under a temporary `HOME`/`NM_HOME` installs a KeepAlive LaunchAgent into the real `gui/<uid>` domain that outlives its root**
>
> On macOS, `no-mistakes daemon start` with a non-default root (temporary `HOME` and/or `NM_HOME`) bootstraps `com.kunchenguid.no-mistakes.daemon.<hash>` (`KeepAlive=true`, `RunAtLoad=true`) into the real per-user launchd domain, which `HOME` does not scope.
> Deleting the temporary root removes neither the loaded job nor, when `HOME` is real, the plist; killing the daemon makes launchd respawn it, and it recreates the deleted root.
> Only `launchctl bootout gui/<uid>/<label>` stops it.
> Suggested behavior: do not install a managed service when the root is non-default or under a temporary directory (or offer an opt-out such as `--no-service` / an env var), and make `daemon stop` (or a new `daemon uninstall`) boot out and remove the service it installed.
> A daemon whose root disappears could also exit instead of recreating it.

## Instructions acknowledged

- I read `/Users/javiermoya/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Applied: everything is in English, TDD was followed (RED recorded before GREEN), new code is within the size limits, and there are no filler abstractions. The independent multi-angle review above was run. No merge is requested or performed here.
- `/ssd/datos-mac/workspace/config/development-policy.md` is absent (`No such file or directory`).
- I read this repo's `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and loaded `.agents/skills/firstmate-coding-guidelines/SKILL.md` before editing. Applied: the one-owner rule (one variable for both scaffolds, with the YAML copy justified above), tests that exercise the public scaffold and parsed config, shellcheck and `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean, and no `commands.test` added.
- Per the task's delivery instructions, this PR was raised directly, without the no-mistakes pipeline.
  The `PR must be raised via no-mistakes` check may therefore report its expected result for a non-pipeline PR.

title: fix(bin): stop leaked firstmate environment from blinding state reads and unblock shared pool slots
body:
## Intent

The developer wanted two internal defects in the firstmate repository fixed and shipped. Defect 1: exported FM_CREW_STATE_META_OVERRIDE, FM_CREW_STATE_STATUS_OVERRIDE, FM_SESSION_START_STAGE_FILE and FM_SESSIONSTART_SUPERVISOR_PID leaked fleet-wide and made bin/fm-crew-state.sh report every task as unknown, so the exporter must scope them to its own child process and fm-crew-state.sh must refuse an override whose target path does not exist while still resolving a valid one. Defect 2: bin/fm-teardown.sh could not retire tasks sharing one treehouse pool slot, so slot ownership must be determined before the exclusive record scan and the reassigned case must skip that scan, keeping the scan unchanged for an absent or self-owned claim, with a regression test covering three records on one slot, the claim naming the newest task, and teardown of both older tasks succeeding without touching the slot. Constraints were to stay inside the scope of those two defects, avoid refactors and unrelated fixes, follow CONTRIBUTING and the coding guidelines (one sentence per line, plain dash, shellcheck-clean bin scripts, colocated tests, maintainer-verification evidence), not hand-edit state/<id>.meta, not add a bypass flag, verify with bash -n and the repo's test command, and never run teardown against a live task id or pool slot. The developer later added that public-facing text must be scrubbed of private task names and incident/date pointers and that the public branch name must be generic rather than carrying the private task id.

## What Changed
- `bin/fm-crew-state.sh` refuses an explicit `FM_CREW_STATE_META_OVERRIDE` or `FM_CREW_STATE_STATUS_OVERRIDE` whose target no longer exists with exit 3 and a stderr diagnostic naming the override and path, unsets those inputs before its own child processes start, and documents the exit-3 contract in its header.
- `bin/backends/herdr.sh` launches the named server through a new `fm_backend_herdr_server_env_scrub` that default-denies every `FM_*` variable except its own `FM_HERDR_*`/`FM_BACKEND_HERDR_*` namespaces plus the harness identity markers, and `bin/fm-session-start.sh` takes `FM_SESSION_START_STAGE_FILE` into a shell variable before its first stage so nothing the digest starts inherits the marker.
- `bin/fm-teardown.sh` decides pool-slot ownership before the record-exclusivity scan at both the top-level and descendant preflight call sites, so a slot claimed by another task takes the reassignment path and skips that scan while an absent or self-owned claim keeps it unchanged; regression tests cover a three-record shared slot, the descendant secondmate-home case, the stale-override refusal, and the server/digest environment scrub, and `tests/lib.sh` clears ambient leaked markers.
- `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/herdr-backend.md` describe the ownership-then-scan order and the default-deny server environment rule.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Both defects are pinned at their shared boundaries with the same invariant at every exclusivity call site, the relaxed guard only changes the reassigned-claim case where no slot step runs (destructive slot work stays gated by teardown_owns_worktree/child ownership), the absent- and self-owned-claim scan is unchanged, and the environment fixes are a strict superset of the previous scrubbing with no found leak-back path.

## Testing

`I derived ten scenarios from the two defects and drove every one against the real products in isolated environments. Defect 1: the live crew-state CLI refuses a stale snapshot override with exit 3 and a diagnostic naming the variable and dead path (the pre-fix copy answers the same command with a fake "no metadata for <id>", so the regression is reproduced before and fixed after), still resolves a valid override, still resolves a status-less capture whose snapshot directory exists, still reports a genuinely absent task as the normal rc-0 verdict, and drops both overrides before its own children (git-probe observation). Fleet-wide leakage is closed at its two producers: the real session-start digest child no longer exports its stage marker to the children it starts (while still writing the breadcrumb the parent's truncation banner reads), and a herdr server started through the real adapter in throwaway lab sessions hands none of the leaked names to a later pane, proven against an unscrubbed control server that leaks all of them, with the adapter's own prefixes, unrelated environment, named-session routing, and the live default session untouched. Defect 2: the live teardown CLI retires both older records that share one claimed pool slot without touching the slot, claim, or worker, still refuses for the claimant, retires a secondmate home over two shared child records through the descendant preflight, and keeps refusing when the claim is absent or self-owned and another record names the same path - both call sites. The changed tests' own suites pass. Live evidence is in the run's evidence directory (four driver logs plus four suite logs and the driver scripts). One caveat that does not affect the verdict: tmux is not installed on this host, so the pane-backed verdict value of a resolved read stayed "backend unreachable" in the crew-state driver; the override-resolution behaviour under test is proven, and the status-log verdict path itself is covered by the repo's hermetic suite. One non-reproducible flake is recorded as an info finding.`

title: fix(bin): avoid argument limits in contribution snapshots
body:
## Intent

Fix the defect reported in https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/5349 and send the fix upstream through the repository's documented no-mistakes pull-request path.
The issue: bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh --contribution-input passes the full backlog JSON and the task-record JSON to jq through --argjson (line 1991 at commit 39f4c2af).
On Linux a single argument is capped by MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131072 bytes); a home with 79 backlog items produced a 159047-byte backlog JSON, so the kernel refused to exec jq and the session-start digest printed /usr/bin/jq: Argument list too long.
The script still exited 0 with a broken result.
Expected: transport both JSON documents through temporary files and --slurpfile, as the default snapshot path already does a few lines later (JSON_TRANSPORT_DIR, BACKLOG_JSON_FILE, TASKS_JSON_FILE) and as lines 938, 975, 1724, and 1928 already do, and propagate a non-zero exit when that jq invocation fails.
Keep the change surgical: only this defect, nothing else in the script.

## What Changed

- Transport contribution backlog and task JSON through temporary files and `jq --slurpfile`, avoiding per-argument size limits.
- Propagate contribution-input assembly failures and add regression coverage for oversized backlogs and failing `jq` assembly.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The surgical change removes ARG_MAX exposure for both JSON documents, preserves the output contract, propagates jq failure, reuses existing cleanup, and adds behavioral regression coverage without introducing unrelated behavior.

## Testing

Reproduced the original ARG_MAX failure on base 39f4c2af, passed the focused target regression test, drove oversized backlog and task documents through the real target CLI, verified injected jq failure returned non-zero, captured transcript/JSON evidence, and left the worktree clean.
