title: feat(bin): add an opt-in per-home worker account pin
body:
## Intent

Implement ready-for-pr issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/4265: add an opt-in per-home account pin so a home that mixes work and personal accounts does not spend an ambient account unintentionally.

Substance of issue 4265: one person runs a fleet across more than one account for the same runner, a work account and a personal one. A worker launch resolves whichever account is ambient for that runner, so which side a task lands on depends on machine state rather than on the home that dispatched the task. A task can run on the wrong account with no signal at launch, surfacing later as an unrelated-looking authorization or quota failure, or not surfacing at all. There is no way for a home to declare "my workers belong to this side" and have a launch refuse when it cannot tell, instead of guessing.
Expected behaviour: a home can declare, in private local configuration, which account its own workers and scouts launch on for a given runner. A launch that cannot resolve a signed-in pinned account refuses with an actionable message rather than falling back to whatever is ambient. A home that declares nothing behaves exactly as it does today. The opt-in is the substance of the proposal rather than a caveat: a single-account installation should see no behaviour change at all, and the pin should stay inert until a home creates it.

## What Changed

- Adds `bin/fm-worker-account-lib.sh`, which reads two optional local files: `config/claude-account` (`ordinary` or an absolute Claude config root) and `config/pi-account` (a root on line 1, and on line 2 the Pi providers this home may use). Before any endpoint, worktree, or task record exists, the spawn asks the runner itself whether the pinned account is signed in (`claude auth status`, or `pi auth check`, falling back to `pi --list-models`). That check runs with a stripped environment, so a credential in firstmate's own environment cannot stand in for the pinned login. A malformed file, an unusable root, or a signed-out account refuses the launch with a message naming the file to fix, and it never falls back to the ambient account. With neither file present, launches are unchanged.
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` applies the pin to ships, scouts, local secondmates, raw Claude commands, and relaunches:
  - A pinned Claude launch gets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set to the pinned root, or unset for `ordinary`. It also has the environment credentials Claude ranks above a stored login removed, such as `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.
  - A pinned Pi launch gets `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` and `--provider`. It must also use `--model <provider>/<id>` with a provider listed in the file.
  - These launches refuse: raw Pi commands, and raw Claude commands that set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or one of the removed credentials themselves.
  - The pin is printed as `account=` / `account_provider=` on the `spawned` line and in the task record. Unpinned records are byte-identical to today's.
- `bin/fm-control.sh` checks the pin before a relaunch stops the running agent, so a stale or signed-out pin refuses while nothing has changed yet. Pins are not inherited into secondmate homes. The contract is documented in `docs/configuration.md` and related docs, and new unit and live end-to-end tests cover it (`tests/fm-worker-account*.test.sh`, `tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh`).

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix round does what the user asked: when a Claude pin is active, a raw Claude command that sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or a shed credential is refused before any endpoint or task record exists, the message names the variable, homes with no pin behave as before, and the pin stays inert until a home creates config/claude-account.

## Testing

I first ran the change's regression tests: the tests/fm-worker-account.test.sh suite and the two account-pin cases in tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh, which use fake runners. I also ran the default-on live sign-in check guard against the real claude 2.1.280 and pi 0.86.1 (pi-signed is not installed). All passed. I then used a lab driver script, kept in the evidence directory, to exercise ten scenarios in an isolated fm-lab-* Herdr session created through bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh and torn down afterwards; the teardown tripwire confirmed the default session was unchanged. Each worker was checked by reading the environment of the live claude or pi process running in the task's worktree (/proc/pid/environ), by reading the task record, and by reading the pane text. The pinned Claude pane shows "API Usage Billing" (the pinned root's synthetic key), and the pinned Pi pane shows OpenAI rejecting that root's stored synthetic key under (openai). Every scenario I could drive passed. The live half of "relaunch follows the pin" is untested for the reason given in its scenario. This is a CLI and launch-environment change, so pane text captures and a CLI transcript are the visual evidence; there is no rendered UI to screenshot.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 9 of 10 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| An unpinned home spawns a Claude worker exactly as before: the ambient CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is forwarded and no account= appears | ✅ pass | live | lab-transcript.txt S1: spawned line and task record have no account=; the worker process env keeps CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<ambient-claude> and the ambient ANTHROPIC_API_KEY |
| A home with config/claude-account naming a signed-in root launches its Claude worker on that root, drops the ambient API key, records account=, and writes workspace trust into the pinned root | ✅ pass | live | lab-transcript.txt S2: spawned line and record show account=<work-claude>; worker env CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<work-claude>, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY absent; trust entry present in <work-claude>/.claude.json; pinn… |
| A pin naming a signed-out root refuses the spawn with an actionable message before any task record or pane exists | ✅ pass | live | lab-transcript.txt S3: the real `claude auth status` check refuses with a sign-in hint; rc=1; no acctO.meta; lab pane count 2 -> 2 |
| A malformed pin (relative path) refuses the spawn and names the file to fix | ✅ pass | live | lab-transcript.txt S4: error names config/claude-account and its expected shape; rc=1; no task record |
| Adversarial: under a Claude pin, a raw command that sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is refused, the message names the variable and how to proceed, and nothing launches | ✅ pass | live | lab-transcript.txt S5: both raw commands refused with rc=1 and no task record; S5b: a plain raw `claude` command under the pin runs on the pinned root with the API key removed |
| An unpinned home still accepts a raw `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=... claude` override | ✅ pass | live | lab-transcript.txt S6: spawn succeeds with no account=; the worker runs with the raw command's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Live driver: real bin/fm-spawn.sh + bin/fm-control.sh, real claude and pi,
# in an isolated fm-lab-* Herdr session. Synthetic account roots only (a Claude
# apiKeyHelper root, a Pi root with a stored fake OpenAI key), so no real
# account is spent and no model call can succeed.
set -u
ROOT=${ROOT:?}
EV=${EV:?}
HELPER="$ROOT/bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh"
. "$ROOT/tests/herdr-test-safety.sh"
herdr_forget_inherited_pane

TMP=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-acct-lab.XXXXXX")
SESSION=$("$HELPER" name acctpin) || exit 1
export HERDR_SESSION="$SESSION"
WTS=()
LOG="$EV/lab-transcript.txt"
: > "$LOG"
say() { printf '%s\n' "$*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }
cleanup() {
  local wt
  for wt in ${WTS[@]+"${WTS[@]}"}; do treehouse return --force "$wt" >/dev/null 2>&1; done
  "$HELPER" teardown "$SESSION" 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG"
  say "teardown rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
  rm -rf "$TMP"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

# Synthetic roots.
AMB="$TMP/ambient-claude"; WORK="$TMP/work-claude"; EMPTY="$TMP/signed-out-claude"
mkdir -p "$AMB" "$WORK" "$EMPTY"
printf '{"apiKeyHelper":"echo sk-ant-ambient-synthetic"}\n' > "$AMB/settings.json"
printf '{"apiKeyHelper":"echo sk-ant-work-synthetic","skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt":true}\n' > "$WORK/settings.json"
# Skip first-run onboarding in the synthetic roots so the worker reaches its prompt.
for r in "$AMB" "$WORK"; do printf '{"hasCompletedOnboarding":true,"theme":"dark","bypassPermissionsModeAccepted":true}\n' > "$r/.claude.json"; done
PIROOT="$TMP/pi-work"; mkdir -p "$PIROOT"
printf '{"openai":{"type":"api_key","key":"sk-fm-synthetic"}}\n' > "$PIROOT/auth.json"; chmod 600 "$PIROOT/auth.json"

# The lab server (and so every pane) inherits an ambient account: another
# Claude root and a credential Claude ranks above a stored login.
export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$AMB" ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-ambient-pane-synthetic
"$HELPER" provision "$SESSION" 2>&1 | tee -a "$LOG" || exit 1
SOCK=$("$HELPER" run "$SESSION" session list --json | jq -r --arg s "$SESSION" '.sessions[]|select(.name==$s)|.socket_path')

PROJ="$TMP/proj"; mkdir -p "$PROJ"; git -C "$PROJ" init -q; echo x > "$PROJ/README.md"
git -C "$PROJ" add .; git -C "$PROJ" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@e.invalid commit -qm i
git clone -q --bare "$PROJ" "$PROJ.origin.git"; git -C "$PROJ" remote add origin "file://$PROJ.origin.git"

H="$TMP/home"; mkdir -p "$H/state" "$H/config" "$H/data"
printf 'off\n' > "$H/config/herdr-presentation-spaces"
brief() {
  mkdir -p "$H/data/$1"
  cat > "$H/data/$1/brief.md" <<EOF
# Task
Delivery contract: mode=local-only
## Captain's intent
Live account pin check for $1; do nothing.

## Firstmate spec
Do nothing.
EOF
}
spawn() { # <id> <args...>
  local id=$1; shift
  brief "$id"
  env -u HERDR_ENV -u HERDR_PANE_ID HERDR_SESSION="$SESSION" HERDR_SOCKET_PATH="$SOCK" \
    FM_SPAWN_NO_GUARD=1 FM_HOME="$H" FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$ROOT" \
    "$ROOT/bin/fm-spawn.sh" "$id" "$PROJ" --mode local-only --yolo off --backend herdr "$@" 2>&1
}
meta() { cat "$H/state/$1.meta" 2>/dev/null; }
track() { local w; w=$(meta "$1" | sed -n 's/^worktree=//p'); [ -z "$w" ] || WTS+=("$w"); }
# proc_env <id> <exe-name>: env + argv of the runner process running in the task worktree.
proc_env() {
  local wt pid c
  wt=$(meta "$1" | sed -n 's/^worktree=//p')
  for i in $(seq 1 40); do
    for pid in $(pgrep -u "$UID" -x "$2" 2>/dev/null) $(pgrep -u "$UID" -f "$2" 2>/dev/null); do
      c=$(readlink "/proc/$pid/cwd" 2>/dev/null) || continue
      [ "$c" = "$wt" ] || continue
      printf 'pid=%s cwd=%s\nargv: %s\n' "$pid" "$c" "$(tr '\0' ' ' < /proc/$pid/cmdline | cut -c1-200)"
      [ "$2" != pi ] || printf 'launch line: %s\n' "$(grep -o 'PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=[^;]*--provider [^ ]* --model [^ ]*' "$(ls -t /tmp/fm-$1+*/launch.*.sh 2>/dev/null | head -1)" | head -1)"
      tr '\0' '\n' < "/proc/$pid/environ" | grep -E '^(CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR|ANTHROPIC_API_KEY|PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR)=' | sed 's/^/env: /'
      tr '\0' '\n' < "/proc/$pid/environ" | grep -qE '^ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=' || echo "env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY <absent>"
      return 0
    done

  done
  echo "no $2 process found in $wt"
}

title: fix(bin): let a slot claim resolve a teardown record collision
body:
## Reproduction

```
$ bin/fm-teardown.sh ti-session-silent-stop
REFUSED: task ti-session-silent-stop's recorded worktree /home/wentao/.treehouse/ti-agent-731776/1/ti-agent is also task ti-turn-budget-silent-stop's recorded worktree.
Returning that pool slot would kill ti-turn-budget-silent-stop's processes and reset its copy, so nothing was changed - not even with --force.
Reconcile whichever record is wrong (bin/fm-crew-state.sh ti-session-silent-stop; bin/fm-crew-state.sh ti-turn-budget-silent-stop), then re-run teardown.
```

`--force` produced the same refusal. The pool had already handed that slot to the other task, and the slot itself said so: `/home/wentao/.treehouse/ti-agent-731776/1/.fm-slot-owner` read `task=ti-turn-budget-silent-stop` and `home=/home/wentao/wentao-agent-workspace`.

The same refusal also blocked the live task's own cleanup, because both records named the same live path.

## Root cause

`require_exclusive_worktree_slot_record` in `bin/fm-teardown.sh` scanned every other task record for the same live path and returned 1 unconditionally on the first match, before the slot's own owner claim was read. The documented reassignment branch (`require_owned_worktree_slot_record`, `TEARDOWN_SLOT_REASSIGNED_RC`) was therefore unreachable whenever a second record named the slot - the exact state a reused pool slot produces.

## Fix

The function now reads the slot's claim first. A readable claim names the record that actually took the slot, so the colliding record is proven stale and the collision alone is no longer a refusal:

- the claim names this record (`mine`): the colliding record is the stale one, and this record's own cleanup proceeds;
- the claim names another task (`other`): this record's slot is gone, and `require_owned_worktree_slot_record` marks the slot reassigned so every step that would kill, reset, or return it is skipped;
- the claim is absent or unreadable: the refusal is unchanged, `--force` included.

One collision stays a refusal even when the claim names this record: another record whose `home=` is this slot. A `home=` owner takes its slot through Treehouse's own durable lease, which never rewrites the claim, so a leftover claim naming this task cannot prove that a home on the slot has been retired. That case now says exactly that and names the home record to reconcile.

Nothing else is relaxed. Every step that would touch the slot keeps its own gate on the same claim, `--force` still has no authority over another task's live work, and its branch-lease interaction is untouched. The unreadable-claim refusal now also names the claim file in the collision state, which is what the script header already promised.

## Verified

`tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh` grows `test_slot_claim_resolves_a_record_collision_without_an_interlock`, which builds the interlock in an isolated home: stale record A, live record B, both `worktree=` the same pool slot, and a claim naming B. It asserts all four acceptance scenarios against a live worker in the slot:

1. A's cleanup completes (its endpoint closed, its check and trust artifacts and record removed, no pending backlog close left behind, no refusal) while the slot keeps B's worker alive, B's record, B's checkout, and B's claim, and no Treehouse return is issued.
2. B's cleanup then completes too - the stale record no longer blocks it - removing B's record and claim and returning the slot.
3. With the claim removed, the same collision refuses for both records and `--force` does not widen it.
4. With a claim file that cannot be read as a claim, the same collision refuses for both records and names the claim file to inspect.

A second new test, `test_home_slot_collision_still_refuses_under_this_records_own_claim`, covers the narrow case above: a record whose `home=` is the slot keeps refusing under this record's own claim, and follows a claim that names another task.

Before the fix, the interlock test failed with the reported defect:

```
not ok - a stale record could not finish its own cleanup on a slot another task holds: ...
```

Results: `bash tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh` -> 28/28 pass. `shellcheck bin/fm-teardown.sh` (0.11.0) and `bin/fm-lint.sh bin/fm-teardown.sh tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh` are clean, with no new findings against the base revision. The full repository suite result is in the comments below.

Note on the head branch: this machine's GitHub account has pull-only access to this repository, so `git push origin` is refused with `403` (that credential gap is tracked separately). The branch is pushed to a fork of this repository under the same account, `wentaonb123/firstmate-1`, and this PR is opened from there; the commit and diff are unchanged.

title: feat(bin): record no-mistakes pipeline spend per task at teardown
body:
## Intent

Implement ready-for-pr issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/4238: no-mistakes pipeline spend must reach Firstmate's durable task records so review-loop cost is visible.

## What Changed
- Adds `bin/fm-pipeline-spend.sh record <task-id>`. It opens no-mistakes' `state.sqlite` read-only and finds the task's runs by repository, current branch, and the oldest surviving reflog entry of that branch. It then adds up the agent invocations of those runs: counts, exit statuses, duration, and input, output, cache-read, and cache-creation tokens. Input, output, and cache-read tokens use no-mistakes' per-round delta columns, so a resumed session is not counted twice. Any token value no-mistakes did not record is counted as unknown, never as zero. The script appends one JSON line per task incarnation to the private `data/pipeline-spend.jsonl` ledger. If it runs again for an incarnation already in the ledger, it appends nothing.
- `bin/fm-teardown.sh` calls `record` for every ship task whose local copy it owns. The call runs before the task branch is deleted and before `state/<id>.meta` is removed. It is best effort: a failure prints a warning and cleanup continues.
- Moves the state-database path logic (`NM_HOME` default, and a relative `NM_HOME` resolved from the worktree) into a shared `fm_nm_state_db` helper in `bin/fm-nm-run-lib.sh`, which run selection now uses. Adds `tests/fm-pipeline-spend.test.sh` and new teardown tests, routes both to the `pr-forge` test family, and documents the ledger in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, and `docs/scripts.md`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change adds a new best-effort ledger writer that only reads the no-mistakes state database (opened read-only). Teardown calls it after the run is concluded and before the branch and meta are removed, and any failure only prints a warning. Tests exercise it through the real teardown/record entrypoints, and the round-1 user decisions (drop `show`, fixed 30s bound, comment fix) are applied.

## Testing

I ran the recorder in a scratch FM_HOME against this task's real pooled treehouse worktree and the real no-mistakes state database, which it opened read-only. It recorded 2 runs and 7 invocations for the task. For the finished run, the input, output, cache-read and cache-write totals (196, 1074, 4,894,896 and 429,232) match `no-mistakes stats` row for row. A second call appended nothing. Adversarial calls behaved as the script documents: exit 1 for a missing task or a secondmate, exit 2 for an unsafe id or the removed `show` subcommand, and an "unavailable" record with a reason when the task copy is gone. I did not run a real teardown against a live task, because that would delete a real worktree, so the teardown scenario is marked untested live. The targeted fm-pipeline-spend and fm-teardown test files pass. They drive the real teardown script with a fake no-mistakes CLI and a fixture database, and they show the ledger line is written before the branch and the task record are removed. The change has no UI, so the evidence is CLI transcripts. I removed the scratch files and the worktree is clean.

fm-pipeline-spend.sh - attribute a task's no-mistakes pipeline spend to the
task and keep it in Firstmate's own records.

Usage:
  fm-pipeline-spend.sh record <task-id>

record appends the task's pipeline spend as one JSON object on one line of
data/pipeline-spend.jsonl, at most once per task incarnation (task id plus
the record's spawn_gen): repeating it for an incarnation already in the
ledger appends nothing, so a retried cleanup never counts a task twice.
bin/fm-teardown.sh calls record for every ship task whose local copy it
cleans up, before it deletes the task branch this script attributes runs by
and before it removes state/<id>.meta. The ledger is private and gitignored
with the rest of data/.
Exit status: 0 when a record was recorded or already present (including one
whose source is unavailable), 1 when the task record is missing, names a
secondmate, or the record could not be built or written, 2 for bad usage.

Source. no-mistakes keeps each agent invocation's token usage only in its
local state database, one agent_invocations row per invocation; its
environment reference documents those fields, and `no-mistakes stats --run
<id>` renders the same rows as a human table. There is no machine-readable
export yet, so this script reads the database read-only (mode=ro), located
by bin/fm-nm-run-lib.sh's fm_nm_state_db, and bounded by 30 seconds per
no-mistakes or database call.

Attribution. A task's runs are the runs no-mistakes recorded for the task
copy's repository and current branch since that branch was created:
  - repository: the `repo:` line `no-mistakes axi` prints from the task copy,
    which is the CLI's own resolution (a pooled worker copy resolves to the
    registered primary clone), matched exactly against repos.working_path;
  - branch: the task copy's current branch, the one bin/fm-crew-state.sh
    reads;
  - since: the oldest surviving reflog entry of that branch. spawn_gen cannot
    bound the task, because a relaunch mints a new one while the same branch
    keeps validating. Teardown deletes the branch, so a later task that
    reuses the id and branch name starts a fresh reflog and never inherits an
    earlier task's runs. With no reflog, every run on the branch counts and
    since is null.
Two live tasks sharing one branch name in one repository would both count
its runs; each record lists run ids, so such an overlap stays visible.

Counting. Every invocation of those runs counts, whatever its exit status
(ok, error, cancelled), and each token field is no-mistakes' own, summed
without reinterpretation (whether input includes cache reads differs by
agent; see no-mistakes' environment reference):
  - input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens sum the per-round
    delta_* columns, because a resumed session's raw counters are cumulative
    for some agents (codex) and summing them would count earlier review
    rounds again. A row with no delta (written before the delta columns
    existed) falls back to its raw counter only when its session_mode is not
    `resumed`, since no-mistakes defines a cold, started, or fallback row's
    delta as its raw counter.
  - cache_creation_tokens sums the raw counter, which has no per-round
    delta, so it counts only for a row whose counters are proven
    per-invocation: not resumed, or every delta equal to its raw counter.
  - reasoning is not summed: no-mistakes counts it inside output and keeps no
    per-round delta for it.
A value no-mistakes did not record is unknown, never zero: each token field
carries its known total and how many invocations were unknown, so a total
with unknown > 0 is a lower bound.

Record schema (this header is its one owner). One JSON object:
  task, spawn_gen         the task id and the incarnation recorded in its meta
  recorded_at             UTC time the record was built
  source                  "no-mistakes-state", or "unavailable" when the runs
                          could not be read; reason then says why, total
                          is null, and runs and purposes are empty
  repo, branch, since     the attribution above (since as UTC time or null)
  total                   a tally over every counted invocation
  runs[]                  {id, status, created_at} plus a tally, oldest first
  purposes[]              {purpose} plus a tally, by no-mistakes' purpose
                          name (review, review-fix, test, document, ci, ...)
A tally is {invocations, exit: {<exit status>: count}, duration_ms,
input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_creation_tokens}, and
each token field is {total, unknown}.

title: feat(bin): add native Orca supervised workers and Secondmates
body:
## Intent

Implement all planned phases of the Firstmate + Orca integration in one closed loop, correcting bugs and rerunning tests until the complete migration is finished. The words authorizing this scope were: "you may complete all phases in a closed loop, fixing bugs until completion". The completed capability spike established that Orca 1.4.206 exposes real worker-start, worker-read, worker-abandon, worker-show, worker-list, worker-release, terminal wait, worktree ps, mailbox/ask, and durable Run/Task/Dispatch identities. The final result must make native supervision usable without losing Firstmate\x27s isolation, steering, validation, recovery, delivery, cleanup, and persistent Secondmate guarantees.

## What Changed
- Adds a native Orca supervision adapter (`bin/backends/orca-supervised.sh` plus a JSON helper). `fm-spawn.sh --orca-mode supervised` runs the full launch in the task's Orca terminal first, then attaches it with `orchestration worker-start --terminal`. Before treating the launch as consumed, it checks that the returned Run/Task/Dispatch/worker/worktree identities match and reads a complete `worker-read` transcript. The mode is capability-gated: agent-context schema 1, the required command shapes, a Claude/Codex/Cursor harness, and a live `ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE`. If any check fails, ordinary ships and scouts fall back to terminal mode.
- Orca now accepts persistent `--secondmate` spawns, but only through native supervision bound to an exact existing home workspace from `orca worktree ps`. A recorded native task never falls back to terminal mode on relaunch or restart: it relaunches in a fresh terminal with `--task`/`--retry-of`. Meta records the durable native identities, and routing (`fm-backend`, `fm-peek`, `fm-send`, `fm-crew-state`, `fm-control`, `fm-classify-lib`) goes through `dispatch:<id>`. It uses transcript-first reads, mailbox doorbells with a terminal fallback, `worker-stop`/`worker-abandon`/`worker-release` control, and it refuses on any identity mismatch.
- Teardown and recovery settle and release the exact Dispatch before closing the launched terminal. A new `cleanup_recovery=orca` record, plus `orca_retry_dispatch_id` for a partial retry, covers attaches or relaunches that cannot settle. The persistent Secondmate home is kept, the Secondmate restart gate and liveness sweep skip recovery records, and the Orca docs, skill, and backend tests are updated to match.

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The fix round correctly implements the authorized relaunch retry sidecar with no new defect I could substantiate, but the overall branch is a large shell-level lifecycle and recovery change whose retry and abandon semantics are proven only against a fake Orca, so follow-up validation against real Orca 1.4.x is advisable.

## Testing

I ran the three targeted regression suites for this change with the live flag set: tests/fm-backend-orca.test.sh, tests/fm-control.test.sh and tests/fm-secondmate-restart.test.sh. All passed; they cover the fake-Orca lifecycle, the recovery records and partial receipts. I then set up a throwaway Orca lab: a scratch repo already registered in Orca, a coordinator worktree and terminal, and isolated Firstmate state/data/config under /tmp. In it I ran the real Firstmate CLIs against the running Orca app. The capability gate accepted native mode only inside a real Orca terminal; a missing or stale handle fell back, and Pi was excluded. A persistent Secondmate refused outside Orca and refused a raw launch, with no mutation. A raw-launch scout asking for supervised mode fell back to the terminal adapter on a real Orca worktree and terminal, and was peeked and torn down, which released the worktree. Forged native records and `cleanup_recovery=orca` records were refused by peek, crew-state, send and teardown, and every record was kept. A native spawn run inside the Orca coordinator hit a real `agent_unconfigured` refusal; spawn closed the launched terminal, released the worktree, wrote no record, and left no Dispatch in the Run. The one remaining gap is a successful attach, which needs a real logged-in agent. The lab was torn down afterwards. There is no UI change, so there are no screenshots; the evidence is CLI transcripts.

The launched terminal `$T` keeps its harness running outside task control, which is the case the new 'close the launched terminal' contract is meant to prevent. The terminal that does get closed was never verified as Firstmate's; it could be any handle Orca put in the receipt, including another task's terminal or the coordinator's. Now that spawn passes `--terminal "$T"`, `$T` is authoritative. Fix: drop the ORCA_TERMINAL assignment from the receipt at line 5162 (or assign it only after the equality check passes).

title: feat(bin): tell every worker brief to load the home's standing skills
body:
## Intent

Dispatch the four ready items. I want all firstmate workers, including you, to start using that Kun skill. It's from the same guy who developed Firstmate and I trust his judgement.

Context: the captain wants every worker brief to tell the worker to load a standing skill (today: kun) before starting. Firstmate currently has no way to say that except hand-adding a line to each brief's Firstmate spec. The captain's fork is lockhartheavyindustries/firstmate; the change is meant as an upstream contribution to kunchenguid/firstmate, like the open PR 5328.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-brief.sh` reads an optional gitignored `config/standing-skills` (one bare skill name per line, blank lines and `#` comments ignored) and, when it names at least one skill, appends a single "Standing skills" paragraph to the end of the `# Setup` section of ship and scout briefs and the `# Operating model` section of secondmate charters, telling the worker to load each skill with its harness's own skill command (`/<name>`, or `$<name>` on Codex) and follow it within the brief's boundaries. An absent or skill-free list leaves every scaffold byte-identical; an unreadable path or a name outside `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]` (starting alphanumeric) fails closed before anything is written.
- `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh` adds `standing-skills` to the primary-authoritative inheritable config set, so secondmate homes and their own crewmates load the same skills as the primary.
- `AGENTS.md` and `docs/configuration.md` document the new file, and `tests/fm-brief.test.sh` plus `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` cover rendering in all three scaffold kinds, the no-op cases, the fail-closed cases, and inheritance propagation.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The feature is additive, fails closed on bad input, leaves briefs byte-identical when unconfigured, and is covered by behavioral tests on the generated brief, but the rendered paragraph hardcodes a per-harness invocation list that already contradicts the Pi adapter reference, which is a wording fix safe to address as a follow-up.

## Testing

Exercised the standing-skills feature end to end against the real scripts: scaffolded ship, scout, and secondmate briefs with and without config/standing-skills in throwaway FM_HOME directories, checked placement and byte-identity, hammered the list parser with invalid names and unusable paths, pushed the list into a secondmate home through fm-config-push.sh and scaffolded a brief there, and confirmed the base commit lacks the paragraph. tests/fm-brief.test.sh and tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh both exited 0 (the latter with all 50 tests ok, including the inheritance tests covering standing-skills); these are unit suite runs, not live product drives, so their scenarios are marked untested and the logs are attached as supporting artifacts only. The config-push reread nudge was not exercised because the product refuses to drive the fleet under the no-mistakes gate guard; that send is unrelated to this change. Overall result: go, based on the nine live scenarios that passed.

title: feat(bin): defer spawns beyond a project's declared machine capacity
body:
## Intent

Implement ready-for-pr issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/4237: workers beyond a project's resource capacity should not be launched only to spend turns retrying admission.

Substance of issue #4237 ("Workers beyond a project resource's capacity are run anyway and spend turns retrying admission"):
On one machine, a private project's heavy test suite could serve at most two workers at a time, and its local editor stack one.
Each worker enforced that limit itself by taking a slot before running the suite, under a local convention outside Firstmate's code.
Firstmate had four workers in flight on the project, and at times up to three of their no-mistakes runs were in the Test step, which needs the same resources.
Firstmate ran all four at the same time, as AGENTS.md section 7 directs ("dispatch isolated work immediately with no concurrency cap").
The workers that found both slots taken kept retrying admission, one model turn per attempt: one worker recorded 60 admission attempts and 129 turns (21.9M tokens) over about two and a quarter hours, and across about two days of the fleet's work 197 wait-only turns (32.6M tokens) were admission retries for that suite, 17% of all wait-only worker tokens.
Section 7 names "shared mutable external state" as a reason to serialize, but a project has no way to tell Firstmate that such a resource exists or how many workers it admits, and nothing at dispatch consults one, so the limit is discovered by the worker at the moment it needs the resource, after it has been dispatched and has built its context.
Expected: when a project has a resource that only N workers can use at once, Firstmate does not keep more than N workers spending turns in the phase that needs it; a worker that cannot get the resource is not left paying full-context turns to find that out.
Consequence today: each surplus worker pays one full-context turn per retry (130K to 250K tokens each) and makes no progress, and the cost grows with every worker dispatched past the limit.
Related issues: #4228 covers the turns a worker spends while it waits on a gate; this issue is about running more workers than a limited resource can admit in the first place. #3625 asks for fan-out and cost ceilings on dispatcher expansion and has no notion of a project resource with a fixed capacity. #978 designs admission for no-mistakes validation runs, not for a worker's own test or editor phase.

## What Changed

- Added an optional local `config/project-capacity` file, read from the machine's root Firstmate home, with one line per project: `<project-name> <capacity>`. The new `bin/fm-project-capacity-lib.sh` owns the file format and decides which tasks hold a place. A non-secondmate task counts against the project, in any local home and in any clone of the same origin, until its ready PR is recorded with `pr=` or it is cleaned up.
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` counts the held places for a fresh ship or scout while holding the shared project lock. It now takes that lock on Orca too whenever a capacity is declared. When every place is held, the spawn prints one `deferred:` line naming the holders and exits 75. This happens before any brief, endpoint, worktree, record, or backlog move is created, so the item stays queued. Batch dispatch reports such a pair as `batch: DEFERRED`. If the declaration or the task records can't be read, the spawn refuses with exit 1. Relaunches and secondmates are never counted.
- Moved the walk over local Firstmate homes out of `bin/fm-teardown.sh` into a shared `fm_local_firstmate_state_dirs` in `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh`, so teardown and capacity counting use the same walk. Also documented the feature in `AGENTS.md` sections 7 and 10 and in the new "Project capacity" section of `docs/configuration.md`. Added `tests/fm-project-capacity.test.sh` to the backend-dispatch test family.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix round only changed documentation, and the new text in the library header and in docs/configuration.md matches the code: the declaration is looked up by basename "$PROJ_ABS", while holders are counted by the project lock path, which is keyed by origin. That is exactly the documentation-only remedy the user asked for. The original admission logic stays bounded and fails closed: the count runs under the project lock, deferral exits before anything is created, and the lock is released on every exit path.

## Testing

I ran the focused capacity test suite (all 11 cases pass), then drove six scenarios live in a throwaway fm-lab Herdr session, with real worker panes, real treehouse worktrees and a real markdown backlog. All six passed. The deferred spawn left no task record, no Herdr pane and no rendered launch brief, and its backlog item stayed queued. Recording a PR with fm-pr-check.sh freed exactly one place, and so did a teardown. A malformed declaration refused the spawn with exit 1, and a batch at capacity reported DEFERRED for each item and exited 75. My first driver attempt had two setup mistakes of its own: teardown needed the gate bypass, and the batch syntax was wrong. I fixed both and re-ran the whole thing. The lab and the treehouse pools I created were removed afterwards. I did not drive two scenarios live: concurrent spawns racing for the last place, and counting across several homes. Only the focused suite covers them, so they are marked untested. This is a CLI change with no visual UI, so the evidence is a CLI transcript.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Live driver: real bin/fm-spawn.sh / fm-pr-check.sh / fm-teardown.sh against a
# guarded fm-lab-* Herdr session and real treehouse, with a throwaway FM_HOME.
set -u
ROOT=${1:?worktree}
EVID=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
LAB="$ROOT/bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh"
TMP=$(mktemp -d /tmp/fm-cap-live.XXXXXX)
ORIG_PATH=$PATH
REAL_HERDR=$(command -v herdr)
FAKEBIN="$TMP/bin"; mkdir -p "$FAKEBIN"
export LAB ORIG_PATH REAL_HERDR
SESSION=$("$LAB" name capacity)

unset HERDR_PANE_ID HERDR_PANE HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID HERDR_TAB_ID 2>/dev/null || :

done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
args=("$@"); n=${#args[@]}
if [ "$n" -ge 2 ] && [ "${args[$((n-2))]}" = --session ] && [ "${args[$((n-1))]}" = "$HERDR_LAB_SESSION" ]; then
  unset "args[$((n-1))]" "args[$((n-2))]"
fi
set -- "${args[@]}"
if [ "${1:-}" = --version ]; then exec env PATH="$ORIG_PATH" "$REAL_HERDR" "$@" --session "$HERDR_LAB_SESSION"; fi
exec env PATH="$ORIG_PATH" "$LAB" run "$HERDR_LAB_SESSION" "$@"
SH

#!/usr/bin/env bash
case "$*" in *isDraft*) echo '{"isDraft":false}';; *) exit 1;; esac

export PATH="$FAKEBIN:$PATH"

LAB_UP=0
WTS=()
cleanup() {
  for wt in "${WTS[@]}"; do [ -d "$wt" ] && treehouse return --force "$wt" >/dev/null 2>&1; done
  [ "$LAB_UP" = 1 ] && PATH="$ORIG_PATH" "$LAB" teardown "$SESSION" && echo "lab $SESSION torn down"

trap cleanup EXIT

PATH="$ORIG_PATH" "$LAB" provision "$SESSION" || { echo "provision failed"; exit 1; }
LAB_UP=1
echo "== lab session: $SESSION"

touch "$HOME_DIR/state/.last-watcher-beat"
printf 'codex\n' > "$HOME_DIR/config/crew-harness"
printf '%s\n' '# Backlog' '' '## In flight' '' '## Queued' '' '## Done' > "$HOME_DIR/data/backlog.md"
printf 'backend = "markdown"\n\n[markdown]\npath = "data/backlog.md"\n' > "$HOME_DIR/.tasks.toml"

git clone -q --bare "$PROJ" "$PROJ.origin.git"; git -C "$PROJ" remote add origin "file://$PROJ.origin.git"

brief() { mkdir -p "$HOME_DIR/data/$1"; printf '# Task\n## Captain'"'"'s intent\nRun the heavy suite for %s.\n\n## Firstmate spec\nlive capacity.\n\n# Definition of done\nDelivery contract: mode=no-mistakes\n' "$1" > "$HOME_DIR/data/$1/brief.md"; tasks-axi add "$1" "item for $1" --kind ship --file "$HOME_DIR/data/backlog.md" >/dev/null; }

printf '# heavy suite serves two workers\nheavy-suite 2\n' > "$HOME_DIR/config/project-capacity"
before=$(panes)
spawn cap-d >"$TMP/out" 2>"$TMP/err"; rc=$?

report cap-d

report cap-e

brief cap-f
spawn cap-f >/dev/null 2>"$TMP/err"; rc=$?; echo "   spawn cap-f exit=$rc"; sed 's/^/   stderr| /' "$TMP/err"
report cap-f

title: fix(bin): arm the busy contract on secondmate launches
body:
## Intent

Implement ready-for-pr issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/4268: a tmux-backed second mate's active-turn gate cannot observe a busy verdict because second-mate launches do not arm the busy contract.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now arms the semantic busy contract for `--secondmate` launches too, not only ordinary tasks. This covers claude, opencode, pi, pi-signed, and omp. As a result, the parent home's active-turn gate for a tmux-backed second mate can now return a busy verdict. Pi secondmates load the parent's `state/<id>.pi-ext.ts` next to their two primary extensions. omp secondmates now pass `-e state/<id>.omp-ext.ts`. The secondmate's hooks update the busy record but never touch the parent's `turn-ended` marker. Grok and kimi keep their parent turn-end wiring on the ordinary-task path only. `exclude_path` now resolves a relative `--git-path` result against the worktree.
- A Claude secondmate gets no `Stop` busy hook. Instead, `fm-spawn.sh` writes a `.fm-busy-stop` pointer into the mate's home. `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh --claude` reads that pointer from an EXIT trap and becomes the only Stop writer. It records `idle` when it allows the Stop, and `busy` (`stop-blocked`) when its exit 2 blocks the Stop into a continuation. A home whose guard is older than `.fm-busy-stop` keeps the ordinary `Stop` idle hook, without the parent turn-ended touch.
- Tests and docs: `tests/fm-busy-adapter-wiring.test.sh` has new coverage for the secondmate wiring. A new opt-in live test, `tests/fm-secondmate-busy-contract-live-e2e.test.sh`, is registered in `fm-test-run.sh`, and `tests/fm-wake-queue.test.sh` was adjusted. Docs were updated in the claude/omp/pi harness references, `docs/turnend-guard.md`, and `docs/verification/` (runtime-backends and supervision).

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The change arms the busy contract for secondmate launches and makes the Claude secondmate's Stop guard the only Stop-state writer; the traced paths look correct, but this is shared supervision state across parent and child homes and depends on Claude's parallel Stop hooks and asyncRewake behavior, so it deserves the dedicated test and live-e2e steps.

## Testing

I ran the change's own live tmux guard and its focused wiring regression, and both pass. I then drove three live labs, each spawning a real Claude secondmate through `fm-spawn.sh --secondmate` on a private tmux socket and running two real model turns. On this change, the parent gate reads busy during each turn (including the full 20-second Bash call) and idle after it, and the parent's turn-ended marker is never touched. When the home's Stop guard is the older version, the ordinary Stop hook is kept and the record still closes to idle. On the base commit the gate reads `unknown missing` throughout, which reproduces issue #4268. Evidence is the per-second verdict logs and pane captures in the evidence directory; there is no UI surface beyond terminal panes, and those were captured as text. Opencode, pi, and omp real model turns were not run, because they would spend the operator's provider credits (omp is not installed). The live guard does prove those harnesses get the busy record at spawn and that their real processes start with the wiring in place. One side effect outside the worktree: fm-spawn's normal Claude trust pre-registration left 3 entries for deleted /tmp lab paths in `~/.claude.json`. I did not remove them, because other Claude sessions write that file concurrently. The lab tmux servers, sockets, and temp homes were all torn down.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 7 of 8 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A real tmux-backed Claude secondmate running a turn is seen as busy by the parent's active-turn gate, then idle after Stop | ✅ pass | live | claude-current.log: busy fm-spawn -> busy claude-hook (user-prompt-submit) -> idle claude-hook (stop) for the launch brief; the typed `sleep 20` turn read busy claude-hook for about 23s, then idle cla… |
| The Claude secondmate's home Stop guard is its only Stop writer (no Stop hook in settings.local.json; .fm-busy-stop points at the parent record) | ✅ pass | live | claude-current.log: settings.local.json events [SessionEnd,StopFailure,UserPromptSubmit]; .fm-busy-stop names the parent state/id/gen; the idle event=stop records came from the guard |
| Secondmate turns never touch the parent's turn-ended marker | ✅ pass | live | claude-current.log and claude-oldguard.log: turn-ended=absent through both turns; live-guard.txt shows the same for opencode/pi/grok |
| Adversarial: a home whose Stop guard predates .fm-busy-stop still closes each turn to idle through the kept Stop idle hook | ✅ pass | live | claude-oldguard.log: .fm-busy-stop ABSENT, Stop hook present, busy during the sleep 20 turn then idle claude-hook event=stop |
| Reproduce issue #4268 on the base commit: the gate cannot see a busy verdict for a working tmux Claude secondmate | ✅ pass | live | claude-base-before-fix.log: no busy-gen, verdict 'unknown missing' throughout while the pane shows `Bash(sleep 20) Running…` |
| opencode and pi tmux secondmate spawns get the busy record, and the real process starts beside the wiring | ✅ pass | live | live-guard.txt: opencode 1.18.32 and pi 0.86.1 armed, real process stayed up, no parent turn-ended |
| grok and codex secondmates stay unarmed and install no parent turn-end wiring | ✅ pass | live | live-guard.txt: grok 1.0.41 stays unarmed with no parent turn-end token (codex is not installed; its case is covered only in the fm-busy-adapter-wiring regression) |
| opencode / pi / omp secondmate real model turns flip the parent gate busy then idle | ⏸️ untested | no | A real turn spends the operator's OpenCode Zen / pi provider credits, which this test step was not authorized to use, and omp is not installed on this host. To run it, approve provider spend and rerun… |

title: fix(bin): wake on pull request movement after arming its monitor
body:
## Intent

Pursue the ready-for-pr issues that map to fork differences.
Upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/3239 is open and marked ready-for-pr.
It asks Firstmate's supported pull-request monitor to wake on actionable review activity, comments, reviewer requests, head changes, and leaving draft instead of reporting monitoring armed while observing only merge state.
The historical fork change is commit 83fd332b from fork PR 37, but its bytes are untrusted after a bad sync and upstream has moved since triage.

## What Changed

- `fm-contributions.sh` now records a PR's requested reviewers and teams (teams as `team:<slug>`) in each observation. A new `movement` function in `fm-contributions.jq` compares each observation with the previous one and queues a pending signal, which wakes the fleet, when the head changes, the PR leaves draft, or a new reviewer is requested. A first observation, or one saved before review requests were recorded, only sets the baseline and never counts as movement. Each signal's token includes the observation time, so the same transition happening again gets a new token.
- `review_requests` is added to the record validation as an optional field. The fleet-facing reason for pending signals changes from "incoming maintainer signal needs triage" to "incoming forge signal needs triage".
- The comments in `fm-contributions.sh` and `fm-pr-check.sh`, `docs/scripts.md`, and the bearings skill now describe pull-request movement as a wake source. They also say that `fm-pr-check.sh` registers the contribution observer. `tests/fm-contributions.test.sh` gains coverage for the movement signals, and two watcher test checkpoints were adjusted to fix timing: one now waits for its completed contributions poll, and one has a 30s bound.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change adds narrowly scoped movement detection: a head change, leaving draft, and a newly requested reviewer or team. A first observation, or one stored before review requests were recorded, counts as the baseline rather than movement. Tokens include the head and the observation time, so a repeated transition gets a new token. On a failed read the previous observation is kept, so movement is still detected on the next good read. The tests run the real poll, pending and watcher paths. The only issue left is an older watcher race, recorded as a separate follow-up.

## Testing

I drove the real contributions observer, PR registration and watcher checkpoint against live GitHub PRs through the authenticated gh CLI, in a throwaway FM_HOME. To create each movement, I set the stored previous observation (persisted local state) so it differed from what GitHub currently reports; the current read was always real. Head change, leaving draft and a new reviewer each woke exactly once and did not re-ring. First observation, a stored record without review requests, and converting to draft stayed silent. The live watcher surfaced the head move once and otherwise expired quietly. The same drive on the base commit produced zero wakes. The targeted test file covers team requests through its fake forge, and its movement and baseline tests passed. The first full-file run failed three watcher tests with empty stderr, including the pre-existing `test_watcher_keeps_diagnostics_separate_from_contribution_wakes`, which this branch does not change. That run exceeded the tool's 600-second limit and was moved to the background mid-run, and host load was about 60. On the same host, an instrumented full rerun passed every test, and the watcher tests passed 3 of 3 on their own, so the failures look environmental rather than caused by this change. This is a CLI and background-watcher change with no rendered UI, so the evidence is CLI transcripts, not screenshots.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 6 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Replaced PR head wakes once: a new head gives exactly one pending 'head' signal and one durable wake, and a re-poll adds nothing | ✅ pass | live | live-movement-branch.log (scenario: head) vs live-movement-base.log (no wake on base) |
| PR leaving draft wakes once with 'pull request left draft' | ✅ pass | live | live-movement-branch.log (scenario: ready) |
| Adversarial: converting a PR to draft does not wake | ✅ pass | live | live-convert-to-draft.log (real draft PR cli/cli#14355, prior non-draft: 0 pending, 0 wakes) |
| Newly requested reviewer wakes once with body 'review requested from <login>' | ✅ pass | live | live-movement-branch.log (scenario: reviewer: 'review requested from niik', 1 wake, re-poll adds none) |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Live drive: real fm-contributions.sh + fm-pr-check.sh + registered custom check,
# real authenticated gh against a real public GitHub PR, isolated throwaway FM_HOME.
# The "previous observation" is persisted local state that we set to model what
# the forge looked like at the last poll; the current forge read is real.
set -u
ROOT=${ROOT:?}
URL=${URL:?}
T=$(mktemp -d /tmp/fm-live-movement.XXXXXX)
home=$T/home
mkdir -p "$home/data/delivery" "$home/state" "$home/config" "$home/projects" "$home/root/bin" "$home/wt" "$home/fakebin"
printf '# Backlog\n\n## Queued\n' > "$home/data/backlog.md"
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n' > "$home/fakebin/tmux"; chmod +x "$home/fakebin/tmux"
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > "$home/root/bin/fm-guard.sh"; chmod +x "$home/root/bin/fm-guard.sh"
printf 'worktree=%s/wt\nkind=ship\n' "$home" > "$home/state/delivery.meta"; chmod 600 "$home/state/delivery.meta"
printf -- '- [ ] delivery - Live contribution %s (repo: sample) (kind: ship)\n' "$URL" >> "$home/data/backlog.md"
H() { PATH="$home/fakebin:$PATH" FM_HOME="$home" FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$home/root" FM_STATE_OVERRIDE="$home/state" \
  FM_DATA_OVERRIDE="$home/data" FM_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="$home/config" "$@"; }
check() { local c; for c in "$home/state/"*.check.sh; do [ -f "$c" ] || continue; echo "+ run registered check $(basename "$c")"; H bash "$c"; echo "  (rc=$?)"; done; }
wakes() { [ -f "$home/state/.wake-queue" ] && awk -F '\t' 'NF>=5 && $3=="check"{c++} END{print c+0}' "$home/state/.wake-queue" || echo 0; }
rec() { jq -c '.records[0] | {head:.observation.head,draft:.observation.draft,review_requests:.observation.review_requests,pending:[.pending[]|{type,body}]}' "$home/data/delivery/contributions.json"; }
seed() { jq "$1" "$home/data/delivery/contributions.json" > "$T/x" && mv "$T/x" "$home/data/delivery/contributions.json"; echo "+ seed prior observation: $1"; }
echo "=== PR: $URL"
echo "+ fm-pr-check.sh delivery $URL"; H "$ROOT/bin/fm-pr-check.sh" delivery "$URL"; echo "  (rc=$?)"
[ -f "$home/state/contributions.check.sh" ] || { echo "+ fm-contributions.sh arm (backlog-linked ownership)"; H "$ROOT/bin/fm-contributions.sh" arm; echo "  (rc=$?)"; }
echo "--- step 1: first observation (baseline)"
check; echo "record: $(rec)"; echo "durable wakes: $(wakes)"
echo "--- step 2: unchanged re-poll"
check; echo "record: $(rec)"; echo "durable wakes: $(wakes)"
for s in "$@"; do
  echo "--- scenario: $s"
  case "$s" in
    head) seed '.records[0].observation.head = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000001"' ;;
    ready) seed '.records[0].observation.draft = true' ;;
    reviewer) seed '.records[0].observation.review_requests = []' ;;
    todraft) seed '.records[0].observation.draft = false' ;;
    legacy) seed '.records[0].observation |= del(.review_requests)' ;;
  esac
  check; echo "record: $(rec)"; echo "durable wakes: $(wakes)"
  echo "+ fm-contributions.sh pending"; H "$ROOT/bin/fm-contributions.sh" pending | jq -c '[.[]|{type,body,source}]'
  echo "--- re-poll unchanged after $s"
  check; echo "record: $(rec)"; echo "durable wakes: $(wakes)"
  for tok in $(H "$ROOT/bin/fm-contributions.sh" pending | jq -r '.[].token'); do
    echo "+ ack $tok"; H "$ROOT/bin/fm-contributions.sh" ack delivery "$URL" "$tok"; done
done
echo "--- wake queue"; cut -f1-5 "$home/state/.wake-queue" 2>/dev/null
rm -rf "$T"

title: feat(bin): detect a Lavish review board that was never armed
body:
## What breaks today

A worker opens a Lavish review board, posts its URL in a status line, and never arms it.

The board stays open. The reviewer annotates it. The browser tells them "Your agent is not listening", and every comment they leave sits queued on the server.

Nothing errors. No status line is written. No wake fires. The failure is completely invisible to firstmate, so the only way it has ever surfaced is the reviewer saying so in chat, after the fact, having left feedback nobody read.

Observed on this machine on 2026-09-22, and more than once before that.

## Does #5099 already fix this?

No, but it changed the shape of the right fix, so this branch was rebuilt on top of it rather than rebased through it.

**What #5099 does cover.** Once a board *is* armed, the process-event runner owns its listener. It captures each round, delivers it to the owning worker's steering inbox, redelivers an open round on every reconcile, restarts a source whose owner is gone, and refuses to retire a board with an unacknowledged round. An armed board is attended in all three states `bin/fm-procevent.sh list` reports: `listening`, `round-open`, and `dead`.

**What it does not cover.** None of that machinery exists until the arm happens. A board that was never armed has no registration to reconcile, no owner to redeliver to, and no claim to restart. #5099 rewrote the instruction telling workers to arm, and an instruction is not enforcement. The gap it leaves is exactly the original defect.

**Where it changed this patch.** The first version of this detector decided attendance by looking for a `lavish-axi poll` process. Under #5099 that is now actively wrong: an armed board sitting in `round-open` has no poll process by design, so the old check would have false-positived on the intended path. Attendance here is a registration, read through `bin/fm-procevent.sh list`, never a process and never the vendor's own `listener` column (see below).

## What this adds

**`bin/fm-lavish-board-guard.sh`** - a watcher-side scan. Its header owns the full contract. Four gates, all of which must hold:

1. A board URL appears anywhere in a task's `state/<id>.status` log. Which mention it is does not matter; whether the board still needs attending is decided by gates 2 and 3.
2. The task is live, via `bin/fm-backend.sh`'s cheap read-only `fm_backend_target_exists`.
3. The Lavish server still lists that URL as `open`, resolved to its artifact file.
4. This home holds no registered process-event source for that artifact, and has not for longer than a grace period (default 300s, `FM_LAVISH_BOARD_GRACE_SECS`, bounded 60..3600).

It then publishes **one** ordinary durable `check` wake per board, deduplicated by its own `state/.lavish-board-unarmed-<hash>` record, which also carries the grace clock and is removed the moment the board is armed, closes, or its task goes away, so a later lapse rings again.

It never arms, polls, opens, resumes, or ends a board. The hosting task owns its listener, so the only correct response to the wake is to steer that worker to arm. Detection only.

**Deliberately out of scope:** an armed board whose owning task later dies, leaving a live listener writing into a dead worker's inbox. Gate 2 skips it, because that is the existing recovery path's business.

**`bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh sessions`** - a new read-only command, the URL-to-artifact-file resolution the scan needs. Bare `lavish-axi` publishes a `sessions[N]{file,status,url,pending_prompts,...}` table; this parses it, applies `config/lavish-axi-host` exactly as the poll does, and keeps every `lavish-axi` invocation inside the adapter that already owns Lavish specifics. It asserts the first four fields in order and **refuses with a diagnostic** when that prefix changes, rather than guessing at a new shape. Columns appended after those four are absorbed.

That absorption is not hypothetical: lavish-axi 0.1.77 appended a `listener` column mid-development, and the strict version refused exactly as intended. **That column is not read as a verdict**, because on 2026-09-22 it reported `none` for a board with a live `lavish-axi poll` attached. The dated evidence is in `docs/verification/process-event-sources.md`.

**`bin/fm-brief.sh`** - the crew instruction now says to arm *before* writing any status line about the board, and names the consequence of not doing so.

## Cost

A home whose status logs name no board never invokes `lavish-axi` and never lists sources: it pays one directory read per call. The watcher runs the scan on its own 60s interval (`FM_LAVISH_BOARD_INTERVAL`) rather than every 15-second cycle, and the grace period is wall-clock from the first observation, so the slower cadence cannot delay a report.

## Tests

- `tests/fm-lavish-board-guard.test.sh` - portable, CI-safe, no Lavish server. Nine cases: no board; an armed board stays silent; an unarmed board past grace reports once; the same board next cycle does not repeat; a dead task never reports; a board named only in a line the log has moved past still reports, while closed and unlisted boards are skipped; arming clears the record and a later lapse rings again; an unreadable session listing and an unreadable source listing both refuse rather than guess; and `sessions` absorbs an appended column while refusing a reordered one. Attendance is proved with a **real** `bin/fm-procevent.sh register`, not a mocked listing.
- `tests/fm-lavish-board-guard-live-e2e.test.sh` - live drift guard in the `live-harness-optin` family, for the one surface a stub cannot prove: the vendor-emitted session listing. It is **opt-in rather than default-on** because `lavish-axi <html-file>` raises a real review window and 0.1.77 publishes no documented way to suppress it. It creates its own scratch session and ends it on every exit path, including failure.

## Verification run locally

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` clean (ShellCheck 0.11.0, actionlint 1.7.12).
- `fm-lavish-board-guard`, `fm-brief`, `fm-procevent` (123 assertions), and `fm-watch-triage` all pass.
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` reports only pre-existing unclassified local skills, unchanged by this branch.
- End to end against the real Lavish server: an open board this home never armed rang once with its task, URL, and file, and did not ring again; a real armed board stayed silent.

## CI

Raised through `no-mistakes` per `CONTRIBUTING.md`; the run is green apart from one override, noted here rather than left for you to find.

Both checks on this PR report `action_required` with zero jobs: GitHub holds workflow runs from a fork until a maintainer approves them, so neither **CI** nor **Require no-mistakes** has executed against this code. Nothing failed, because nothing ran. Approving the workflow run should be enough.

What did run locally against this exact head (`a2eed8a`), with the pinned toolchain:

- `bin/fm-lint.sh` exit 0, full ShellCheck extended analysis, 3 workflow files valid.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --check-coverage` exit 0, 222 tests partitioned, none missing or duplicated.
- `bin/fm-test-run.sh --changed --base d92cea0`: zero failures.
- `tests/fm-lavish-board-guard.test.sh`, `tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh`, `tests/fm-brief.test.sh`, `tests/fm-procevent.test.sh` all exit 0.
- `bin/fm-doc-audience-check.sh` exit 0, 102 surfaces, 457 local links.

The pipeline's own review caught two things the first version got wrong, both fixed in `64f4194`:

- Gate 1 originally skipped a board URL whose only mention was a terminal status line the log had moved past. That hid the exact defect: a `needs-decision` line naming the board, followed by any later line, went unreported while the task was live and the board still open. Gate 1 is now a plain "named anywhere in the log", and gates 2 and 3 do the narrowing.
- `FM_LAVISH_BOARD_INTERVAL` was read without the numeric guard its sibling `FM_HOME_SUMMARY_INTERVAL` gets, so a non-numeric value would have made the scan silently vanish every cycle. It is now normalized and documented.

title: fix(bin): move codex max-effort validation key from gpt-5.6-luna to gpt-6-luna
body:
## Intent

Retire the gpt-5.6 engine references from firstmate's own guidance and validation: move the codex max-effort validation key from gpt-5.6-luna to gpt-6-luna. The captain's words: "fyi gpt 5.6 luna and sol are retiring, so replace them with gpt 6 luna and gpt 6 sol in your guidance, may need to udpate codex cli across our hosts". Firstmate's local verification (re-check it yourself before changing anything): installed codex-cli 0.155.1 catalog at ~/.codex/models_cache.json lists gpt-6-luna, gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-astra, and the gpt-6-luna entry advertises the max reasoning level - the whole key exists because a model's own catalog must support max, so the catalog is the precondition, not a formality. Retiring-model references live in: bin/fm-spawn.sh (around lines 2357-2362, the codex max-effort gate), bin/fm-bootstrap.sh (around line 1140), bin/fm-dispatch-resolve.sh (around line 136), docs/configuration.md (around line 500), and .agents/skills/harness-adapters/references/harness/codex.md (the effort-flag row). Dated verification captures in docs/verification/ and historical PR bodies or receipts naming gpt-5.6 are records of what actually ran - never rewrite them.

title: fix(bin): refuse a Herdr Claude submit that would send only a message tail
body:
## Intent Fixes #3473 Herdr and Claude typed delivery can report success while submitting only the tail of a long message. That affects away-mode digests and ordinary fm-send steers alike, so the fix has to cover every Claude-on-Herdr delivery, not only the digest path. ## What Changed - The Herdr backend's typed submit (`fm_backend_herdr_send_text_submit` in `bin/backends/herdr.sh`) now checks the composer before pressing Enter when the pane's native identity is Claude. This covers away-mode digests and ordinary `fm-send` steers alike. The adapter types only into an empty composer. It sends Enter only when the composer shows the full payload (ignoring whitespace and the U+2063 operational mark), or shows only Claude `[Pasted text #N]` placeholders with nothing else. If the composer shows a shorter suffix, a placeholder followed by leftover literal text, or can't be read, Enter is not sent. The adapter then presses Ctrl+U until the composer reads empty and reports `send-failed`, or reports `unknown` if it can't confirm the composer is empty. Other harnesses keep the existing type-then-Enter path. - `docs/herdr-backend.md` and `docs/architecture.md` describe the Claude pre-Enter check, the Ctrl+U clear, and the `send-failed`/`unknown` verdicts. - `tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh` adds unit coverage for the check and the clear. The opt-in live e2e (`tests/fm-herdr-submit-confirm-live-e2e.test.sh`) now accepts Claude's folder-trust prompt and adds a check that a U+2063 away-supervisor payload is submitted and answered. Separately, `tests/fm-procevent.test.sh` raises one fixture's launch floor from 3 to 15 seconds to fix a timing race seen in CI. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The pre-Enter proof applies only to panes that native identity reports as Claude, follows the recorded user decisions (clear to a verified-empty composer before returning send-failed, return unknown otherwise, ignore U+2063, accept placeholder-only read-backs, leave other harnesses unchanged), covers both the digest path and the fm-send path through the shared send_text_submit, and is tested through the executable interface; the procevent change only lengthens a test fixture's launch floor to remove a timing race. ## Testing I ran the branch's existing live Herdr submit-confirm e2e, which passed for both the ASCII steer and the U+2063 away-supervisor payload. I also wrote a 7-scenario live script and ran it against real Claude Code in a throwaway fm-lab Herdr session, first on this branch and then on the base commit for comparison. On this branch all 7 scenarios passed. In the three long-message scenarios, the message starts with a code and Claude must reply with that code followed by a second code from the end, so a reply containing both proves Claude received the start of the message. On the base commit, S4 and S5 show the old unsafe behavior. S1-S3 also failed on base, but not from truncation: there, Claude received the whole message and declined to act on text it read as pasted content. The natural tail-only truncation from the issue did not reproduce on this host, so S5 creates it by wrapping send_literal so it types only the last 400 characters. Every lab session was torn down, and the worktree is clean. There is no UI change, so there are no screenshots; the saved pane screens are the visual record. - Live validation: ✅ go - 9 of 10 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Short fm-send style steer to Claude on Herdr returns empty and Claude replies (existing live e2e) | ✅ pass | live | live-e2e-submit-confirm.log (ok line 1) | | Short U+2063 away-supervisor digest to Claude is accepted even though the read-back drops the mark, and Claude replies (existing live e2e) | ✅ pass | live | live-e2e-submit-confirm.log (ok line 2) | | S1: a 2,634-char single-line steer arrives whole: verdict empty, and Claude's reply combines the code from the start with the code from the end | ✅ pass | live | long-delivery-scenarios.log S1, screen-S1.txt | | S2: a 1,847-char multi-line steer arrives whole (verdict empty, reply uses the code from the start) | ✅ pass | live | long-delivery-scenarios.log S2, screen-S2.txt | | S3: a 2,107-char away-mode digest with the U+2063 prefix arrives whole (verdict empty, reply uses the code from the start) | ✅ pass | live | long-delivery-scenarios.log S3, screen-S3.txt | | S4 (adversarial): the composer already holds an operator draft, so the send returns send-failed, the draft is left untouched, and the payload is never typed or submitted (base typed onto the draft and… | ✅ pass | live | screen-S4.txt vs baseline/screen-S4.txt | | S5 (adversarial, injected fault): only the last 400 characters are typed, so the proof refuses: verdict send-failed, composer verified empty, no turn submitted (base submitted the tail) | ✅ pass | live | long-delivery-scenarios.log S5, screen-S5.txt vs baseline/screen-S5.txt. The fault was injected by wrapping send_literal; the Herdr and Claude underneath were real | | S6: retrying the same long message after a refusal delivers it whole, with no leftover text prepended | ✅ pass | live | long-delivery-scenarios.log S6, screen-S6.txt | | S7: a non-Claude pane (plain shell) skips the proof and still types and runs a long command | ✅ pass | live | long-delivery-scenarios.log S7 (output file written with NONCLAUDE_OK_ prefix) | | Natural Herdr/Claude tail-only truncation from issue 3473 happens on its own and is refused | ⏸️ untested | no | The truncation did not happen naturally with herdr 0.9.1 and Claude Code 2.1.280 on this host, so the refusal path was covered by S5's injected tail-only send instead. Proving the natural case needs a… |

Evidence: Live scenario script Source: [Live scenario script](https://github.com/tiago-peixoto/firstmate/blob/4cc705c36b96222251ca5c9409245590fad76a41/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/upstream-3473-typed-delivery-truncation/long-delivery-scenarios.sh) ```text #!/usr/bin/env bash # Live scenarios for upstream issue 3473 (Herdr + Claude tail-only submit). # Drives real Claude Code in an isolated fm-lab-* Herdr session through # bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh, mirroring tests/fm-herdr-submit-confirm-live-e2e.test.sh. set -u ROOT=${ROOT:?} EVID=${EVID:?} LAB_HELPER=$ROOT/bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh . "$ROOT/tests/herdr-test-safety.sh" herdr_forget_inherited_pane ORIGINAL_PATH=$PATH SESSION=$("$LAB_HELPER" name issue3473-live) TMP_ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/fm-issue3473.XXXXXX) FAKEBIN="$TMP_ROOT/fakebin"; mkdir -p "$FAKEBIN" RESULTS=() cleanup() { trap - EXIT PATH="$ORIGINAL_PATH" "$LAB_HELPER" teardown "$SESSION" && echo "teardown ok: $SESSION" rm -rf "$TMP_ROOT" printf '%s\n' "${RESULTS[@]}" } trap cleanup EXIT cat > "$FAKEBIN/herdr" <&2; exit 97; } exec env PATH="$ORIGINAL_PATH" "$LAB_HELPER" run "$SESSION" "\${args[@]:0:\$((n-2))}" EOF chmod +x "$FAKEBIN/herdr" "$LAB_HELPER" provision "$SESSION" || { echo "provision failed"; exit 1; } export PATH="$FAKEBIN:$ORIGINAL_PATH" . "$ROOT/bin/backends/herdr.sh" . "$ROOT/bin/fm-operational-input.sh" lab() { env PATH="$ORIGINAL_PATH" "$LAB_HELPER" run "$SESSION" "$@"; } rec() { RESULTS+=("$1"); echo "$1"; } snap() { lab pane read "$PANE" --source recent --lines 400 > "$EVID/screen-$1.txt" 2>/dev/null || true; } WS_JSON=$(lab workspace create --cwd "$ROOT" --label fm-3473 --no-focus) || exit 1 PANE=$(printf '%s' "$WS_JSON" | jq -er '.result.root_pane.pane_id') || exit 1 TARGET="$SESSION:$PANE" lab pane run "$PANE" "CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false CLAUDE_CODE_SEND_FEEDBACK=0 claude --dangerously-skip-permissions --settings '{\"feedbackDrafts\":\"off\"}'" >/dev/null wait_idle() { local i=0 st while [ "$i" -lt 90 ]; do st=$(lab agent get "$PANE" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.result.agent.agent_status // empty') case "$st" in idle|done) return 0 ;; blocked) case "$(lab pane read "$PANE" --source visible 2>/dev/null)" in *'Yes, I trust this folder'*) lab pane send-keys "$PANE" down enter >/dev/null ;; esac ;; esac i=$((i + 1)); sleep 1 done return 1 } wait_reply() { # -> 0 when needle rendered local i=0 while [ "$i" -lt 90 ]; do lab pane read "$PANE" --source recent --lines 400 2>/dev/null | grep -Fq "$1" && return 0 i=$((i + 1)); sleep 1 done return 1 } filler() { # local out='' k=0 while [ ${#out} -lt "$1" ]; do out+="Filler sentence $k is context only and needs no action.$2"; k=$((k + 1)) done printf '%s' "$out" } wait_idle || { rec "FATAL: Claude never idle"; exit 1; } sleep 2 echo "claude=$(claude --version | head -1) herdr=$(herdr --version | head -1) session=$SESSION" # S1: long single-line steer (~2600 chars). Head carries a code the reply needs. A="HEADA$RANDOM"; B="TAILB$RANDOM" msg="The head code is $A. $(filler 2500 ' ')Now reply with only the head code immediately followed by $B with no space, nothing else." v=$(fm_backend_herdr_send_text_submit "$TARGET" "$msg" 3 0.4 0.6) if [ "$v" = empty ] && wait_reply "$A$B"; then rec "S1 PASS long single-line (${#msg} chars) verdict=$v reply=$A$B"; else rec "S1 FAIL verdict=$v"; fi snap S1; wait_idle; sleep 2 # S2: long multi-line steer (~1800 chars, newlines). A="HEADM$RANDOM"; B="TAILM$RANDOM" msg="The head code is $A."$'\n'"$(filler 1700 $'\n')"$'\n'"Reply with only the head code immediately followed by $B with no space, nothing else." v=$(fm_backend_herdr_send_text_submit "$TARGET" "$msg" 3 0.4 0.6) if [ "$v" = empty ] && wait_reply "$A$B"; then rec "S2 PASS long multi-line (${#msg} chars) verdict=$v reply=$A$B"; else rec "S2 FAIL verdict=$v"; fi snap S2; wait_idle; sleep 2 # S3: long away-mode operational digest (U+2063 prefix, ~2000 chars). A="HEADO$RANDOM"; B="TAILO$RANDOM" op= fm_operational_input_encode away-supervisor "Digest head code $A. $(filler 1900 ' ')Reply with only the head code immediately followed by $B with no space, nothing else." op v=$(fm_backend_herdr_send_text_submit "$TARGET" "$op" 3 0.4 0.6) if [ "$v" = empty ] && wait_reply "$A$B"; then rec "S3 PASS long U+2063 digest (${#op} chars) verdict=$v reply=$A$B"; else rec "S3 FAIL verdict=$v"; fi snap S3; wait_idle; sleep 2 # S4 adversarial: operator draft already in composer -> nothing typed, send-failed. DRAFT="operator draft $RANDOM keep me" lab pane send-text "$PANE" "$DRAFT" >/dev/null; sleep 1 T4="NEVERSENT$RANDOM" v=$(fm_backend_herdr_send_text_submit "$TARGET" "Reply with exactly $T4." 3 0.4 0.6) sleep 3 scr=$(lab pane read "$PANE" --source recent --lines 60 2>/dev/null) printf '%s\n' "$scr" > "$EVID/screen-S4.txt" if [ "$v" = send-failed ] && ! grep -Fq "$T4" <<<"$scr" && grep -Fq "$DRAFT" <<<"$scr"; then rec "S4 PASS pre-filled composer refused verdict=$v, draft kept, payload not typed"; else rec "S4 FAIL verdict=$v"; fi i=0; while [ "$i" -lt 10 ] && [ "$(fm_backend_herdr_composer_state "$TARGET")" != empty ]; do lab pane send-keys "$PANE" ctrl+u >/dev/null; i=$((i+1)); sleep 0.3; done sleep 1 # S5 adversarial: inject the reported fault - only the tail of the text lands. eval "orig_$(declare -f fm_backend_herdr_send_literal)" fm_backend_herdr_send_literal() { orig_fm_backend_herdr_send_literal "$1" "${2: -400}"; } A="HEADT$RANDOM"; B="TAILT$RANDOM" msg="The head code is $A. $(filler 2000 ' ')Reply with exactly $B-TRUNCATED and nothing else." v=$(fm_backend_herdr_send_text_submit "$TARGET" "$msg" 3 0.4 0.6) st=$(fm_backend_herdr_composer_state "$TARGET") sleep 5 scr=$(lab pane read "$PANE" --source recent --lines 200 2>/dev/null) printf '%s\n' "$scr" > "$EVID/screen-S5.txt" n=$(grep -F -c "$B-TRUNCATED" <<<"$scr" || true) if [ "$v" = send-failed ] && [ "$st" = empty ] && [ "$n" = 0 ]; then rec "S5 PASS tail-only composer refused verdict=$v composer=$st, no turn submitted"; else rec "S5 FAIL verdict=$v composer=$st occurrences=$n"; fi eval "$(declare -f orig_fm_backend_herdr_send_literal | sed 's/^orig_fm_backend_herdr_send_literal/fm_backend_herdr_send_literal/')" # S6: clean retry of the same message after refusal delivers it whole. msg="The head code is $A. $(filler 2000 ' ')Reply with only the head code immediately followed by $B with no space, nothing else." v=$(fm_backend_herdr_send_text_submit "$TARGET" "$msg" 3 0.4 0.6) if [ "$v" = empty ] && wait_reply "$A$B"; then rec "S6 PASS clean retry after refusal verdict=$v reply=$A$B"; else rec "S6 FAIL verdict=$v"; fi snap S6; wait_idle # S7: non-Claude pane (plain shell) keeps type-then-Enter without the proof. SH_JSON=$(lab pane split "$PANE" --direction right --no-focus 2>/dev/null || lab tab create --workspace "$(printf '%s' "$WS_JSON" | jq -r '.result.workspace.workspace_id')" --no-focus) SH=$(printf '%s' "$SH_JSON" | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id // .result.root_pane.pane_id') sleep 2 OUT="$TMP_ROOT/nonclaude.out" v=$(fm_backend_herdr_send_text_submit "$SESSION:$SH" "echo NONCLAUDE_OK_$(filler 1200 ' ' | tr -dc 'a-z' | head -c 1200) > $OUT" 3 0.4 0.6) sleep 2 if [ -s "$OUT" ] && grep -q '^NONCLAUDE_OK_' "$OUT"; then rec "S7 PASS non-Claude shell pane executed long command (verdict=$v, ident='$(fm_backend_herdr_agent_identity_raw "$SESSION" "$SH")')"; else rec "S7 FAIL verdict=$v"; fi ```

title: fix(bin): preserve armed PR merge polls across relaunches
body:
## Intent Take the two upstream ready-for-pr issues https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/5291 and https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/5135, both about a relaunch silently breaking an armed PR merge poll so a merge is never announced. Judge whether they are one defect or two before building: if one fix closes both, say so plainly and deliver once, linking both issues. Deliver on the standard upstream path (the maintainer merges), with a behavioral regression that fails on the current base. Say plainly in the report whether the fix was proven on a real relaunch of a task with an armed poll, or only by tests. Out of scope: any wider rework of the merge-poll authentication model beyond what these two tickets describe. Context: 5291 says `bin/fm-control.sh relaunch` appends `control_relaunch_tx=` after `pr=`/`pr_head=` in `state/.meta`, and `fm_pr_metadata_identity_parse` in `bin/fm-pr-lib.sh` rejects any unrecognised key after `pr=`, so `fm_pr_poll_artifacts_valid` fails and the watcher reports `check: rejected unauthenticated state checks` for the task's own untampered poll. 5135 describes the same observed failure from the relaunch side: the `bin/fm-spawn.sh` relaunch meta rewrite emits owned keys, then `preserve_relaunch_meta` (carrying `pr=`/`pr_head=`), then `control_relaunch_tx=`; its suggested fix is to emit `control_relaunch_tx=` with the owned keys before the preserved ones, with allowlisting the key as the narrower alternative. The maintainer's triage on both is ready-for-pr, contract-class restore, and prefers keeping preserved identity keys last over allowlisting keys one at a time; both suggest a regression that arms a poll, relaunches, and asserts the poll still validates. Workaround today: re-running `bin/fm-pr-check.sh ` rewrites `pr=`/`pr_head=` last and restores the binding. ## What Changed - Write `control_relaunch_tx` before preserved PR identity fields so relaunch keeps armed merge polls authenticated, fixing the same defect reported in [#5291](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/5291) and [#5135](https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/5135). - Prepend recorded `traceparent` so traced relaunches preserve the same ordering without relaxing authentication checks. - Add regressions for repeated control and direct relaunches with tracing on/off, including rejection of unknown trailing fields. Document that coverage uses stubbed session and forge CLIs, not a live-agent relaunch. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: Both issues share one metadata-ordering defect; the bounded fix, including the trace-writer correction, preserves PR identity ordering without weakening authentication. ## Testing The base reproduced the defect; targeted regressions passed after fixing fixture layout. Five real relaunches preserved the original poll, and watcher checks proved corruption rejection and merge notification.
