title: feat(bin): add loopback operator console with durable memory and source-linked retrieval
body:
## Intent Continue VPS work by giving the console durable conversation memory and source-linked retrieval. Preserve every interaction beyond the inbox note, retrieve only bounded relevant excerpts from curated local markdown, show each answer's source-linked excerpt, and provide a visible cursor for later curation. Retrieval cost must scale with retrieved material rather than accumulated history. Do not use embeddings or paid APIs. Include a confined server-side artifact route for report links rather than exposing a static directory. ## What Changed - Added `bin/fm-console.py` and a static page under `web/console/`. The console listens only on `127.0.0.1` and every route requires HTTP Basic auth with a private `config/console-operator-secret`. Order writes also need a same-origin request and a CSRF token. The page shows fleet state from `fm-bearings-snapshot.sh`, with polling shared across clients and never more often than every 15 seconds. It also shows orders, receipts, replies, and readiness from `fm-inbox.sh`. - Each durable reply in `/api/receipts` gets a `curated` flag and, when something matches, one best excerpt from this home's curated markdown. The excerpt names its source file, its line, and an opaque artifact id. Only a fixed allowlist is searched: `captain.md`, `captain-shared.md`, `learnings.md`, and task `report.md` files under `data/`. The search uses plain substring matching with no embeddings or paid APIs. The number of candidate files and the bytes read per file are both capped, so cost does not grow with history. `GET /artifact/[?line=N]` returns a bounded window of lines from a file on that same allowlist, and any id that doesn't resolve returns 404 instead of reading from disk. A curation cursor in `state/console-curated-through` only moves when someone runs `--mark-curated `, and the page shows how many answers are still uncurated. - Added `bin/fm-inbox-receipts.py`, a serialized, owner-only SQLite projection of the inbox. `fm-inbox.sh receipts` now reads its bounded pages from it. Each note, reply, announcement, and ack goes through a publish step that updates that one record, and interrupted publishes are reconciled on the next operation. The new `receipts --rebuild` re-imports from the inbox files, which stay authoritative. Docs (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/scripts.md`) and tests (`tests/fm-console.test.sh`, `tests/fm-inbox.test.sh`) are updated to cover this. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The current fixes are bounded and address the selected findings; review found no additional material defects beyond previously accepted concerns. ## Testing I ran the console and inbox as a user would, against isolated throwaway homes on port 18765, using curl and headless Chromium. Everything passed: - **Durable memory:** orders and replies survive a console restart. - **Source-linked answers:** each answer shows its source excerpt and a working "View source" link (screenshot captured). - **Curation cursor:** it rejects an invalid cursor and flips the per-answer `curated` flags when advanced. - **Artifact route:** it returns 404 or 400 for every traversal, symlink, archive, and extra-query attempt, and 401 without credentials. - **Bounded cost:** polling took a median of 47 ms with both 2 and 5000 replies. Search opened exactly 40 files (the cap) out of 5000 task dirs in 4 ms. - **Permissions:** a pre-existing 0644 receipt database was tightened to 0600. - **Existing suites:** `tests/fm-console.test.sh` and `tests/fm-inbox.test.sh` both passed. This was an operator-console check only, so no Herdr lab was needed. The chrome-devtools-axi helper failed with a pageId validation error, so I drove Playwright's bundled Chromium directly over CDP. A throwaway local proxy added the Basic auth header for the browser. All temporary homes and processes were removed afterwards. - Live validation: ✅ go - 9 of 9 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Operator sends an order and receives replies; after a console restart, /api/receipts still lists the order and both answers | ✅ pass | live | order-persistence-and-permissions.txt, receipts-api-transcript.txt | | Each durable answer in /api/receipts and the Do work UI shows one bounded 'Related from memory' excerpt naming its file:line from curated markdown | ✅ pass | live | receipts-api-transcript.txt, console-do-work-answers.png | | Clicking 'View source' loads a line-windowed view of that file through /artifact/<id> | ✅ pass | live | console-view-source-expanded.png, artifact-route-transcript.txt | | Adversarial: artifact route refuses traversal ids, encoded slashes, memory-archive.md, symlinked curated/report files, extra query params, static /data paths, and unauthenticated requests | ✅ pass | live | artifact-route-transcript.txt (all 404/400/401) | | Curation cursor is visible ('1 of 2 durable answers are not yet folded'), --mark-curated advances it, and an invalid cursor is rejected | ✅ pass | live | curation-cursor-transcript.txt, console-do-work-answers.png | | Adversarial: poll latency (receipts --after latest) does not grow with history (2 vs 5000 replies) | ✅ pass | live | bounded-retrieval-timing.txt (47 ms vs 47 ms; full scan 265 ms) | | Adversarial: retrieval over 5000 task report dirs reads only the capped candidate set and returns one budget-bounded excerpt | ✅ pass | live | bounded-search-bighome.txt (40 files opened, 153-byte excerpt, /api/receipts in 0.06 s) | | Receipt SQLite projection mirroring private notes becomes owner-only even when a 0644 database already exists under umask 022 | ✅ pass | live | order-persistence-and-permissions.txt (before -rw-r--r--, after -rw-------) | | No embeddings or paid APIs are used for retrieval | ✅ pass | live | Retrieval ran fully offline in isolated homes with no model credentials and returned literal-match excerpts (receipts-api-transcript.txt) | - Evidence: [Do work lane with source-linked excerpts and curation status](https://github.com/cliflacata-svg/firstmate/blob/9dff802c6849b93658a262a62685c5ff51777626/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-console-memory-lane/console-do-work-answers.png) - Evidence: [View source expanded via confined artifact route](https://github.com/cliflacata-svg/firstmate/blob/9dff802c6849b93658a262a62685c5ff51777626/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-console-memory-lane/console-view-source-expanded.png)

The browser ignores result.curated_through, so its stored reply remains curated=false indefinitely and the visible count stays wrong until reload. Recompute cached replies' flags from the returned cursor on every poll. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-console.py:109` - Artifact resolution uses the first-40 search candidate list as its authorization allowlist. Once that list fills, adding an alphabetically earlier report can push a previously linked report out and make its existing View source link return 404, although the file remains valid. No supplied intent requirement needs this separate monitoring feature. Remove that component from this change. - ⚠️ `web/console/index.html:35` - Simplification: the disabled Quick ask lane and its model-cost explanation satisfy no stated requirement for local conversation memory or source retrieval. Remove the placeholder lane and its associated navigation and styling. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-console.py:160` - Simplification: search_curated assembles up to four excerpts, but its sole production caller consumes only matches[0]. No intent requirement needs the discarded results or configurable chunk count. Return one bounded best excerpt and remove the unused multi-result accumulation. 🔧 Fix applied. 2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open: - ⚠️ `bin/fm-inbox-receipts.py:96` - The fix round wraps every drain, note, announcement, reply, and voice transcription in one exclusive receipt lock and unconditionally rebuilds all history afterward. Even read-only `drain` now scans and rewrites every handled note and reply; `say` holds up receipt polling throughout audio input and transcription. This exceeds bounded receipt retrieval and introduces history-dependent latency across existing inbox operations. Revert this broad command wrapper to a minimal projection update at actual record mutations, leaving read-only drains and transcription outside the lock. - 🚨 `bin/fm-console.py:89` - The requirement "Retrieval cost must scale with retrieved material rather than accumulated history" remains violated by `sorted(data_dir.iterdir())`: every uncached answer and artifact lookup enumerates and sorts all accumulated task directories before the 40-file limit applies. With many retained task reports, returning one excerpt still costs O(N log N) directory processing. Use bounded candidate discovery that does not enumerate accumulated task history; the current post-enumeration cap does not establish the required bound. 🔧 Fix applied. 1 error still open: - 🚨 `bin/fm-inbox-receipts.py:104` - With a normal 022 umask and traversable home/state directories, SQLite creates this database mode 0644. refresh_note/rebuild copy complete private note and reply bodies into it, allowing other local users to read records whose original mktemp-created files are mode 0600. Create the projection with owner-only permissions before connecting, and restrict existing projection files and SQLite sidecars. 🔧 Fix applied. ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix(bin): accept and pass Grok xhigh reasoning effort
body:
## Intent Fix Firstmate so a requested Grok extra-high effort is passed through and not dropped. Grok 1.0.40 on this machine accepts extra-high. Firstmate still omits it at launch, and the startup check plus typed dispatch check reject a dispatch profile that sets Grok to extra-high. That rejection is blocking worker dispatch in the finweave home: the hard-design rule sets grok-4.7 to extra-high, and that home only accepts low, medium, or high for Grok. Leave max omitted. Do not change the dispatch file. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-spawn.sh` now passes `--reasoning-effort 'xhigh'` when launching Grok. It still leaves out `max`. - The startup dispatch check in `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` and the typed dispatch check in `bin/fm-dispatch-resolve.sh` now accept `xhigh` for Grok. Agy stays limited to `low`/`medium`/`high`, and Grok `max` is still rejected. - The Grok harness reference now records that extra-high effort was verified with Grok 1.0.40. The tests that expected Grok `xhigh` to be rejected or dropped now check that it is accepted and passed at launch. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change adds xhigh to the Grok effort list in three places: the launch flag, the startup check and the typed dispatch check. max stays omitted, the dispatch file is untouched, and composer title parsing already recognizes Grok (xhigh). ## Testing Confirmed that the real Grok 1.0.40 accepts xhigh and rejects max. Ran the startup check and the typed dispatch check on base and target with a grok-4.7/xhigh hard-design rule: base rejects it (CREW_DISPATCH invalid effort; resolver exit 2), target accepts it (rule listed; resolver status clear with profile `--effort 'xhigh'`). On target, Grok max and agy xhigh are still rejected. The targeted spawn dispatch-profile test file passed; it records `--reasoning-effort 'xhigh'` in the launch line, keeps max out, and records the effort in meta. That test uses a fake backend, so the full fm-spawn scenario is marked untested as a live run. In a throwaway fm-lab Herdr session, the spawn-shaped Grok command ran for real: the TUI footer shows `Grok 4.7 (xhigh)` and the model replied. The lab was torn down and the default session was untouched. This is not a UI change, so the evidence is CLI and pane-capture text. All live scenarios passed. - Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 6 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Startup check (fm-bootstrap.sh) accepts a dispatch profile whose hard-design rule sets grok-4.7 to xhigh, and base rejected it | ✅ pass | live | 02-bootstrap-startup-check.txt | | Typed dispatch check (fm-dispatch-resolve.sh) resolves the grok-4.7/xhigh rule to a clear profile instead of exiting 2 as base did | ✅ pass | live | 03-typed-dispatch-resolve.txt (typesafe.ai API stubbed; real quota-axi) | | Spawn passes --reasoning-effort 'xhigh' to Grok and records effort=xhigh | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: the full fm-spawn run was only exercised through the unit test's fake backend (tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh). A live fm-spawn run against… | | The spawn-shaped Grok xhigh launch runs for real in an isolated Herdr lab pane and Grok reports xhigh | ✅ pass | live | 05-herdr-lab-real-grok-xhigh-pane.txt (footer 'Grok 4.7 (xhigh)', reply FMXHIGHLIVEOK) | | Adversarial: Grok max is still left out of the launch and still rejected by the startup and typed dispatch checks | ✅ pass | live | 04-guards-max-and-agy.txt; 01-real-grok-effort-acceptance.txt (real grok rejects max); spawn test test_grok_omits_invalid_max_reasoning_effort | | Adversarial: widening Grok does not let agy accept xhigh | ✅ pass | live | 04-guards-max-and-agy.txt |
Evidence: Real Grok 1.0.40 accepts xhigh, rejects max Source: [Real Grok 1.0.40 accepts xhigh, rejects max](https://github.com/TiberiusNemesis/firstmate/blob/06bcb34c3cb5688f581dc9c4bf2b72a1463deb63/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/grok-xhigh-pass/01-real-grok-effort-acceptance.txt) ```text $ grok --model grok-4.7 --reasoning-effort xhigh -p 'Reply with exactly: OK' OK exit=0 $ grok --model grok-4.7 --reasoning-effort max -p 'Reply with exactly: OK' --effort/--reasoning-effort: unknown effort level 'max'; use one of: xhigh, high, medium, low Error: --effort/--reasoning-effort: unknown effort level 'max'; use one of: xhigh, high, medium, low exit=0 ```
Evidence: Startup check: base rejects grok:xhigh, target accepts Source: [Startup check: base rejects grok:xhigh, target accepts](https://github.com/TiberiusNemesis/firstmate/blob/06bcb34c3cb5688f581dc9c4bf2b72a1463deb63/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/grok-xhigh-pass/02-bootstrap-startup-check.txt) base: CREW_DISPATCH: invalid config/crew-dispatch.json - invalid effort: grok:xhigh target: BOOTSTRAP_INFO: crew dispatch rule: hard design work -> grok/grok-4.7/xhigh ```text === base (ada21f5) fm-bootstrap.sh, FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS=1, CREW_DISPATCH lines === CREW_DISPATCH: invalid config/crew-dispatch.json - invalid effort: grok:xhigh === target (353c0e8) fm-bootstrap.sh, FM_BOOTSTRAP_VERBOSE_FACTS=1, CREW_DISPATCH lines === BOOTSTRAP_INFO: crew dispatch active config/crew-dispatch.json BOOTSTRAP_INFO: crew dispatch rule: hard design work -> grok/grok-4.7/xhigh BOOTSTRAP_INFO: crew dispatch rule: routine fixes -> grok/grok-4.7/high config/crew-dispatch.json used: {"rules":[{"when":"hard design work","use":{"harness":"grok","model":"grok-4.7","effort":"xhigh"},"why":"deep reasoning"},{"when":"routine fixes","use":{"harness":"grok","model":"grok-4.7","effort":"high"}}]} ```

Evidence: Guards: grok max and agy xhigh still rejected Source: [Guards: grok max and agy xhigh still rejected](https://github.com/TiberiusNemesis/firstmate/blob/06bcb34c3cb5688f581dc9c4bf2b72a1463deb63/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/grok-xhigh-pass/04-guards-max-and-agy.txt) ```text === target guard: grok max ({"rules":[{"when":"hard design work","use":{"harness":"grok","model":"grok-4.7","effort":"max"}}]}) === -- fm-bootstrap.sh: CREW_DISPATCH: invalid config/crew-dispatch.json - invalid effort: grok:max -- fm-dispatch-resolve.sh: error: malformed rules file: /tmp/fm-grok-xhigh-test/home-guard-grok-max/config/crew-dispatch.json - each use profile effort must be supported by its harness and model exit=2 === target guard: agy xhigh ({"rules":[{"when":"hard design work","use":{"harness":"agy","effort":"xhigh"}}]}) === -- fm-bootstrap.sh: CREW_DISPATCH: invalid config/crew-dispatch.json - invalid effort: agy:xhigh -- fm-dispatch-resolve.sh: error: malformed rules file: /tmp/fm-grok-xhigh-test/home-guard-agy-xhigh/config/crew-dispatch.json - each use profile effort must be supported by its harness and model exit=2 ```
Evidence: Herdr lab pane: real Grok TUI running at xhigh Source: [Herdr lab pane: real Grok TUI running at xhigh](https://github.com/TiberiusNemesis/firstmate/blob/06bcb34c3cb5688f581dc9c4bf2b72a1463deb63/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/grok-xhigh-pass/05-herdr-lab-real-grok-xhigh-pane.txt) FMXHIGHLIVEOK ... Grok 4.7 (xhigh) · always-approve ```text Herdr lab session: fm-lab-grokxhigh-30260-23504 pane: fm-lab-grokxhigh-30260-23504:w1:p2 Launch line typed into the pane (the grok shape fm-spawn.sh emits for --model grok-4.7 --effort xhigh, with a one-line brief): grok --always-approve --model 'grok-4.7' --reasoning-effort 'xhigh' "Reply with exactly the single word FMXHIGHLIVEOK and do nothing else." --- pane capture --- main /p/t/fm-grok-xhigh-test/wt 20K / 500K │ [Dashboard] ❯ Reply with exactly the single word FMXHIGHLIVEOK and do nothing else. 5:26 PM FMXHIGHLIVEOK 5:26 PM Worked for 3.1s ╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ ❯ │ ╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Grok 4.7 (xhigh) · always-approve ─╯ Shift+Tab:mode │ Ctrl+.:shortcuts ```

The change adds regression coverage for the startup check (tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh:1135) and for launch (tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh:537), but nothing checks that fm-dispatch-resolve.sh now accepts `{"harness":"grok","effort":"xhigh"}`. title: fix(bin): accept Codex max effort for any catalog-advertised model
body:
## Intent

File a PR for Firstmate for that model level issue.

Context: the GPT-6 research scout (section Local availability and Firstmate compatibility of its report) found that Firstmate's Codex profile path accepts and emits the max reasoning effort only for gpt-5.6-luna: bin/fm-dispatch-resolve.sh line 132 and bin/fm-bootstrap.sh line 1140 special-case that model in their jq validators, and bin/fm-spawn.sh lines 2355-2364 emit model_reasoning_effort="max" only for it, so any other model passed max gets no effort flag at all. The installed Codex catalog (~/.codex/models_cache.json, codex-cli 0.155.1) advertises max for gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, gpt-6-astra and gpt-5.6-terra as well. Firstmate's harness reference records that the earlier catalog advertised max only for gpt-5.6-luna, which is why the special case exists. The routing config now uses gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna on probation; the desk cannot pin max for them. Codex ultra stays out of scope (Firstmate reserves ultra for its native Pi route).

## What Changed

- Added `bin/fm-harness.sh codex-max-models`, a single reader that prints the model slugs whose entry in `${CODEX_HOME:-~/.codex}/models_cache.json` lists `max` under `supported_reasoning_levels[].effort`, and exits 1 with an error naming the catalog when the file is absent, unreadable, malformed, or `jq` is missing.
- `bin/fm-dispatch-resolve.sh` and `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` now validate a Codex `effort: max` profile against that catalog list instead of hardcoding `gpt-5.6-luna`; when the catalog cannot be read they accept the profile and emit one diagnostic (a `dispatch-resolve: notice:` stderr line, or a `BOOTSTRAP_INFO: crew dispatch codex max:` fact) rather than rejecting the config. `bin/fm-spawn.sh` emits `model_reasoning_effort="max"` for any model the catalog advertises it for, and otherwise records `max` in task metadata and omits the flag with a stderr notice.
- Updated `docs/configuration.md` and the Codex harness reference to describe the catalog-driven rule (gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna on codex-cli 0.155.1), added `tests/fm-harness-codex-catalog.test.sh`, and extended the bootstrap, dispatch-resolve, and spawn dispatch-profile tests to cover advertised, non-advertised, and unreadable-catalog cases. Codex `ultra` remains out of scope.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: The fix satisfies the intent (catalog-advertised models now validate and launch with max, ultra stays refused, no luna special case remains) and is well tested, but it makes dispatch-config validity depend on a local cache file and reports a missing catalog as a malformed config, which is safe to merge and worth a follow-up.

## Testing

Ran the four targeted suites touched by the change (all passed), then drove the catalog reader, resolver, and bootstrap validator live against the real installed Codex catalog, including a before/after run of the resolver at the base commit that reproduces the original rejection of gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna max; every live-driven scenario matched the intent. The fm-spawn launch composition was exercised only through the suite's recording tmux stub without starting codex, so those two scenarios are reported as untested, and a real Codex agent launch with max effort inside a Herdr lab was not attempted.

title: fix(bin): guard teardown of a pool slot bound to another home's clone
body:
## Intent Fix the defect in which cleaning up a finished task (bin/fm-teardown.sh) can kill a live sibling worker and reset its local copy, and propose the fix upstream to kunchenguid/firstmate as a public pull request from the fork moraismtgo-source/firstmate. Publish decision of 2026-09-22, verbatim: "1 - propor as correcoes ao autor do firstmate, com uma copia no GitHub da conta e pedidos de integracao publicos". What happened on 2026-09-22: in a secondmate home, two task records named the same treehouse slot, because the pool had already handed the slot of a finished task to a new task. Teardown of the finished task did not refuse; it reaped every process under the slot, including the live worker of the other task, returned the slot to the pool and left it detached at origin/main. No work was lost only because that worker had already pushed. Why the guards did not fire: both slot-ownership guards in bin/fm-teardown.sh (the record-exclusivity scan and the .fm-slot-owner claim check) are scoped to teardown_live_slot_path, which fails whenever fm_treehouse_pool_slot cannot match the recording home's project clone to the slot's git common dir. A pool bound to ANOTHER home's clone of the same project, which is the case for every project cloned both in the main home and in a secondmate home, passes both guards vacuously while the destructive reap-and-return still runs. bin/fm-spawn.sh skips the .fm-slot-owner claim write for the same reason, which is how the slot could be handed to a second task while a stale record still named it. The incident record says: after merging a finished task, both that task and a live sibling recorded the same worktree path. The pool had already handed the slot on (checkout moved from the finished branch to origin/main, then to the sibling's branch). Teardown did not refuse. It reaped every process under the slot, force-killed the live worker, returned the slot, and left it detached at origin/main. The sibling's branch was already pushed, so no work was lost, but the worker and its local copy were gone. Both ownership guards return success when the slot proof fails. That proof requires the recording home's project clone and the slot to share a git common directory. The pool was bound to the other home's clone, so the proof failed, the guards did not run, and the reap and return still did. Spawn never wrote the slot claim for the same reason. Done when a slot that cannot be proven safe is never reaped or returned, a second home sharing the pool is protected by the same guards as the owning home, spawn records the slot claim in that case too, a regression test proves it, and the upstream PR is open with checks green. ## What Changed - `fm_treehouse_pool_slot` in `bin/fm-wake-lib.sh` now accepts a slot whose pool is bound to another clone of the same project. The lock path and the slot check now share a new `fm_treehouse_project_identity` helper (the resolved origin, or the worktree top when there is no origin). A slot counts as this project's when its git common directory matches the project's, or when both resolve to the same project identity. title: fix(bin): prefer a live run over an older failed row on the same branch
body:
A rebase can leave the live validation on a head the local tip is not an ancestor of, while an older failed row still names that tip. The runs list is newest-first, so a same-branch row whose status is running now wins immediately. Other rows still have to match the worktree head.

Covered by a test where a newer running row on a rebased head outranks an older failed row that sits on the local tip.

title: fix(bin): install lavish-axi without machine-wide SessionStart hooks
body:
## Intent Stop firstmate's lavish-axi install command from installing machine-wide SessionStart hooks. bin/fm-bootstrap.sh install_cmd told operators (and 'fm-bootstrap.sh install lavish-axi' executed) 'npm install -g lavish-axi && lavish-axi setup hooks'. 'lavish-axi setup hooks' writes an unconditional, user-level SessionStart hook into Claude Code (~/.claude/settings.json), Codex (~/.codex/hooks.json), OpenCode (a global plugin) and GitHub Copilot CLI, with no project scoping. Observed effect on a real machine: after a firstmate session ran it, every agent session on the machine - including ones unrelated to firstmate - started with ~10KB of Lavish ambient context listing all open firstmate boards and instructing the agent to run 'lavish-axi ' and 'lavish-axi poll'. That contradicts firstmate's own crew-hosted board contract (bin/fm-brief.sh LAVISH_LINE: arm the board with bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh and never run lavish-axi poll yourself; AGENTS.md: firstmate never arms or polls boards itself). Firstmate does not need the hook because briefs and AGENTS.md already name lavish-axi and the adapter. Decision: only lavish-axi changes to a plain 'npm install -g lavish-axi'; gh-axi and chrome-devtools-axi keep 'setup hooks' because their ambient context does not conflict with a firstmate contract and changing them is out of scope. The rationale lives as a short comment beside install_cmd (the script owns install mechanics per the coding guidelines); docs/configuration.md is intentionally unchanged because it defers the lavish install command to the script. tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh's expected PRESENTATION_UNAVAILABLE line is updated accordingly. Out of scope: uninstalling hooks already installed on existing machines (lavish-axi has no uninstall command), and changing lavish-axi itself. ## What Changed - `install_cmd` in `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh` now returns `npm install -g lavish-axi` for lavish-axi, without `&& lavish-axi setup hooks`. That `setup hooks` step writes a user-level SessionStart hook with no project scoping into Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Copilot CLI. As a result, every agent session on the machine received Lavish ambient context that tells it to poll boards directly. This change affects both the install hint in the `PRESENTATION_UNAVAILABLE` message and `fm-bootstrap.sh install lavish-axi`. `gh-axi` and `chrome-devtools-axi` still run `setup hooks`. - A short comment next to the case entry explains the exception. The hook's ambient context conflicts with the crew-hosted board contract, where the board is armed through `bin/fm-procevent-lavish.sh` and firstmate never polls boards itself. - `tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh` (`test_lavish_axi_min_version`) now expects the new install hint in the `PRESENTATION_UNAVAILABLE` line. Hooks that earlier runs already installed on existing machines stay in place, because lavish-axi has no uninstall command. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A small change moves lavish-axi into the plain `npm install -g` branch of install_cmd. gh-axi and chrome-devtools-axi still run `setup hooks`. The rationale comment and the expected test string match the stated intent, and no other docs or code point to the old lavish install command. ## Testing I ran the real `fm-bootstrap.sh install` command against fake npm and fake axi tools that log every call and mimic `setup hooks` writing a user-level SessionStart hook, with HOME set to a throwaway directory. On the base commit, installing lavish-axi wrote the hook. With this change it runs only `npm install -g lavish-axi` and leaves no settings file. gh-axi and chrome-devtools-axi still install their hooks. I also ran tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh. Its lavish-axi min-version test passed with the new PRESENTATION_UNAVAILABLE line. One test in that file failed, the per-clone fleet-sync timing test, which covers code this change does not touch. No Herdr lab was needed because the change is limited to CLI install commands. - Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Operator runs `fm-bootstrap.sh install lavish-axi`: only `npm install -g lavish-axi` runs and no user-level SessionStart hook is written | ✅ pass | live | install-transcript.txt: AFTER section shows a single npm call and $HOME/.claude/settings.json absent | | Regression check: the base commit installs the machine-wide hook on the same command, and this change does not | ✅ pass | live | install-transcript.txt: BEFORE (base f5735dc) ran `lavish-axi setup hooks` and wrote a SessionStart hook; AFTER did neither | | gh-axi and chrome-devtools-axi still install their hooks (the intent keeps these out of scope) | ✅ pass | live | install-transcript.txt: both run `<tool> setup hooks` after the npm install | | Installing several tools at once (tasks-axi + lavish-axi) still triggers no hook setup | ✅ pass | live | install-transcript.txt: last section shows two plain npm installs and no settings file | | Bootstrap with lavish-axi absent or too old prints PRESENTATION_UNAVAILABLE with the plain `npm install -g lavish-axi` hint and does not block the run | ✅ pass | live | tests/fm-bootstrap.test.sh `test_lavish_axi_min_version` ran the real bin/fm-bootstrap.sh with a fake toolchain: 'ok - bootstrap permits nonvisual work without compatible lavish-axi and retains its pr… |

title: fix(bin): consult the slot owner claim before teardown's record scan
body:
## Intent Two Firstmate task records that name the same reused treehouse pool slot deadlock each other: neither can ever be torn down, the stale one keeps its endpoint alive in the fleet view, and the watcher re-fires a stale wake for it on every poll. Reproduced live on 2026-09-22 in the main home, twice: - cache-tags-guard (stale: worker gone, PR #175 merged to waselni-backend master on 2026-09-19) and ts-parity-s1 (the real current owner) both record worktree=/Users/cto/.treehouse/waselni-backend-89119c/2/waselni-backend. - underpay-ts1 (stale, superseded) and api-driver-suspension both record worktree=/Users/cto/.treehouse/waselni-backend-ts-ad71ac/2/waselni-backend-ts. Tearing down either member refuses with "REFUSED: task X's recorded worktree is also task Y's recorded worktree", including under --force, so the pair is permanently stuck. In the first pair the slot-owner claim file at /Users/cto/.treehouse/waselni-backend-89119c/2/.fm-slot-owner reads task=ts-parity-s1, which proves cache-tags-guard is the stale record and owns nothing in that slot. bin/fm-teardown.sh's own header (lines 81-105) already describes the intended behaviour for exactly this case: a claim naming another task is proof of reassignment, so teardown should warn, name the claimant, and finish only that task's own cleanup - endpoint, status, records, checks, backlog - while skipping every step that would read or touch the slot. That carve-out never gets a chance to run, because require_exclusive_worktree_slot_record() refuses first. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-teardown.sh` now gates a task's own pool slot through a single `require_task_worktree_slot_ownership()` that reads the slot's owner claim first and only falls through to `require_exclusive_task_worktree_slot` when the claim does not settle ownership (absent, or naming this very record). A claim naming a different task now reaches the existing reassignment carve-out — warn, name the claimant, finish only this record's endpoint/status/records/checks/backlog cleanup — instead of being refused by the record-exclusivity scan that previously ran first and rejected both records of a reused-slot pair. - `preflight_descendant_treehouse_slots()` applies the same order for secondmate children: a child slot the claim proves was reassigned is skipped before the record scan runs, so the rest of the forced teardown proceeds without touching that slot. - Documented the claim-first ordering and its deadlock rationale in the `bin/fm-teardown.sh` header, the `require_owned_worktree_slot_record()` comment, and `docs/architecture.md`; added `test_claim_breaks_the_two_record_slot_deadlock_only_for_the_non_owner` (covering the disowned record, the real owner's subsequent normal teardown, and the unclaimed / self-claimed / unreadable-claim cases that must still refuse) and `test_secondmate_force_teardown_clears_reassigned_duplicated_child_slot` for the descendant path. ## Risk Assessment 🚨 High: The reordering itself is sound, well-documented, and strictly safer than what it replaces, but source and on-disk evidence prove one of the two live reproductions the authoritative intent names remains permanently un-tearable with no supported escape, so shipping a partial fix needs the author's explicit call. ## Testing I read the change, ran the two suites that own this boundary (fm-teardown-endpoint-safety and fm-secondmate-safety) - both green - and proved the commit's new test is a genuine regression test by temporarily reverting bin/fm-teardown.sh to base f5735dc, where it fails with the exact reported "REFUSED ... not even with --force" refusal, then restoring it. For end-user evidence I built a live reproduction of the 2026-09-22 report (cache-tags-guard stale vs ts-parity-s1 owner, both records naming one reused pool slot, the slot claim naming ts-parity-s1, and a real worker process running inside the slot) and captured CLI transcripts of the real fm-teardown.sh before and after the fix: before, both members refuse under --force and the stale endpoint stays in the fleet view; after, the stale record warns, names the claimant, clears only its own records, and leaves the worker alive, the slot copy intact, the claim untouched and the slot un-returned, after which the real owner tears down and returns the slot. I also found that the commit reordered the same two guards in the descendant/secondmate preflight with no test covering it, so I added a focused test there that drives fm-teardown.sh domain --force over a secondmate home whose two child records name one reused slot claimed by a third task - it fails at base and passes at target. The second reported pair (unclaimed slot) still refuses, which matches the recorded declined decision and is pinned by the slot-reuse-unclaimed case. No screenshot applies: this change is a CLI/state-machine fix with no rendered UI surface, so the reviewer-visible artifacts are the CLI transcripts and the persisted record/slot state they print. The worktree is left with only the intentional new test.
Evidence: Before vs after summary of the deadlock repro Source: [Before vs after summary of the deadlock repro](https://github.com/ammar00sheikh/firstmate/blob/67eac71fc1405bab0d4bb50863baa78a400fdb9b/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/teardown-slot-deadlock/deadlock-before-after.md) ```text # Two-record treehouse slot deadlock - before vs after End-to-end reproduction of the live 2026-09-22 report, with the names from it: `cache-tags-guard` (stale) and `ts-parity-s1` (the real owner) both record `worktree=/2/waselni-backend`, and the slot's own claim file reads `task=ts-parity-s1`. A live worker process runs inside the contested slot. Driver: `repro-two-record-slot-deadlock.sh` (in this directory). It builds a real treehouse pool slot (git worktree + `treehouse-state.json` + `.fm-slot-owner`), two task records, and a live process in the slot, then runs the real `bin/fm-teardown.sh` against them. Full output: `before-fix-deadlock-transcript.txt`, `after-fix-deadlock-transcript.txt`. ## Before (base f5735dc) - both members permanently stuck `` ` $ fm-teardown.sh cache-tags-guard --force REFUSED: task cache-tags-guard's recorded worktree .../2/waselni-backend is also task ts-parity-s1's recorded worktree. Returning that pool slot would kill ts-parity-s1's processes and reset its copy, so nothing was changed - not even with --force. [exit 1] $ fm-teardown.sh ts-parity-s1 --force REFUSED: task ts-parity-s1's recorded worktree .../2/waselni-backend is also task cache-tags-guard's recorded worktree. Returning that pool slot would kill cache-tags-guard's processes and reset its copy, so nothing was changed - not even with --force. [exit 1] state/cache-tags-guard.meta (stale record) PRESENT <- stale endpoint stays in the fleet view state/ts-parity-s1.meta (live owner record) PRESENT slot returned to the treehouse pool no `` ` ## After (b7049e7) - the claim breaks the tie `` ` $ fm-teardown.sh cache-tags-guard --force warning: task cache-tags-guard's recorded worktree .../2/waselni-backend was reassigned to task ts-parity-s1 (home ...), which claimed that pool slot after this record was written; that slot is no longer cache-tags-guard's, so its processes, copy, and claim are left untouched and only cache-tags-guard's own cleanup runs. teardown cache-tags-guard complete (window firstmate:fm-cache-tags-guard; pool slot .../2/waselni-backend left to task ts-parity-s1 (home ...), which it was reassigned to) [exit 0] state/cache-tags-guard.meta (stale record) GONE <- stale endpoint cleared state/ts-parity-s1.meta (live owner record) PRESENT pool/2/.fm-slot-owner (slot claim) PRESENT <- owner's claim untouched ts-parity-s1 worker in the slot ALIVE <- live worker never killed slot returned to the treehouse pool no <- slot never returned/reset $ fm-teardown.sh ts-parity-s1 --force # the real owner, once its worker finished teardown ts-parity-s1 complete (window firstmate:fm-ts-parity-s1, worktree .../2/waselni-backend) [exit 0] state/ts-parity-s1.meta (live owner record) GONE pool/2/.fm-slot-owner (slot claim) GONE slot returned to the treehouse pool YES `` ` ## Guard states that must still refuse Covered by `tests/fm-teardown-endpoint-safety.test.sh` (`test_claim_breaks_the_two_record_slot_deadlock_only_for_the_non_owner`): - no claim on the contested slot -> still REFUSED (no evidence which record is stale) - claim naming *this* record -> still REFUSED (the other record is the stale one) - unreadable claim -> still REFUSED, and names the claim file to inspect ## Descendant (secondmate) half `tests/fm-secondmate-safety.test.sh::test_secondmate_force_teardown_clears_reassigned_duplicated_child_slot` (added in this test pass) drives `fm-teardown.sh domain --force` over a secondmate home whose two child records name one reused slot whose claim names a third task: before the fix the whole forced teardown refused; after it the home is retired, both child windows are killed, and the slot's checkout, sentinel file and claim survive with no `treehouse return`. ```
Evidence: CLI transcript - base f5735dc (both records permanently stuck) Source: [CLI transcript - base f5735dc (both records permanently stuck)](https://github.com/ammar00sheikh/firstmate/blob/67eac71fc1405bab0d4bb50863baa78a400fdb9b/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/teardown-slot-deadlock/before-fix-deadlock-transcript.txt) $ fm-teardown.sh cache-tags-guard --force REFUSED: task cache-tags-guard's recorded worktree .../2/waselni-backend is also task ts-parity-s1's recorded worktree. title: fix: require same-turn work admission after every wake
body:
## Intent

Defect observed: the supervising root spends its turns answering wakes on captain-held or unchanged rows instead of admitting eligible work. At 15:40Z on 2026-09-22 there was 1 worker working, 15 queued rows with no hold and no blocked-by, and 9.7 GB RAM available against the 6144 MiB floor.

Deliverable, stock-first (existing configuration and the existing resolver, no second scheduler): on every wake, after the acknowledgement, the root counts dispatchable rows (queued, unheld, unblocked) against measured headroom (the RAM floor, provider quota, serial slots) and admits up to that headroom in priority order in the SAME turn. It emits one line per wake: dispatchable=N admitted=M bound=<headroom|quota|slots|none>. Acceptance: a wake with dispatchable>0 and headroom>0 that admits nothing is a failure. Prefer an AGENTS.md, skill, or config change over Firstmate code.

## What Changed
- Require supervisors to admit eligible backlog rows in priority order after wake acknowledgement, using existing intake and spawn guards.
- Add a wake-admission skill defining memory, quota, and slot limits, actor ownership, and the `dispatchable=N admitted=M bound=...` summary.
- Update every harness supervision protocol, document policy ownership, and add rendered-instruction coverage for admission guidance.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is bounded to supervision instructions and generated-prompt coverage, preserves existing intake authority, and introduces no second scheduler.

## Testing

The focused generated-instruction tests passed and emitted prompts were captured. Live supervisor scenarios were blocked by the missing Herdr-managed execution context. No broad suite, linters, or lifecycle commands ran; no worktree changes remain. The previously declined live-evidence blocker is not raised again.

- Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 0 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A captain-held or unchanged-row wake acknowledges then admits eligible queued work in the same turn | ⏸️ untested | no | The Herdr skill prohibits control outside a Herdr-managed process. Re-run from a managed agent with an authenticated supervisor using the required isolated fm-lab-* helper lifecycle. |
| Multiple queued rows are admitted in priority order up to measured RAM, quota, and serial-slot capacity | ⏸️ untested | no | Requires the Herdr-managed execution context and authenticated supervisor described above. |
| A row-specific hold, escalation, or reasoning-class stop does not prevent admission of later eligible work | ⏸️ untested | no | Model interpretation requires an authenticated supervisor in the required named Herdr lab; this process lacks the managed execution context. |
| In-flight, held, blocked, and future-gated rows are excluded from new admission without bypassing intake authority | ⏸️ untested | no | Requires an isolated supervisor lab launched from a Herdr-managed agent; HERDR_ENV is unset here. |
| Every wake reports accurate dispatchable, admitted, and bound values, including repeated wakes and zero capacity | ⏸️ untested | no | Requires actual supervisor turns and persisted admission evidence from the authorized named Herdr lab. |

Mode: Claude Stop-hook-owned supervision.

When this session owns supervision and away mode is not active:
1. Drain first with `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh`.
   After handling all emitted wakes and reconciling open decisions and unread status lines, run the exact `--ack-through` command printed as `WAKE_ACK_REQUIRED`; until then the work remains durable for idempotent re-handling after interruption.
   After that acknowledgement, run AGENTS.md section 8's admission step and emit its one-line summary in the same turn.
2. Routine watcher arm and re-arm are owned by the Stop `asyncRewake` hook (`bin/fm-claude-stop-autoarm.sh`), never by you.
   Every turn end while supervision is needed launches or attaches one home-scoped watcher cycle with no model command and no model tokens.
   An actionable close wakes you through the hook's exit-2 rewake, delivered as a `Stop hook feedback` message.
3. On a `Stop hook feedback` wake (`signal:`, `stale:`, `check:`, or `heartbeat`), run `bin/fm-wake-drain.sh` first and handle the wake.
   Do not run `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh` after an ordinary wake; the next turn end re-arms automatically when supervision is still needed.
   Do not invent a wake from an attach-status line alone; drain and act only on real wake records, the drain's `OPEN DECISIONS` and `UNREAD STATUS` entries, or a real watcher reason line.
4. On the one `Stop hook feedback` automatic-mechanism failure notice (`firstmate watcher auto-arm FAILED ...`), drain, inspect the automatic mechanism failure, and do not turn the notice into a repeating manual-arm loop.
5. If the Stop hook does not claim the home or reports an exhausted failure, inspect its registration and watcher startup path before ending blind.
   Keep the Stop-owned automatic mechanism as the only Claude arm owner.
6. Treat `watcher: started ...` and `watcher: attached ...` inside automatic arm output as proof that one live cycle exists.
   On attach, the arm follows verified identity-matched successors instead of exiting when the first cycle ends.
7. The durable wake queue preserves actionable events between a rewake and the next Stop-launched arm, while the bounded turn-end guard prevents a blind Stop when recovery did not start.
   No PreToolUse hook denies fleet commands based on watcher status.
   [`watcher-continuity.md`](../watcher-continuity.md) owns the exact session-lock recovery boundary.
8. The turn-end guard (`bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh --claude`) remains the final backstop.
   It requires the PID-strict live-watcher and fresh-beacon predicate at the Stop boundary, except for the Claude-specific foreign-live-owner safe exit owned by [`turnend-guard.md`](../turnend-guard.md#guard-predicates); that document also owns the distinct model-aware mid-turn pull-guard rules.
   Otherwise, it allows the stop when a watcher is healthy or an open auto-arm generation claim owns recovery, while fresh failure epochs advance the bounded one-time attended fail-open progression described there.
9. Waiting on the hook-owned cycle is silent: do not send idle progress while the watcher is parked.

The watcher itself remains `bin/fm-watch.sh`, and `bin/fm-watch-arm.sh` remains the verified arm wrapper that the Stop hook foregrounds.
Re-arm attaches to an existing healthy cycle when one is already present and follows its verified successor chain.
See [`watcher-continuity.md`](../watcher-continuity.md) for the arm-layer successor and clean-close failure contract and the Claude ownership model.

title: fix(composer): recognize Muse 1.3's titled-rule composer and idle hints
body:
## Intent

Make firstmate able to restart Muse workers and second mates again after Muse's self-update to 1.3: teach the composer classifier Muse 1.3's input box so exit and relaunch can prove an empty composer, and stop fm-send skipping its doorbell on Muse's empty-composer placeholder hints. The ask, from a list of five queued firstmate fixes: "Start all five", with the Muse fix named as the one that currently prevents any automatic Muse restart.

Evidence, 2026-09-19: Muse self-updated to 1.3.0 (R3401.1). Its input box is now a bordered box whose top border carries the title '── Voice input (⌥ + v to start) ────' and whose prompt glyph is ❯, where 0.1.0 drew an unbordered ⟩ row. bin/fm-control.sh exit and relaunch refused every Muse target with "composer state is 'unknown', not proven empty; refusing to type the /exit exit command", so bin/fm-secondmate-restart.sh could restart neither second mate and the captain had to type /exit by hand in each pane. Separately, on 2026-09-18 fm-send reported "doorbell skipped (composer visibly holds pending text)" three times in a row on a Muse pane whose composer showed only Muse's idle placeholder hints ('Type @ to search and insert workspace file paths', '/loop 10m <prompt> schedules a recurring prompt'), leaving inbox records unrung until the mate's own cycle read them. Both are the same defect: the classifier does not know Muse 1.3's empty composer.

## What Changed

- `bin/fm-composer-lib.sh`: adds a `separated`-region opening shape for a horizontal rule that carries an embedded title (e.g. Muse 1.3's `── Voice input (⌥ + v to start) ───…`), so a titled opening rule paired with a solid closing rule around a `❯` glyph row now proves an empty composer instead of reading `unknown`; a titled rule only opens a region and never updates the staleness/closing state. Also adds recognition of a row that is nothing but one of the fleet's idle placeholder hints (extends `FM_COMPOSER_IDLE_RE_DEFAULT` with two Muse tip-catalogue strings) as composer furniture that bounds a bare composer's wrap region, so such rows no longer get swallowed into "pending" and skip fm-send's doorbell.
- `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/references/harness/muse.md`: updates the Muse composer/effort reference rows for 1.3.0-R3401.1 (titled opening rule, `❯` glyph color/luminance including its unfocused recolor back to the tight 0.1.0 margin, idle hint rotation, and the new `max` effort value), while noting every other row is still the 0.1.0 verification.
- `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md`: documents the Muse 1.3 self-update regression and fix, and records a fresh live matrix run (`fm-composer-matrix-live-e2e.test.sh`) showing Claude, Grok, and Muse now classify a real idle composer as `empty`.
- `tests/fm-composer-lib.test.sh` and `tests/fm-composer-matrix-live-e2e.test.sh`: add portable regression coverage for the titled-rule and idle-hint shapes (including a check that replacing the titled rule with ordinary transcript text reverts the same glyph row to `unknown`), and update the live e2e matrix to launch Muse with `--yolo` so its trust dialog doesn't block the composer check.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is a well-scoped, additive classifier extension (new titled-rule shape + idle-hint furniture recognition) with narrow, well-guarded matching logic, live-verified against the real Muse 1.3 binary, and covered by non-vacuous tests using real byte-for-byte captures; tracing the new titled-rule/pi-overlap interaction confirms it correctly resolves to the intended `empty` verdict without weakening any existing harness's staleness or safety checks.

title: fix(spawn): detect Grok folder-trust dialog scrolled above the visible pane
body:
## Intent Make Grok dispatch detect a folder-trust dialog that is present but scrolled outside the visible pane, without mistaking historical scrollback for an active dialog. ## What Changed - Grok dispatch now runs a trust gate after launch. It reads bounded pane history instead of only the visible viewport. The new `bin/fm-grok-trust.sh` classifier calls a complete trust frame active only when Grok's own session surface doesn't follow it. A clipped repaint after the frame doesn't count as proof the dialog was answered. `fm-spawn.sh` reads only what this launch printed: it records a pre-launch baseline and finds the end of the echoed launch line, even when that line wraps. Because of that, dialog text left in an adopted relaunch pane's scrollback isn't mistaken for an active dialog. The gate polls on the same 60 × 0.5s budget as the other harness gates. - Before Grok starts in a tmux pane, `alternate-screen` is turned off through a new `fm_backend_scrollback_retain` backend primitive, which only tmux supports. Without it, a dialog that is scrolled or resized out of view is destroyed instead of kept in history. When the gate refuses a spawn, it now closes the unconfirmed endpoint through a shared `launch_gate_endpoint_cleanup`, which rovo and agy use too. Before, the pane was left parked on the dialog even though the message said it would be closed. - New tests: - Portable cases in `tests/fm-grok-harness.test.sh`: a dialog below the visible slice, dialog text in adopted scrollback, a wrapped launch echo, a scrollback row that is only a fragment of the launch line, and a pane that keeps its history. - A tmux smoke test for scrollback retention. - An opt-in live drift guard against real Grok (`tests/fm-grok-trust-dialog-live-e2e.test.sh`). Docs updated: harness-adapter references, the configuration, scripts and tmux-backend docs, and the runtime-backends verification record. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The suffix tightening closes the round-3 boundary leak (verified by running both the current and previous awk programs against the same input, with opposite results) while all three designed boundary paths still resolve, every unresolved state fails safe toward withholding the no-dialog verdict, and the behavior is pinned by five portable regression cases plus a token-free live drift guard. ## Testing Ran the four targeted suites the diff touches (fm-grok-harness, fm-backend-tmux-smoke, fm-spawn-dispatch-profile, and the live Grok trust-dialog guard) and all passed, with the live guard green on 4 of 4 runs against real grok 1.0.40 where round 2 had reported intermittent failures on its older form. Because passing unit and classifier tests do not show the operator-facing behavior, I additionally drove the real bin/fm-spawn.sh against a real tmux 3.7b server and a real grok 1.0.40 in a throwaway sandbox, tapping the tmux transport so every capture the trust gate actually read is recorded with the pane geometry at that instant: with the dialog rendered at 80x12 and the window then shrunk to 80x5, the gate's deciding read shows the complete frame only in pane history and nothing but a clipped repaint in the viewport, and the spawn refused with its real error and exit 1 while the throwaway trust store confirmed the dialog was still unanswered; the mirror arm, where the same displaced frame is followed by Grok's own session surface, dispatched normally. Two watched-to-fail controls against ephemeral copies of the tree - one restoring only the retired trailing-content rule, one neutering the scrollback-retention primitive - each dispatched a worker into a pane still waiting at the dialog, confirming both halves of the change are load-bearing; my first attempt at the rule mutant was inert and passed, which I caught by verifying the mutant could still produce the right answer before trusting it. The end-user surface here is a terminal pane rather than a browser UI, so the reviewer-visible artifact is the actual tmux pane content rendered as a PNG with the viewport boundary drawn, alongside the raw transcripts. Ephemeral lab trees and tmux servers were removed and the worktree is clean.
Evidence: End-to-end transcript: all four arms (refuse, dispatch, and two watched-to-fail controls) ```text Grok folder-trust dispatch gate - end-to-end evidence real bin/fm-spawn.sh -> real tmux 3.7b (private socket) -> real grok 1.0.40 (eb1a2256660d) [stable] macOS arm64, 2026-09-22 00:55 CDT Every arm uses a throwaway FM_HOME, HOME, GROK_HOME (auth.json copy only) and git project. The dialog is never answered in the refusing arms; the throwaway trust store is checked after each run. ========================================================================= ARM A - shipped code: a dialog present but scrolled OUTSIDE the visible pane ========================================================================= Sequence: fm-spawn creates the task window and launches grok at 80x12; the real dialog renders; the operator window is then shrunk to 80x5, which makes grok repaint a clipped frame and pushes the complete one above the viewport. --- pane facts ------------------------------------------------------- dialog_rendered=1 before_resize history_size=0 size=80x12 alternate_screen_option= off after_resize history_size=12 size=80x5 trusted_folders_toml=absent spawn_exit=1 --- what the operator SEES in the 80x5 pane (tmux capture-pane -S -0) --  fm/grok-e2e-armA worktree /p/v/f/p/4/T/f/armA/wt Grok Build 1.0.40 [stable] --- what the gate READS (tmux capture-pane -S -200) -------------------  fm/grok-e2e-armA worktree /p/v/f/p/4/T/f/armA/wt Do you trust the contents of this directory? /private/var/folders/pq/43bb80gj31x7009tmpvfjcy40000gn/T/fm-grok-e2e-zrjp3W/armA Yes, proceed y No, quit n Grok Build 1.0.40 [stable]  fm/grok-e2e-armA worktree /p/v/f/p/4/T/f/armA/wt Grok Build 1.0.40 [stable] --- fm-spawn.sh output ----------------------------------------------- error: grok stopped at an active project-folder trust dialog; refusing to grant project content and hooks additional execution authority automatically; the unconfirmed endpoint will be closed exit status: 1 RESULT: the dialog is invisible to the operator, still unanswered, and the spawn REFUSED to dispatch a worker into that pane. ========================================================================= ARM C - shipped code: the SAME displaced frame, but already answered ========================================================================= The harness replays the exact rows live grok 1.0.40 painted for the waiting frame and then for the answered session, so the retained scrollback holds a complete dialog frame outside the viewport in this arm too. The only difference from arm A is WHAT FOLLOWS it. --- pane facts ------------------------------------------------------- dialog_rendered=1 before_resize history_size=10 size=80x12 alternate_screen_option= off after_resize history_size=31 size=80x5 trusted_folders_toml=absent spawn_exit=0 --- what the operator SEES ------------------------------------------- ╭────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮ │ ❯ y │ ╰───────────────── Weekly limit left: 0% · Grok 4.7 (high) · always-approve ─╯ Enter:send │ Opt+Enter:newline │ Shift+Tab:mode │ Ctrl+x:shortcuts --- what the gate READS ---------------------------------------------- The default interactive shell is now zsh. '/tmp/fm-abc-x1+deadbeef/launch.s1774000000.12345.6789.sh'`, baseline = [PRIOR-SESSION-TOP, deadbeef, "Tip: prior session", "Weekly limit left: 50%", echo-line], capture = the four prior-session rows with no echo row. The same input against the round-2 program (38aa549) exits 1, the withheld/unknown verdict, so this is a new regression in the unsafe direction rather than a pre-existing gap. I could not exhibit a real grok pane row that collides, which is why this is a warning and not an error - the trigger is a coincidental row whose entire text is a contiguous fragment of a nonce path. The anchor is only needed when the capture window has cut the mark, and in both designed cases the row it must match is a SUFFIX of the literal (verified: `2345.6789.sh'` for the wrapped geometry, `8/launch.s1774000000.12345.6789.sh'` for the cut-window case), so tightening the predicate from substring to suffix preserves both paths and removes the middle-fragment class. 🔧 Fix: anchor Grok launch boundary only on echo tail row ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: docs: reduce always-loaded AGENTS.md context
body:
## Summary

Cut the always-loaded supervisor contract so Firstmate does not re-pay a ~21k-token `AGENTS.md` on every turn.

- Before: **85,400 bytes** (~21,350 tokens at 4 bytes/token; captain-measured ~21,000 tokens on 85,356 bytes on 2026-09-22).
- After: **31,417 bytes** (~7,854 tokens at 4 bytes/token).
- Reduction: **53,983 bytes** (~63%).

Safety boundaries stay in `AGENTS.md`: the five hard rules in priority order, captain-instruction precedence, merge/`yolo` semantics, worktree isolation, unlanded-work protections, away/quiet-mode safety facts, and captain-facing translation rules. Detail that already had another owner was replaced with a pointer; this branch does not change runtime behavior.

**The no-mistakes pipeline did not run on this branch.** The configured gate agent (`acp:cursor`) cannot neutralize `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, and Codex was ruled out, so this ships as a direct PR. Please read it closely.

## Relocations

Each passage left `AGENTS.md` as a short owner pointer. The owner already held the contract; this change does not invent a second copy.

| Relocated from always-loaded `AGENTS.md` | Owner that holds the detail |
| --- | --- |
| Section 2 operational-home file/config/state inventory | `docs/configuration.md` (layout and config schemas) plus each producer script header and `--help` (child fields and mutation) |
| Section 3 session-start digest contents, ordering, lock/bootstrap/queue/network walkthrough | `bin/fm-session-start.sh` header; adapter routing in `docs/sessionstart-nudge.md`; deferred network in `bin/fm-startup-network.sh` |
| Quota-array selection procedure (TOON, gates, `spendPriority`, runway) | `.agents/skills/quota-array-dispatch/SKILL.md` |
| Typed dispatch-resolution result handling | `docs/configuration.md` "Typed dispatch resolution" and `bin/fm-dispatch-resolve.sh` |
| Runtime-backend selection, spawn-capable backends, no silent retry | `docs/configuration.md` "Runtime backend" and `bin/fm-spawn.sh` |
| Dispatch-profile and harness-pin schemas | `docs/configuration.md`; static resolution in `bin/fm-harness.sh`; harness consequences in `harness-adapters` |
| Steer / durable inbox / safe retry | `bin/fm-send.sh` header and `bin/fm-task-inbox-lib.sh` |

title: docs: record verified Pi 0.85.1 effort-level fault with dual-cause explanation
body:
## Intent

Two documentation edits are sitting uncommitted in the primary firstmate copy and need to be landed, corrected to match what was actually reproduced today rather than what was first assumed.

Edit 1, in .agents/skills/harness-adapters/references/harness/pi.md, records that Pi cannot run certain Anthropic models. Edit 2, in docs/configuration.md, refreshes a stale example model id.

What was reproduced on 2026-09-18, on Pi 0.85.1 (the current release), against the anthropic provider with an OAuth credential, using pi -ne so no extension was involved:

- claude-opus-5 returns HTTP 400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Invalid effort level"}} on every request. It fails identically at --thinking low, high, max, and with the flag absent.
- claude-fable-5 returns the same 400.
- claude-sonnet-4-6 succeeds on the same credential with the same command, so the fault is not the account or the credential.
- claude-fable-5-1, claude-sonnet-5, claude-opus-4-5 and claude-sonnet-4-5 return HTTP 404 not_found_error on that account, so their behaviour under this fault is untested.

The cause, read from Pi's own source at packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts in buildParams, on both the main branch and the v0.85.1 tag:

- claude-opus-5 carries supportsMidConvoEffort: true in Pi's shipped catalog, so it takes the branch that hardcodes params.output_config = { effort: "high" } and ignores the requested level entirely.
- claude-fable-5 does NOT carry supportsMidConvoEffort. It carries forceAdaptiveThinking: true and fails through the neighbouring branch, which sets params.output_config = { effort: options.effort }.

So the single-cause wording in the uncommitted edit is wrong: two different code paths produce the same 400, and the hardcoded-high explanation covers claude-opus-5 only.

The verified workaround is claude-sonnet-4-6.

## What Changed

- Updated `pi.md` to replace the single-cause wording for the Pi 0.85.1 `Invalid effort level` fault with a precise dual-cause explanation: `claude-opus-5` fails because `buildParams` hardcodes `output_config = { effort: "high" }` via `supportsMidConvoEffort: true`, while `claude-fable-5` fails through the neighbouring branch that forwards `output_config = { effort: options.effort }` due to `forceAdaptiveThinking: true`.
- Expanded the list of models with untested behaviour under the fault from one to four: `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-sonnet-5`, `claude-opus-4-5`, and `claude-sonnet-4-5` all return HTTP 404 on the tested account and are therefore excluded from the confirmed failure set.
- Updated the example provider-qualified model ID in `docs/configuration.md` from the stale `claude-sonnet-4-5` to the current `claude-sonnet-4-6`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Both documentation edits are accurate to the stated reproduction, the fix-round correctly applied the prescribed 404-model sentence, and no logic or behavior is changed.

## Testing

Both documentation files verified by direct inspection. The pi.md note correctly records two distinct failure paths (supportsMidConvoEffort vs forceAdaptiveThinking), names claude-sonnet-4-6 as the workaround, and lists all four HTTP-404 models per the review decision. The configuration.md example model ID is updated. No live product surface exists for this documentation-only change.

- Live validation: ⚠️ no-surface - 0 of 3 scenarios driven live against the product

title: fix: distinguish rejected state-check diagnostics
body:
## Intent Start the queued work now: make a rejected state-check notification distinguish a real trust failure from a malformed record or transient re-arm state. The current single message conflates a possible security event with a broken merge notification and gives the operator no reliable next action. ## What Changed - Classify rejected state checks as authentication failures, malformed or unsupported registrations, or incomplete PR poll publications, with a distinct operator action for each case. - Serialize PR metadata and poll artifact publication so transient re-arm states do not produce false trust alerts, and suppress repeated unchanged rejection notifications without starving other diagnostics. - Expand security regression coverage for rejection classification, notification behavior, and concurrent PR re-arming. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The diagnostic classification and re-arm serialization are well bounded, but the change also introduces an unrequested persistent suppression mechanism that alters operator notification behavior. ## Testing Two isolated real-watcher runs produced reviewer-visible trust-failure and malformed-record notifications. The focused regression transcript covered the concurrent PR re-arm and notification-starvation boundaries, but those scenarios were not driven against the live product. No Herdr lab was used because the affected surface is the local watcher notification path, not a Herdr lifecycle path. - Live validation: ✅ go - 2 of 4 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A check changed after registration is refused as a real authentication failure | ✅ pass | live | Live tampered-check notification shows `authentication failed, not run` and gives the operator the next action; the rejected script's `SHOULD_NOT_RUN` output was absent. | | An unsupported trust record receives a distinct malformed-record diagnosis | ✅ pass | live | Live unsupported-record notification shows `malformed or unsupported registration, not run`, recommends inspecting the producer/version or unregistering it, and does not claim an authentication failur… | | An ordinary concurrent PR re-arm waits for matched publication without a false security alert | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload recorded only a deterministic repository regression using an isolated lock holder and stub forge, not a live product result; live validation would require authority to create or muta… | | A persistent rejected check does not starve another actionable operator signal | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload recorded only a repository test-harness result with controlled persisted state and acknowledgement timing, not a live fleet result. |

a repeat identical merged poll for an already-notified task is absorbed, never queued as a main-blocking row ok - a failed upward merge report keeps its poll armed for repair and retry ok - staged self-merge and poll interleavings are never silent ok - queued merges retain their away authority after captain return ok - poll distinguishes attended authorization from external landing ok - accepted merge authority refuses rebound task metadata ok - accepted merge authority persists under the lifecycle lock ok - teardown cannot race merged-poll authority consumption ok - poll retirement preserves a replacement authority record ok - a merge detected by the poll is reported upward from a secondmate home exactly once ok - a different merged PR for the same task gets its own first notification ok - merged poll retirement preserves every persistent secondmate lifecycle artifact ok - queue, receipt, and every fixed-path removal crash point recover without loss or repeated execution ok - open/red, closed-unmerged, malformed, and forge errors remain armed until an exact merged transition ok - replacement, nonterminal, tampered, and custom results receive no deletion authority ok - queue failure and untrusted receipts preserve canonical poll evidence ok - GitHub and GitLab exact merged results share one retirement path ok - PR and teardown entrypoints reject invalid arguments before every side effect ok - arming refuses a draft pull request, naming it, and arms a ready or unreadable one ok - valid direct and merge flows record exact metadata and reject multiline head metadata ok - rejected metacharacter bytes remain inert at generation and watcher time ok - static poll is silent except for one merged line and remains watcher-bounded ok - interrupted atomic preparation cleans private temporaries and publishes nothing ok - concurrent watchers observe only complete private poll publications ok - poll publication paths refuse symlinks and directories ok - live poll and custom-check artifacts require private single-link files ok - a poll armed before a volume renumber is re-recorded under the control lock and keeps detecting merges ok - a renumbered registration is never re-recorded around a tampered artifact: swapped-check altered-check swapped-sidecar altered-sidecar altered-template-hash wrong-mode hardlinked-check split-device (foreign-device not exercisable on Darwin), or a pending retirement ok - direct re-arm publication waits without replacing an armed poll ok - device re-record publication waits without rewriting its registration ok - post-rename poll validation faults revoke both names and allow a clean retry ok - bootstrap does not rewrite unauthenticated checks or emit retired migration diagnostics ok - watcher diagnostics distinguish malformed, unsupported, and authentication failures ok - an unchanged rejected check does not starve a distinct actionable diagnostic ok - ordinary PR re-arm publishes one matched generation without a false trust alert ok - watcher signals promptly stop custom checks and clean private state ok - returned custom check descendants are drained on installed and fallback timeout paths ok - title: feat(bin): nest same-project Herdr task spaces under their home
body:
## Intent In the Herdr sidebar the firstmate space and the crewmate task spaces are aligned in parallel, and they should have a different level view: each task space should read as a level below the home space it belongs to instead of sitting beside it as a sibling. ## What Changed - Same-project tasks now preallocate their durable Treehouse checkout and open it via `herdr worktree open --workspace `, so the task presentation workspace renders as a linked child one level below its owning home instead of a sibling; foreign-project tasks keep the established top-level disposable workspace path. - Projection create and recovery prove the exact response and `worktree list` shape (fresh, not-already-open linked checkout whose workspace, tab, pane, checkout path, and source-parent listing agree), and carry a recorded durable checkout across recovery only when the journal/path proof and the durable slot-owner claim both name the recovering task; aborted recovery retains the lease and task record rather than allocating or force-returning a second checkout. - Teardown binds the projected endpoint to its journal and closes the exact pane under the session lock before any process reap or checkout return can implicitly remove the linked workspace, and docs/tests were extended for nested projection, durable-checkout recovery, and the foreign-project top-level guarantee. ## Risk Assessment ⚠️ Medium: The change is well-tested and internally consistent with the authorized decisions, but it modifies delicate Herdr spawn/recovery/teardown lifecycle code whose only end-to-end validation is a live-Herdr suite recorded as stale, so it warrants cautious, sequential-lane merge rather than being treated as trivial. ## Testing Drove the nesting change live against real Herdr 0.9.1 in throwaway fm-lab-* sessions through bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh. The full real-Herdr presentation and launcher-workspace e2e suites passed, covering fresh same-project nesting, workspace ordering, focus preservation, foreign-project top-level fallback, durable-checkout recovery across closed/restarted spaces, the adversarial other-task slot-claim case, aborted carried-recovery record/lease retention (including a backlog-dispatch failure), and nested teardown. A separate manual lab run produced a direct API transcript: worktree list on the home workspace reports the home source plus the task's linked Treehouse checkout with open_workspace_id set to the task workspace, the task workspace is exactly one position after its home, the v2 journal binds parent_workspace_id to the home, and teardown returns the checkout and removes the child workspace. No screenshots/GIFs were produced because the Herdr sidebar is a terminal TUI and the supported lab viewer deliberately drains its pty; the runbook requires lab mechanics to stay owned by bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh, so the rendered surface is evidenced through the socket-API structure that drives the sidebar hierarchy. One setup note: the launcher e2e teardown resolves the Treehouse project lock against $FM_HOME/state with FM_HOME defaulting to the repo root, so a fresh worktree needs an empty `state/` directory; creating it (then removing it) let the suite pass. That block is unchanged by this change and is not a regression. - Live validation: ✅ go - 9 of 9 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Launch a same-project crewmate from a home workspace and see its task space nested one level below that home as a real linked-worktree child, not beside it as a sibling | ✅ pass | live | sidebar-nesting-live.txt: `worktree list --workspace w1` reports source w1 plus the Treehouse checkout as a linked worktree with open_workspace_id=w2;
