title: fix(bin): stop the ship project-memory step from renaming an existing CLAUDE.md
body:
## Intent Arreglar la instruccion de memoria del proyecto que genera el brief, porque en cada tarea de ws3 dispara un renombre de CLAUDE.md a AGENTS.md que nadie pidio y que cuesta una ronda de review. Paso CINCO veces seguidas, en cinco tareas distintas de ws3: el trabajador corre el paso de memoria del proyecto, el archivo de instrucciones del repositorio queda renombrado, y el review lo marca como componente no pedido. Las cinco veces la decision fue la misma: sacarlo del cambio, que va en su propio PR. O sea que el costo no es del trabajador ni del revisor: es de la instruccion. La quinta vez el revisor aporto la evidencia que faltaba para entender por que importa: el renombre dejo DOS punteros colgados en ws3 —`TODO.md:13` ("Convencion documentada en CLAUDE.md") y `CONTEXT.md:74` ("Ver ... en `CLAUDE.md`")— que despues del renombre apuntan al stub de dos lineas en vez de al contenido. Eso es exactamente por que la migracion necesita su propio cambio: tiene referencias cruzadas que actualizar, y ninguna tarea de feature las va a mirar. El mecanismo, verificado: `bin/fm-brief.sh` linea 508 instruye correr `bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh .` cuando ya existe `AGENTS.md` O `CLAUDE.md`. Y ese script, segun su propio encabezado, "promotes a real CLAUDE.md file when it is the only file present". Entonces en cualquier repositorio que tenga CLAUDE.md y no AGENTS.md —que es el caso de ws3— la instruccion produce el renombre como efecto colateral de una tarea que solo queria anotar conocimiento. Lo que la tarea de feature necesita es anotar conocimiento durable en el archivo de instrucciones que el repositorio YA tiene. No necesita, ni pidio, cambiar cual es ese archivo. ## What Changed - `bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh` gains a `--no-promote` flag (with argument parsing reworked to accept flags before the directory): when a real non-pointer `CLAUDE.md` is the project's only memory file, it now leaves the worktree untouched, reports `CLAUDE.md` as the file to record knowledge in, and exits 0. Every other path — bare project, existing `AGENTS.md`, pointer handling, refusals — is unchanged. - `bin/fm-brief.sh` invokes the helper with `--no-promote` in the ship project-memory section and rewords the contract: record knowledge in whichever memory file the helper leaves in place, never switch which file the project uses as a side effect, and treat the self-governance requirement as scoped to `AGENTS.md` (a `CLAUDE.md` left in place owes no such section). - Docs and memory-routing wording in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/scripts.md`, and `.agents/skills/stow/SKILL.md` now say "the project's memory file" (`AGENTS.md` unless the project already uses `CLAUDE.md`); tests cover the `--no-promote` paths plus an end-to-end check that running the command extracted from a generated brief leaves an existing `CLAUDE.md` byte-identical while still establishing `AGENTS.md` in a bare project; `.atl/` is added to `.gitignore`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is well-bounded and opt-in: --no-promote suppresses exactly one branch of fm-ensure-agents-md.sh, every other path is byte-identical, the previously recurring .atl artifacts are verified untracked and ignored, docs and the stow skill were updated consistently, and the new coverage executes the real command extracted from a generated brief instead of asserting on source text. ## Testing I ran the two targeted behavior suites for the changed scripts (both fully green), then drove the product by hand. The key evidence is a before/after on the same ws3-shaped fixture: the base-commit helper prints `promoted: moved CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md` and leaves the `TODO.md` and `CONTEXT.md` CLAUDE.md references resolving to the two-line stub, while the branch helper invoked exactly as the new brief invokes it prints `kept: CLAUDE.md is this project's agent memory file ...` and leaves the file untouched. I also generated a real ship brief, pulled the project-memory command straight out of the rendered Markdown, and ran it — CLAUDE.md stayed byte-identical and no AGENTS.md appeared. Adversarial runs confirmed the flag suppresses only the rename: skeleton creation, pointer installation, and the self-governance section on a pre-existing AGENTS.md all still happen, and bad arguments or conflicting files still exit 1. This change has no graphical surface; the user-facing artifact is the generated brief text, which I captured as a rendered Markdown excerpt. Worktree left clean and the temporary lab removed. - Live validation: ✅ go - 8 of 8 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A crewmate follows the ship brief's project-memory step in a CLAUDE.md-only project and the instruction file is not renamed | ✅ pass | live | Generated a real brief with `bin/fm-brief.sh ws3-live-demo some-proj --mode no-mistakes`, extracted `fm-ensure-agents-md.sh --no-promote .` from the rendered Markdown, ran it: exit 0, CLAUDE.md byte-i… | | Regression reproduction: the same step on the base commit does rename CLAUDE.md and strands its cross-references | ✅ pass | live | ws3-claude-md-before-after.txt — base helper prints `promoted: moved CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md`, CLAUDE.md becomes the two-line stub, and TODO.md:3 / CONTEXT.md:1 still say "CLAUDE.md" | | Repeating the memory step across consecutive tasks never converges on a rename | ✅ pass | live | `bash tests/fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh` — "--no-promote stays a no-op across repeated runs" (three consecutive runs, CLAUDE.md cksum unchanged, no AGENTS.md) | | A project with no memory file still gets AGENTS.md plus the CLAUDE.md pointer under the new flag | ✅ pass | live | `bash tests/fm-brief.test.sh` — "the ship memory step still establishes memory for a bare project"; plus live run on a canonical-pointer-only fixture printing `created: AGENTS.md and kept CLAUDE.md @A… | | Adversarial: --no-promote does not silently skip the self-governance section on a pre-existing real AGENTS.md | ✅ pass | live | no-promote-scope-is-only-the-rename.txt — `updated: added ## Maintaining this file to AGENTS.md and wrote CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md pointer`, section count 1, pointer written | | Adversarial: the deliberate CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md migration is still available when the flag is omitted | ✅ pass | live | `bash tests/fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh` — "promotion still runs when the flag is omitted" (content carried into AGENTS.md, canonical pointer restored) | | Adversarial: malformed invocations fail loudly instead of being read as a directory or silently ignored | ✅ pass | live | adversarial-arg-and-guard-paths.txt — `--promote-everything` exit 1 with usage, two directories exit 1, flag after directory accepted (exit 0, no rename), real AGENTS.md+CLAUDE.md conflict exit 1, mis… | | The new .gitignore rule actually causes git to ignore the generated .atl artifacts | ✅ pass | live | `git check-ignore -v .atl/skill-registry.md` → `.gitignore:16:.atl/` exit 0; `git ls-files .atl` returns nothing |
Evidence: ws3-shaped project: rename before the fix vs preserved after it Source: [ws3-shaped project: rename before the fix vs preserved after it](https://github.com/alejandromaier/firstmate/blob/7b67d4aeacd2fcb68d5e6dd70372695baf86d9ef/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-brief-memoria-proyecto-r5/ws3-claude-md-before-after.txt) ```text === ws3-shaped project BEFORE the fix (base commit 6f0f139 helper, no flag) === $ ls CLAUDE.md CONTEXT.md TODO.md $ fm-ensure-agents-md.sh . promoted: moved CLAUDE.md to AGENTS.md and wrote CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md pointer in /private/tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/before $ ls AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md CONTEXT.md TODO.md --- CLAUDE.md is now the stub the cross-references point at: @AGENTS.md --- dangling pointers left behind: /tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/before/CONTEXT.md:1:Ver la convencion en `CLAUDE.md` /tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/before/TODO.md:3:Convencion documentada en CLAUDE.md === same project AFTER the fix (branch helper, as the brief now invokes it) === $ ls CLAUDE.md CONTEXT.md TODO.md $ fm-ensure-agents-md.sh --no-promote . kept: CLAUDE.md is this project's agent memory file in /private/tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/after; record durable knowledge there and migrate it to AGENTS.md as its own change exit=0 $ ls CLAUDE.md CONTEXT.md TODO.md --- CLAUDE.md content is untouched, so TODO.md: and CONTEXT.md still resolve: # ws3 agent memory ## Conventions Run the suite with `make test`. ```
Evidence: Rendered 'Project memory' section of a real generated ship brief Source: [Rendered 'Project memory' section of a real generated ship brief](https://github.com/alejandromaier/firstmate/blob/7b67d4aeacd2fcb68d5e6dd70372695baf86d9ef/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-brief-memoria-proyecto-r5/ship-brief-project-memory-section.md) ```text === Rendered 'Project memory' section of a real ship brief (fm-brief.sh ws3-live-demo --mode no-mistakes) === # Project memory If `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` already exists, or if this task produced durable project-intrinsic knowledge, run `~/.no-mistakes/worktrees/087e5452ff4f/01M34EWGDNRE25KQBG3EQSP2HD/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh --no-promote .` in the worktree. Record the knowledge in whichever memory file that command leaves in place, and never change which file this project uses as a side effect of this task; switching it is its own separate change. Record only project knowledge useful to almost every future session. For anything the codebase already shows, prefer a pointer to the authoritative file, command, or doc over copying the detail. If you touch a project `AGENTS.md`, follow `~/.no-mistakes/worktrees/087e5452ff4f/01M34EWGDNRE25KQBG3EQSP2HD/bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh`'s self-governance contract in the same pass; a `CLAUDE.md` the helper left in place owes no self-governance section. Keep it proportionate: skip memory-file edits entirely for trivial tasks that produced no durable project knowledge. # Definition of done Delivery contract: mode=no-mistakes The task is complete only when committed on your branch. When you believe it is complete, append `done [at=]: {summary}` to the status file and stop. Firstmate will then instruct you to run /no-mistakes to validate and ship a PR. ```
Evidence: Adversarial argument and guard paths with exit codes Source: [Adversarial argument and guard paths with exit codes](https://github.com/alejandromaier/firstmate/blob/7b67d4aeacd2fcb68d5e6dd70372695baf86d9ef/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-brief-memoria-proyecto-r5/adversarial-arg-and-guard-paths.txt) ```text === adversarial: argument-boundary and guard paths under --no-promote (exit codes) === $ fm-ensure-agents-md.sh --promote-everything /tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/adv usage: fm-ensure-agents-md.sh [--no-promote] [repo-or-worktree-dir] --no-promote leaves a real non-pointer CLAUDE.md in place as the project's exit=1 $ fm-ensure-agents-md.sh --no-promote /tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/adv /tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/adv usage: fm-ensure-agents-md.sh [--no-promote] [repo-or-worktree-dir] --no-promote leaves a real non-pointer CLAUDE.md in place as the project's exit=1 $ fm-ensure-agents-md.sh /tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/adv2 --no-promote kept: CLAUDE.md is this project's agent memory file in /private/tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/adv2; record durable knowledge there and migrate it to AGENTS.md as its own change exit=0 $ fm-ensure-agents-md.sh --no-promote /tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/adv3 conflict: both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are real files in /private/tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/adv3; reconcile them manually exit=1 $ fm-ensure-agents-md.sh --no-promote /tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/does-not-exist error: not a directory: /tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/does-not-exist exit=1 ```
Evidence: --no-promote suppresses only the rename (AGENTS.md and pointer paths intact) Source: [--no-promote suppresses only the rename (AGENTS.md and pointer paths intact)](https://github.com/alejandromaier/firstmate/blob/7b67d4aeacd2fcb68d5e6dd70372695baf86d9ef/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-brief-memoria-proyecto-r5/no-promote-scope-is-only-the-rename.txt) ```text === --no-promote must NOT suppress anything except the CLAUDE.md-only rename === $ fm-ensure-agents-md.sh --no-promote updated: added ## Maintaining this file to AGENTS.md and wrote CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md pointer in /private/tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/agents-existing exit=0 AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md --- self-governance section present in the pre-existing AGENTS.md: 1 --- CLAUDE.md pointer written: @AGENTS.md === canonical CLAUDE.md pointer with no AGENTS.md: still completed under --no-promote === created: AGENTS.md and kept CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md pointer in /private/tmp/fm-ws3-lab.aqB1uF/pointer-only exit=0 AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md ```
Evidence: Brief-extracted command run in a CLAUDE.md-only repo ```text extracted command: .../bin/fm-ensure-agents-md.sh --no-promote . kept: CLAUDE.md is this project's agent memory file in /private/tmp/.../brief-follow; record durable knowledge there and migrate it to AGENTS.md as its own change exit=0 CLAUDE.md CLAUDE.md byte-identical: PASS no AGENTS.md created: PASS ```

The intent is scoped to one thing - the brief's project-memory step must stop renaming an existing CLAUDE.md - and that is fully satisfied by the `--no-promote` case plus the brief change at bin/fm-brief.sh:556. Without this branch the behavior is still safe: an unknown or mistyped flag falls into the `*)` case, becomes DIR, and the existing `[ -d "$DIR" ]` guard exits non-zero with `error: not a directory: --promote-everything`, so no promotion and no rename can occur. The branch therefore buys a clearer message, not a new guarantee, and it brings its own test (tests/fm-ensure-agents-md.test.sh:512-522) as ongoing surface. title: fix: match Pi Codex home candidates to their quota row
body:
## Intent Both Codex accounts are signed in through Pi, and quota-axi reports both with real numbers under accountKey codex-home and accountKey openai-codex-work. A dispatch candidate written as harness `pi` with model `openai-codex/` still comes back eligible but unranked, with "provider codex has no quota row for account openai-codex", so the account that still has quota never competes for a task. Done means a Pi candidate whose model begins `openai-codex/` is ranked instead of skipped, proven by a regression test that fails before the change and passes after. The binding rule, in order: when the snapshot has a row keyed exactly `openai-codex`, that candidate uses that row; when it does not, the candidate uses the codex-home row; when the snapshot has neither row, the candidate stays unranked exactly as it is today. Every other lane keeps the behavior it has today: `codex-native/...` and the `codex` harness stay on codex-home, `openai-codex-work` stays on its own row, schema 5 snapshots keep their single-row behavior, and non-Codex lanes are untouched. Out of scope: quota-axi itself, the dispatch profiles in `config/crew-dispatch.json`, and how candidates are compared or chosen once their rows are found. in https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/pull/5303 make it test we never do the minimum if its possible to do better them minum The three rows the PR's live evidence left untested, each to be tested: a snapshot supplying both an exact `openai-codex` row and a `codex-home` row, where the exact row wins even when exhausted; a snapshot supplying neither named row, where the Pi home candidate stays eligible but unranked; and a schema-5 snapshot, where candidates keep single-provider-row behavior. ## What Changed - Match Pi `openai-codex/` candidates to their exact schema-6 account row, then `codex-home`; keep them eligible but unranked when neither exists. - Add regression coverage for fallback ranking, exhausted exact-row precedence, missing named rows, sibling/native accounts, and schema-5 matching. - Document the account lookup order and unchanged `default` fallback for other lanes. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The bounded lookup change at bin/fm-quota-axi-lib.sh:41 preserves exact-row precedence, sibling-account behavior, and schema-5 compatibility. ## Testing Five real resolver/API scenarios passed using the explicitly authorized quota snapshot stub and separate scratch homes. CLI transcripts capture all results; the regression failed before the change and passed after. Both targeted suites passed after correcting locale and incomplete-fixture setup. - Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Pi openai-codex uses codex-home when its exact row is absent and wins over an exhausted sibling account | ✅ pass | live | quota-validation.log: home-fallback | | An exhausted exact openai-codex row blocks the candidate despite healthy codex-home and default rows | ✅ pass | live | quota-validation.log: exact-exhausted | | Missing both named rows leaves Pi home eligible but unranked despite a healthy default row | ✅ pass | live | quota-validation.log: neither-named | | Schema 5 gives every Codex candidate the same provider row and preserves tie handling | ✅ pass | live | quota-validation.log: schema5 | | Native Codex, Pi codex-native, sibling Codex account, and Claude retain their account mappings | ✅ pass | live | quota-validation.log: other-lanes | Evidence logs that printed the real sibling account key were dropped from this body (account key redacted). ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

title: fix(bin): let fm-control exit stop idle agy workers
body:
## Intent Make it possible to stop an agy worker through the ordinary control plane, then ship the fix as a pull request. Context this ask refers to. `bin/fm-control.sh:539-549` refuses the `exit` verb unless `fm_backend_composer_state` classifies the worker's composer as `empty`, because typing the harness's exit command into a composer holding text would concatenate onto that text. agy's composer is a borderless bare `>` row, which the shared classifier reads as `unknown` and never as `empty`. That is recorded as structural in `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/references/harness/agy.md` under "Composer", not as a bug to fix in the classifier. The consequence, hit live on 2026-09-22 during task customeros-context-fix: `bin/fm-control.sh exit` fails on every agy worker, an interrupt beforehand does not change the verdict, and a finished agy worker therefore stays alive emitting `stale:` wakes until its whole task is torn down. Because a ship task waiting for a merge is deliberately kept alive until landing is confirmed, that is a supervision-noise loop with no supported way out. This is not a permission or environment problem. The refusal comes from firstmate's own guard. One direction, established before the task was written and not binding on the design: agy exposes a recovery-grade native agent state on the herdr backend through `fm_backend_agent_state` (`bin/fm-backend.sh:953`), and `agy.md` records that agy's steer path already resolves the same unprovable-composer problem by trusting native agent state and the delivery footer instead of composer emptiness, calling that the cursor precedent. ## What Changed - Teach the shared separator-pair classifier to prove an identity-gated idle/done agy composer empty (`>` between solid `─` rules), while `> draft` stays pending and a bare `>` outside a pair stays unknown under the dead-shell rule. - Extend the tmux foreground-process identity probe to live `agy` processes so that empty proof is available on both herdr and tmux, matching the existing pi separator-pair path. - Update agy/control/composer docs and pin the contract in composer-lib and fm-control tests (idle `/quit` exit, pending-draft refusal, non-agy unproven composers still refused). ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a bounded extension of the existing identity-plus-separator proof from pi to agy, still fail-closed on drafts, working state, missing identity, and a bare dead-shell `>`. ## Testing Targeted composer and control tests passed, then a throwaway Herdr lab spawned a real agy 1.2.8 scout. The idle separator-pair composer classified empty, a typed draft made exit refuse without sending /quit, a working turn classified unknown rather than empty, and `fm-control exit` interrupted and stopped the worker; the next exit reported already-stopped. Default Herdr was left running and untouched. - Live validation: ✅ go - 4 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | An idle agy worker's separator-pair composer reads empty so ordinary exit is allowed | ✅ pass | live | ~/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M34T60WZY39D5C720ZJP0SG6/idle-composer.txt and idle-pane.txt | | fm-control exit refuses a visible agy draft and does not type /quit | ✅ pass | live | ~/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M34T60WZY39D5C720ZJP0SG6/pending-exit.txt | | A working agy turn does not classify empty, then fm-control exit interrupts and stops the worker | ✅ pass | live | ~/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M34T60WZY39D5C720ZJP0SG6/busy-exit.txt | | A second exit on the stopped agy worker reports already-stopped | ✅ pass | live | ~/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M34T60WZY39D5C720ZJP0SG6/second-exit.txt | | A bare shell glyph outside a separator pair stays unknown under the dead-shell rule | ⏸️ untested | no | The post-stop pane still showed the leftover agy separator pair plus a shell prompt, so a bare-glyph-only dead shell was not isolated on the live TUI. |

title: fix(bin): label fresh herdr worker panes with task id and project at spawn
body:
## Intent

The captain runs multiple agents/tasks at once under the herdr backend and
cannot tell them apart in herdr's own on-screen tab bar: every freshly
spawned Claude Code worker pane shows the generic terminal title "Claude
Code" (Claude Code's own OSC title before it has generated a topic-specific
one), while the herdr tab itself does carry a static `fm-<task-id>` label
that isn't what's visually prominent. The captain's own long-running
interactive sessions eventually get a descriptive title from Claude Code
itself, but a fresh worker does not have that yet when it matters most (right
after spawn). The ask: every future worker should be visibly distinguishable
in herdr's tab bar immediately at launch, not only after it happens to earn
its own descriptive title later.
As an immediate one-off mitigation this session already ran
`herdr pane rename <pane_id> "<task-id> (<short description>)"` by hand for
one running task; this task is the durable fix so that stops being manual.

## What Changed
- Added `herdr_pane_rename()` to `bin/fm-spawn.sh`, which calls `herdr pane rename` (via `fm_backend_herdr_cli` when available, falling back to the `herdr` CLI directly) to label a freshly spawned pane as `<task-id> (<project>)`, logging a warning on failure without aborting the spawn.
- Wired this rename into both herdr spawn call sites in `bin/fm-spawn.sh`, applied only when `KIND` is `ship` or `scout` so secondmate task panes are left unlabeled.
- Documented the new behavior in `docs/herdr-backend.md`.
- Extended `tests/fm-backend-herdr-launcher-workspace-e2e.test.sh` and `tests/fm-backend-herdr-workspace-per-home-e2e.test.sh` with pane-label assertions covering the unique-label path, the presentation-projection path, primary/secondmate/secondmate-shaped-home crewmate spawns, and confirming secondmate task panes stay unlabeled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Change is small and well-bounded: a new helper renames only ship/scout herdr panes at the two/three herdr spawn call sites (fresh spawn and rebind-recreate), correctly excludes secondmate, fails open with a stderr warning on rename failure without aborting the spawn, and is covered by real e2e tests that assert observable pane-label state via `herdr pane get` rather than source pattern matching.

## Testing

Environment is unchanged from the two prior declined test rounds: `herdr session list --json` still reports the default session as running:false, so bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh's fleet-state tripwire still refuses to provision an isolated fm-lab-* session, and starting/touching the default session is explicitly forbidden by the live-validation runbook. No scenario in this change could be driven live; the two real-herdr e2e tests that already assert the exact pane-label behavior (label_of_pane / herdr pane get assertions added to fm-backend-herdr-launcher-workspace-e2e.test.sh and fm-backend-herdr-workspace-per-home-e2e.test.sh) remain the correct live-validation vehicle once a lab session can be provisioned, but that precondition is out of this phase's control and was already surfaced as a warning finding in rounds 1 and 2 and declined by the user. Since nothing about this blocker or the code under test changed this round, it is not re-reported as a new finding.

- Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 0 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh ship/scout worker pane is labeled `<task-id> (<project>)` immediately at spawn, before it earns its own OSC title | ⏸️ untested | no | bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh's fleet-state tripwire requires the default Herdr session to report running:true (herdr session list --json shows running:false); starting the default session is forbidden by the r… |
| Crewmate pane spawned from a primary- or secondmate-shaped home is labeled `<task-id> (<project>)` | ⏸️ untested | no | same fleet-state tripwire blocker as above |
| Adversarial: a --secondmate task pane must NOT receive the ship/scout label (KIND gating boundary) | ⏸️ untested | no | same fleet-state tripwire blocker as above |

title: fix(bin): fold whole-file open decisions in one awk pass to stay under the watcher grace
body:
## Intent Fix the fleet watcher so one poll no longer takes longer than its own 300-second heartbeat grace on a home with a large status log, which today makes the watcher report itself as down and every automatic re-arm fail while it is in fact delivering wakes. Established cause (investigation report at ~/projects/firstmate/data/fm-watch-poll-over-grace/report.md, reproduced on the live home on 2026-09-22): the whole-file open-decision fold in bin/fm-classify-lib.sh - status_open_decisions and _fm_status_open_decision_origins, built on the per-line subshell loop in _fm_decision_fold_line - is O(n*k) and runs on the watcher's hot path (bin/fm-watch.sh signal_files_actionable -> status_span_first_actionable_record) and in bin/fm-crew-state.sh (status_current_line), bin/fm-home-summary-refresh.sh and bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh. On a 4455-line status log with 132 still-open decisions the fold costs 40 to 80 seconds in isolation and 300 to 500 seconds under the box's real load, so the beacon (touched once per cycle at bin/fm-watch.sh:2309) goes stale. The identical open-set is computed in 0.03 seconds by the existing bounded incremental fold (status_open_decisions_incremental / scan_open_decisions_incremental, bin/fm-classify-lib.sh:913 and following), which only the wake-drain path uses. The defect predates the a09090d..6f0f139 update. ## What Changed - Added `_fm_open_decisions_awk`, a single-pass awk restatement of the `_fm_decision_fold_line` open/resolved rule, and routed the two whole-file readers (`status_open_decisions` and `_fm_status_open_decision_origins`) through it, replacing the per-line subshell fold whose O(n*k) cost on a large status log grew past the watcher's 300s heartbeat grace and made the still-alive watcher report itself down. - Reimplemented `_fm_status_open_decision_origins` on the new awk "origins" mode and removed the now-unused `_fm_decision_origin_drop` helper; the bash `_fm_decision_fold_line` rule stays the owner of the bounded incremental fold and `status_key_closing_verb`. - Added `tests/fm-open-decisions-fold.test.sh`, which pins the awk fold byte-for-byte against the historical bash whole-file loop across documented line shapes and a large high-open-count log, and demonstrates the awk fold's speed against the old per-line cost. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A hot-path fold rewrite, but it is a faithful byte-for-byte awk restatement of the still-present bash rule, pinned by a behavioral differential test over documented shapes and a large log, and my manual trace of every helper found no divergence. ## Testing See testing_summary field above. - Live validation: ✅ go - 4 of 4 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | The awk fold produces byte-for-byte the same open-set and origins as the old per-line bash rule across every documented decision shape (keyed/unkeyed, colon-first, reopened, resolved, captain-held, sh… | ✅ pass | live | `bash tests/fm-open-decisions-fold.test.sh` assert_equiv over documented shapes, empty/absent log, and large high-open log | | The whole-file awk fold and the incremental cursor-backed bash fold agree on what is open, so the two consumption strategies never drift | ✅ pass | live | `bash tests/fm-classify-decision-key.test.sh` ('incremental fold matches the full fold across appends'), `bash tests/fm-classify-corr-token.test.sh` ('cursor-backed and whole-file fold agree'), `bash… | | The watcher signal hot path (signal_files_actionable -> status_span_first_actionable_record, using _fm_status_open_decision_origins) still surfaces buried open decisions and OPEN DECISIONS fold cases… | ✅ pass | live | `bash tests/fm-watch-triage.test.sh` 46 assertions including the 'close after OPEN DECISIONS fold' cases; `bash tests/fm-wake-drain-open-decisions.test.sh` fleet-wide scan | | One fold of a large status log completes fast enough that a watcher poll stays under its 300s heartbeat grace (the reported defect: poll exceeds grace, beacon goes stale, watcher reports itself down) | ✅ pass | live | Manual repro on identical 4455-line/2005-open log: new fold 0.54s (open) / 0.64s (origins) vs old bash fold running >7 min past the 300s grace; plus fold-test bounds (5000-line under 10s; one bash fol… |
Evidence: open-decisions fold: awk-vs-bash equivalence + performance Source: [open-decisions fold: awk-vs-bash equivalence + performance](https://github.com/karotkriss/firstmate/blob/52b100fbcb39774de74abe1802c25830c2381d38/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-watch-incremental-decision-fold/open-decisions-fold-test.txt) ok - the awk fold matches the bash rule byte for byte on every documented shape ok - the awk fold matches on an empty log and yields nothing for an absent one ok - the awk fold matches the bash rule on a 127-open, 180-line log ok - the awk fold holds a 5000-line log under the 10s bound (open=2.760s, origins=3.331s) ok - one per-line bash fold (30.927s) outweighs 30 awk folds (0.400s) ```text === fm-open-decisions-fold.test.sh (awk-vs-bash equivalence + performance) === ok - the awk fold matches the bash rule byte for byte on every documented shape ok - the awk fold matches on an empty log and yields nothing for an absent one ok - the awk fold matches the bash rule on a 127-open, 180-line log ok - the awk fold holds a 5000-line log under the 10s bound (open=2.760s, origins=3.331s) ok - one per-line bash fold (30.927s) outweighs 30 awk folds (0.400s) ```
Evidence: repro of intent scenario: 4455-line/2005-open poll timing (old vs new) Source: [repro of intent scenario: 4455-line/2005-open poll timing (old vs new)](https://github.com/karotkriss/firstmate/blob/52b100fbcb39774de74abe1802c25830c2381d38/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-watch-incremental-decision-fold/repro-4455-line-poll-timing.txt) log lines: 4455 still-open decisions: 2005 OLD per-line bash fold (one poll): still running >7 min (exceeded 300s grace) when stopped NEW status_open_decisions (one poll): 0.544s NEW _fm_status_open_decision_origins (hot path): 0.644s ```text Repro of the intent's reported scenario on a 4455-line status log with ~2005 still-open decisions (heavier than the report's 132; same O(n*k) shape). status_line_verb strips every bracket tag before the colon, in any order, and recovers the bare verb ok - a [corr=...] tag ahead of [key=...] no longer swallows the verb: opens and closes under the stated key ok - a [corr=...] tag with no stated key opens under 'default', exactly like a bare needs-decision line ok - a [key=x] tag alone (no corr tag) still opens x - no regression from the tag-stripping fix ok - blocked/resolved parse their bare verb with any bracket-tag order preceding the colon ok - the incremental fold matches the full fold across appends in both key positions ok - status_key_closing_verb separates resolution, durable transfer, and still-open ok - status_key_closing_verb reports the last real transition, in either key position ok - per-key reads retain resolutions without subprocess work growing with unrelated history ok - overridden resolve and durable-transfer verbs still close keys behind unrelated history ok - per-key filtering retains ship/scout terminals, reopenings, and secondmate blockers ok - prose without a colon cannot impersonate a ship or scout terminal declaration ok - only a colon-bearing or keyed line is a decision transition in the fold === fm-classify-corr-token === ok - captain regex overrides preserve timed and legacy relevance and event bytes ok - malformed event times stay ordinary line bytes without hiding the event ok - malformed event times never open or close a decision ok - optional event time preserves parsing and legacy unknown time ok - a correlation token between the verb and the key breaks neither opening nor closing ok - the token is read through before the key, after it, doubled, bracketed, and unkeyed ok - the untokened opener/closer pair behaves exactly as before ok - prose, malformed, wrong-length and unknown name=value tokens stay non-transitions ok - a token-first line cannot impersonate any opening or closing verb ok - untokened captain-relevance, pause, terminal-verb and captain-held verdicts are unchanged ok - captain-relevance, terminal-verb, pause and captain-held all read through the token ok - the daemon and crew-state verb case arms read through the token ok - reading through the token does not weaken the reserved-key namespace rule ok - the cursor-backed fold and the whole-file fold agree on every correlated transition ok - a cursor persisted under the previous reading is discarded and refolded ok - both real correlation-token writers produce lines this classifier reads through === fm-wake-drain-open-decisions-cursor === ok - terminal supersession reaches whole-file reads, incremental drains, old caches, and captured spans ok - a failed presentation read preserves status state for retry ok - a cursor-cache read failure refolds decisions without replaying handled unread status ok - a pre-fix cursor is rebuilt so a previously skipped corr-tagged decision surfaces ok - an old fold cache is rebuilt once before same-version incremental reads resume ok - a buried decision survives many growing drains with bounded read cost, and resolution durably clears it at bounded cost too === fm-wake-drain-open-decisions === ok - a needs-decision buried under later routine/other-key lines still reports as open ok - an over-long open decision is cut to its per-item budget with the shared truncation marker ok - an explicit resolved [key=X] closes the keyed decision ok - a later unrelated terminal line never clears an open decision ok - a reserved decision key can only be opened or closed by its owning library ok - no open decisions across the fleet prints nothing WAKE_ACK_REQUIRED: after handling completes run bin/fm-wake-drain.sh --ack-through 1 --recovery-generation 94665.1790088898.TdbTbW ok - the open-decision section is fleet-wide, not scoped to this drain's own queued records ok - a buried open decision surfaces even when the wake queue itself is empty ok - the fleet-wide decision scan does not follow status symlinks [exited with code 0] ```

title: fix(bin): identify Bun-run omp sessions across lock, harness, and liveness detection
body:
## Problem

omp 18.2.8 changed packaging: `~/.bun/bin/omp` is a Bun SCRIPT executed by the real `bun` interpreter, so a live session reports `ps -o comm=` as `bun` with `bun /Users/<u>/.bun/bin/omp` in args. Every identity surface missed it:

- **Session lock**: `fm_harness_process_matches` matched only bare `omp` command names, so `bin/fm-lock.sh` refused every omp primary with "cannot locate harness process in ancestry" — read-only forever, no supervision, no wake drain.
- **Harness detection**: `OMPCODE=1` is now published on tool subprocesses (alongside `CLAUDECODE=1`, since omp is Claude-Code-compatible), but the marker ladder tested `CLAUDECODE` first, so an omp session identified as `claude` (or `unknown` when markers were cleared).
- **Liveness**: the tmux/herdr agent classifier read a Bun-omp pane as `other` instead of `agent`.

## Fix

- `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh`: the bare-interpreter arm identifies the harness from the script path in **args[1] only**, whole path components, via `fm_harness_path_name` (keeps `FM_HARNESS_IS_CLAUDE` working for node-run Claude chains).
- `bin/fm-harness.sh`: `OMPCODE` marker tested **before** `CLAUDECODE` (same ordering hazard as cursor/gemini/rovo, documented inline); `ancestry_names_omp` and `harness_process_verdict` gained `bun`/`node` arms matching the omp script path in args[1].
- `bin/fm-agent-process-lib.sh`: `fm_agent_process_classify` classifies `bun|node <...>/omp` as agent from args[1] only.
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: clears `OMPCODE` at every non-omp launch boundary alongside the other foreign markers.
- `docs/verification/runtime-backends.md`: dated 18.2.8 identity refresh (live proof: this home's own primary session acquired its fleet lock after the patch).

## Tests

- `tests/fm-omp-harness.test.sh`: new bun-run omp detection test, OMPCODE precedence cases, bun-run liveness classification cases; anchored-name cases moved to a deterministic fake-ps table so the suite passes both from inside a live omp session and from CI.
- `tests/fm-harness-precedence.test.sh` + `tests/fm-watcher-lock.test.sh`: clear leaked `OMPCODE` at probe boundaries (same hygiene as the other foreign markers).
- Local: fm-omp-harness 12/12, fm-harness-precedence 13/13, fm-session-lock-ancestry 16/16, fm-watcher-lock green; `bin/fm-lint.sh` runs in CI (full-analysis local run exceeded the 300s tool budget, rerunning on the isolated worktree).

title: feat(bin): add quota-balanced Claude account profiles
body:
## Intent

Den zweiten Claude-Account `martin.lange@consight-swiss.ch` dauerhaft und parallel zum bestehenden Claude-Account in Firstmate integrieren, ohne wiederholtes Ab- und Anmelden. Die ganze Flotte soll beide Accounts kennen, bei jedem neuen Claude-Arbeiter beide Kontingente sauber in die Auswahl einbeziehen und den Account mit der besseren tatsächlichen Restkapazität so wählen, dass beide Kontingente sinnvoll und möglichst gleichmäßig genutzt werden. Ein laufender Auftrag darf niemals still auf den anderen Account wechseln. Keine Tokens kopieren oder bestehende Profile überschreiben.

## What Changed

- Added `bin/fm-claude-profile-lib.sh`, a new library that validates `config/claude-profiles.json`, measures each declared Claude account directory in isolation via `quota-axi --provider claude --profile-only --json`, and selects the profile with the best applicable `spendPriority` (ties broken lexically by name); exhausted profiles are excluded and a single invalid/unreachable/unauthenticated profile refuses the whole selection rather than being skipped.
- Wired the new library into `bin/fm-spawn.sh`: fresh Claude launches select a profile from current isolated quota, relaunches and secondmate recoveries instead re-validate and reuse the previously bound `claude_profile`/`claude_config_dir` from task metadata (never reselecting), a legacy task with no prior binding keeps the historical ambient `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` behavior, and switching harness away from and back to Claude clears the binding and reselects fresh. The chosen store is exported as `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` for both trust registration and the launched worker.
- Propagated the account binding through remote secondmate routing (`bin/fm-remote-secondmate-control.sh` now reports `claude_profile=`/`claude_config_dir=` in `print_route`) and through local config inheritance (`bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh` adds `claude-profiles.json` to `FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG` so secondmate homes inherit the same account references without copying credentials).
- Documented the new schema and selection contract in `docs/configuration.md` ("Claude account profiles"), cross-referenced it from `docs/architecture.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/references/harness/claude.md`, and recorded isolated-measurement verification evidence in `docs/verification/dispatch-auth.md`.
- Added/extended tests: `tests/fm-spawn-dispatch-profile.test.sh` (new, covers per-profile quota calls, best-capacity selection, deterministic ties, durable metadata, trust registration, unknown-quota handling, and absent-config backward compatibility), `tests/fm-control-relaunch.test.sh` (new, proves a bound assignment is not reconsidered on relaunch even if another account later has more capacity), and `tests/fm-secondmate-harness.test.sh` (updated for the inherited reference-only profile declaration).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix round's change is a minimal, well-targeted one-line gate (bin/fm-spawn.sh:3185) plus a matching doc update and a genuine behavioral regression test; it fully closes the previously flagged stale-binding gap (verified against the meta-write path at bin/fm-spawn.sh:4545-4546 and preserve_relaunch_meta at bin/fm-spawn.sh:4524-4531, which now omit/clear claude_profile and claude_config_dir when HARNESS != claude) without introducing new scope or defects.

Ran the three test suites that exercise this change's product surface (fm-spawn.sh's Claude account-profile selection/binding and fm-control.sh's relaunch/harness-switch handling) as real subprocesses against an isolated FM_HOME with faked external binaries (tmux, quota-axi) — the standard and only practical way to drive this bash CLI orchestrator end-to-end; all passed. To confirm the review-fix commit (a288f15) genuinely fixes the flagged stale-binding defect rather than the test being coincidentally green, I temporarily reverted bin/fm-spawn.sh's one-line guard to its pre-fix form and reran the suite: the new regression test failed exactly as the review finding predicted (binding carried into a non-Claude harness), then restored the fix and confirmed all tests pass again with a clean worktree. No live Herdr-lab session was needed since this change's logic is entirely in meta-file bookkeeping and quota-selection bash logic, not Herdr pane/TUI rendering, and the existing tests already drive the real fm-spawn.sh/fm-control.sh binaries as an end user would invoke them.

The automated remote-secondmate lifecycle suite, review, documentation checks and lint completed successfully.

title: fix(bin): keep GitHub readers paused across re-registration
body:
## Intent Treat the non-durable no-GitHub-read pause as a Firstmate safety bug and route the smallest owner-side fix. Start from the operator-visible reproduction: while a no-GitHub-read credential-safety pause is active, startup or later PR registration can silently re-arm contribution observation or merge polling. Separate trigger, masking condition, and visible symptom; compare the re-arming paths with the supported local-only retirement path; inspect relevant history; test the smallest counterfactual and disconfirming evidence. Implement only if the cause is proven, turning both startup and PR-registration reproductions into regression tests. Preserve PR/head metadata, contribution records, and sidecars needed for later resumption. Do not release or weaken the pause, perform GitHub or Vault operations, touch the currently retired live observers, publish, or merge. Use the project standard validation path when credentials become safely available; until then preserve a clean implementation and report the evidence. ## What Changed - Add a durable GitHub-read pause command that retires contribution observation and GitHub merge polling without deleting resumable records. - Prevent startup, contribution polling, PR registration, and watcher snapshots from performing or re-arming GitHub reads while paused, while preserving PR/head metadata and poll sidecars. - Add regression coverage for startup and PR-registration re-arming, marker-first races, idempotent pauses, record preservation, and unaffected GitLab polling. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The requested status mode removal is complete, and the remaining change is a well-bounded durable pause implementation with no newly substantiated material issues beyond the previously reviewed and explicitly ignored finding. ## Testing Live isolated CLI registration and startup confirmed that no GitHub reader was armed, no GitHub CLI was available, and PR/head metadata plus resumable sidecars remained intact. The focused six-scenario regression passed but was not live product validation, so its adversarial and scope-boundary scenario is untested under this contract. - Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 2 of 3 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Registering a GitHub PR during an active pause records resumable metadata without GitHub access or re-arming observers | ✅ pass | live | Live durable GitHub-read pause transcript | | Starting Firstmate during an active pause leaves contribution observation and merge polling retired while preserving PR metadata and sidecars byte-for-byte | ✅ pass | live | Live durable GitHub-read pause transcript | | The pause is idempotent, blocks an already-snapshotted reader, preserves durable records, and does not retire GitLab polling or alter normal unpaused behavior | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload cited only a test command and explicitly recorded live=false, so it did not establish this scenario against the live running product. |
Evidence: Live durable GitHub-read pause transcript Source: [Live durable GitHub-read pause transcript](https://github.com/connectwithclayton/firstmate/blob/5351765aae4d13a220a53a2af852584ea5b9ca2f/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/fm-github-read-pause-durability/github-read-pause-live.txt) ```text LIVE SCENARIO: active durable pause, GitHub CLI absent from PATH gh available: no ACTION: register PR while pause is active recorded: state/delivery.pr-poll (GitHub reads paused) STATE AFTER REGISTRATION: absent delivery.check.sh absent contributions.check.sh absent contributions.check-trust present delivery.pr-poll present delivery.pr-poll-registration present delivery.meta present .github-read-pause ACTION: run local startup while pause is active MISSING: tmux (install: brew install tmux # or the platform's package manager) MISSING: treehouse (install: curl -fsSL https://kunchenguid.github.io/treehouse/install.sh | sh) MISSING: node (install: brew install node # or the platform's package manager) MISSING: gh (install: brew install gh # or the platform's package manager) MISSING: no-mistakes (install: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes/main/docs/install.sh | sh) MISSING: gh-axi (install: npm install -g gh-axi && gh-axi setup hooks) MISSING: chrome-devtools-axi (install: npm install -g chrome-devtools-axi && chrome-devtools-axi setup hooks) MISSING: tasks-axi (install: npm install -g tasks-axi) MISSING: quota-axi (install: npm install -g quota-axi) PRESENTATION_UNAVAILABLE: lavish-axi (requires >=0.1.46; install: npm install -g lavish-axi && lavish-axi setup hooks) - nonvisual work may proceed with plain-text decisions and reports; install or upgrade before using Lavish STATE AFTER STARTUP: absent delivery.check.sh absent contributions.check.sh absent contributions.check-trust present delivery.pr-poll present delivery.pr-poll-registration present delivery.meta present .github-read-pause PR poll preserved byte-for-byte: yes PR registration preserved byte-for-byte: yes metadata: worktree=/var/folders/nz/2_wts0tj2_s7x1flcwlpvvdh0000gn/T//fm-pause-live.MDi13k/home/wt kind=ship pr=https://github.com/o/r/pull/8 pr_head=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa ```
- Outcome: ⚠️ 1 warning across 1 run (4m34s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)

✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 2 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `bin/fm-github-read-pause.sh:93` - The pause classifies a runnable check solely from the adjacent `.pr-poll` sidecar. A stale GitHub sidecar can coexist with a later custom check registered under the same task ID, causing pause to delete that non-GitHub check. body:
## Summary

title: fix(backlog): carry a confirmed GitLab merge request through task cleanup
body:
## Summary

Firstmate's backlog tool `tasks-axi` rejects GitLab `/merge_requests/` URLs passed through its GitHub-only `--pr` flag. During a merged GitLab merge request, teardown recorded the URL in its pending-close receipt and finished worker and local-copy cleanup, but the atomic backlog close failed, leaving the receipt stranded with no replay path.

This change carries a confirmed GitLab merge request through task cleanup without passing a GitHub-only `--pr` argument, and retires the pending-close receipt on both the ordinary teardown path and the session-start pending-close replay path. The GitHub `/pull/<number>` validation path is unchanged.

## Changes

- `bin/fm-backlog-transition-lib.sh`: normalize a GitLab merge-request URL passed as `--pr` into a plain `--note` recording the link, at the single choke point both `fm_backlog_close_transition` and `fm_backlog_retain_transition` call before applying completion args. This covers ordinary teardown, crash-recovery replay, and a retained/held task, with no change to GitHub URL handling.
- `tests/fm-backlog-atomicity.test.sh`: four new colocated regression tests covering ordinary teardown of a GitLab-MR task, pending-close replay of the same shape, retention of a GitLab-MR task for a held captain decision, and its own replay path. Each asserts the row ends `done` (or correctly held) with no leftover `state/<id>.backlog-close` receipt, and the GitLab link preserved.
- `docs/configuration.md`: one pointer line.

## Pipeline attestation

This branch was driven end to end through `no-mistakes`: the `intent`, `rebase`, `review`, `test`, `document`, and `lint` steps all ran through the pipeline's own gate agents and completed. Two `ask-user` findings were escalated to and decided by Firstmate:

- Review gate: fixed a gap where `fm_backlog_retain_transition` did not apply the same GitLab normalization as the close path (now covered by the added retention tests).
- Test gate: accepted with an explicit caveat — **live fleet validation was not driven for this change; it was blocked by the gate agent's own safety boundary, not by any test failure.** Only focused automated regression coverage (the four tests above, plus existing GitHub and malformed-URL coverage) was run.

The `lint` gate's only finding was `fm-lint-workflows.sh: actionlint not found` on the pipeline's own test machine — a missing tool in that environment, not a defect in this branch, which touches no GitHub workflow file (confirmed by diff against `origin/main`).

**Push and PR were completed manually, outside the pipeline**, because this account (`bzeffren`) has read-only access to `kunchenguid/firstmate` and `no-mistakes` has no way to retarget its own push/PR steps to a fork remote. So: pipeline attestation is present for `intent` through `lint`. It is **absent** for the `push`, `pr`, and `ci` steps — those ran as ordinary manual `git push` / PR creation, and CI on this PR runs through the repository's standard GitHub Actions workflows rather than through a `no-mistakes`-driven `ci` step.

A fresh cross-provider (provider-family-independent) review round is expected after CI is green, per this task's review requirement; this branch and PR are kept ready for it.

## Out of scope

The stranded live record for a separate task (`optimize-prepush-parallelism`) in the primary Firstmate home was deliberately left untouched; it will replay on its own once this fix lands.

✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 3 issues found → auto-fixed ✅ - ⚠️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:1005` - secondmate_health_model_melt returns immediately when fm_secondmate_melt_cooldown_active matches the live harness/model, before any quota-dead check. After a successful melt the cooldown is written for the replacement (line 1057); after new=none/relaunch-failure it is written for the dead pin (lines 1024/1047). Concrete residual path: melt onto Luna → cool Luna for 1h → Luna becomes exhausted_now (or the prior snapshot was stale-ok) → every health tick short-circuits at line 1005 with no wake and no remelt until the marker ages out. Same shape after new=none: a later-recovered quota-ok crew-dispatch profile is ignored for the full cooldown while the dead pin keeps running. Earliest shared boundary: only honor cooldown when the live pin is not currently quota-dead (and, for pane-only triggers, when evidence has not re-armed); thrash prevention should not outrank a still-dead commander. - ⚠️ `bin/fm-watch.sh:1076` - secondmate_health_tick skips secondmate_health_model_melt entirely when secondmate_health_capture fails (not alive, transport error, missing target), even if secondmate_health_quota_snapshot already proves the recorded pin is dead. title: feat(bin): route crew dispatch with declared quality preference
body:
## Intent

Captain 2026-09-22: GPT quota is usually plentiful; near reset (e.g. Codex ~Sep 24, Claude ~Sep 25) with headroom remaining, project work should use high-quality models (Sol medium), not default Luna to "save".

This preference must enter **model routing**, not only captain chat. Design then implement the smallest coherent path so firstmate (and secondmates) pick models with quota-axi evidence: effectivePercentRemaining, resetsAt, spendPriority, runway — and captain standing "prefer high quality when headroom + near/through reset".

Do not invent a second router. Extend existing crew-dispatch + quota-array-dispatch + fm-dispatch-resolve / spawn intake.

## What Changed

- Extend crew-dispatch resolution so a top-level `quality_preference` and per-profile `prefer_quality` can prefer marked high-quality candidates after the existing eligibility/reasoning/runway gates, then rank the resulting pool by `spendPriority` (with unmarked fallback, or escalate when no fallback remains).
- Validate the new fields in `fm-bootstrap` / `fm-dispatch-resolve`, surface activation notes and per-candidate `prefer_quality` / `resetsAt` / `quality_reason` evidence, and update `quota-array-dispatch` plus configuration docs to match the same policy.
- Point the starter `crew-dispatch` example at Sol medium as the marked quality route with Luna as unmarked fallback, and cover accept/reject config plus near-reset, comfortable-headroom, and inactive-fallback resolution paths in tests.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Quota quality preference is a bounded extension of the existing crew-dispatch → quota-array-dispatch → fm-dispatch-resolve path, with matching validation, docs/example standing config, and deterministic filter semantics that preserve spendPriority as the sole ranker.

## Testing

Automated dispatch-resolve and bootstrap crew-dispatch validation both passed. Manual fm-dispatch-resolve E2E with the documented example config showed the captain standing in routing: near-reset (31% through_reset) and comfortable (60%) headroom pick Sol medium; insufficient headroom keeps Luna; malformed prefer_quality without quality_preference exits 2.

title: fix(bin): resolve capped run inventories for worker copies
body:
## Intent

Issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate/issues/5211.

Once a repository has more than ten recorded validation runs, current-state reads report every ship task running in a pooled worker copy as unknown with an unreadable run inventory, and the fleet view and heartbeat reviews inherit that verdict.

The cause is a lookup, not missing data. On a capped overview the run selector resolves the inventory by the worker copy path, but `no-mistakes init` registered the primary clone, so no row exists under that path and the whole inventory reads unreadable. The overview itself names the repository it resolved on its `repo:` line.

Two cases that should read correctly come back unknown: a branch whose newest run completed but falls outside the ten rows shown, and a branch with no run at all, such as a task that has not started validation or a direct-PR task that never validates.

The consequence is that a finished validation, a task that never validated, and a genuinely unreadable inventory become indistinguishable. Every ship task in a busy repository reads unknown, which buries real problems among false ones and prompts recovery checks that are not needed.

Expected: with a capped overview, a worker copy of a registered repository reads the same as the primary clone - a completed run outside the shown rows is selected as completed, and a branch with no recorded run reads as having no run - while a missing, mismatched, truncated or ambiguous inventory still reads unknown.

## What Changed

- Resolve capped run inventories using the overview’s `repo:` path alongside the worker-copy path, so completed runs beyond the ten-row window and branches with no runs are identified correctly.
- Require exact path matches to identify one repository, retaining `unknown` for unresolved or conflicting identity and unreadable inventories.
- Add worker-copy regression cases for absent and completed runs, and clarify that the captured overview excerpt omits the `repo:` field.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is a bounded, read-only lookup correction; review found no material correctness, intent-conformance, or simplification issues.

## Testing

The live CLI probe was blocked by the unregistered checkout. Focused automated regressions, primary/worker comparisons, and inventory guards passed; both reported failures reproduced against the base. A broader test-file run was stopped to narrow scope, and a temporary harness quoting error was corrected before rerunning. CLI evidence was retained; this change has no rendered UI requiring screenshots.

- Live validation: ⚠️ inconclusive - 0 of 6 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Read a worker-copy branch whose completed run falls outside the ten displayed rows; report completed, matching the primary. | ⏸️ untested | no | No registered live repository is accessible within scope. Provide an isolated registered repository with a genuine completed run outside its latest ten rows. |
| Read a worker-copy branch with no recorded run; use worker activity instead of reporting an unreadable inventory. | ⏸️ untested | no | The permitted checkout is unregistered. Provide an isolated registered repository with capped history and a branch that has never validated. |
| Read current state when the complete inventory cannot be read; retain unknown and available run identities. | ⏸️ untested | no | A registered disposable live environment is unavailable. Provide one for controlled inventory failure injection without modifying production state. |
| Read a mismatched or truncated inventory; reject a confident state. | ⏸️ untested | no | Only simulated inventory faults could be exercised. Provide a registered disposable live environment supporting controlled fault injection. |
| Read a worker copy when its path and the overview path identify different repositories; report unknown. | ⏸️ untested | no | No disposable live repository registrations are available within scope. Provide an isolated environment containing the conflicting registrations. |
| Read capped history containing competing active runs for the branch; report unknown and identify both runs. | ⏸️ untested | no | Creating or controlling validation runs is forbidden in this phase. Provide an isolated registered repository with genuine competing run records. |

title: feat(bin): add openhands as a verified crewmate/scout adapter
body:
## Intent

Be able to delegate tasks to DeepSeek 4.1 Flash. The standing route for it is Fireworks AI DeepSeek 4.1 Flash through the OpenHands adapter (model fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4p1-flash), and that route is broken: an openhands spawn sits idle at its composer and never processes its brief. Confirmed live on 2026-09-22. `openhands --help` says `-f FILE` only seeds the composer in the interactive TUI, while `--headless` (which requires `--task` or `--file`) is what runs non-interactively with auto-approve.

## What Changed
- `openhands` is now a verified crewmate/scout harness everywhere harnesses are listed: `fm-control-lib.sh`, `fm-harness.sh` detection (anchored on the process name), dispatch and bootstrap validation (effort is not supported), Escape interrupt, and `/exit`. `--secondmate` launches on it are refused. It gets its own busy regex, `ESC: pause`, used both as a delivery guard in `fm-composer-lib.sh` and as a rendered-tail fallback in `fm-busy-lib.sh`. The `Type your message, @mention a file` placeholder is now recognized as an idle composer.
- `fm-spawn.sh` launches the OpenHands TUI with `--override-with-envs --always-approve --exit-without-confirmation`. The model comes from `--model` or `LLM_MODEL`, for example `fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4p1-flash`. The API key comes from `LLM_API_KEY` or `config/openhands-llm.env`, and both are written to a per-task env file readable only by the owner. Each task also gets its own HOME and persistence dir. The spawn does not use `-f`/`--headless`: it waits for the idle composer, types a pointer to the brief file, presses Enter, and reports success only after the `ESC: pause` busy row appears. This fixes spawns that sat idle and never processed their brief. `fm-teardown.sh` removes the per-task openhands env file, persistence dir, and HOME.
- Adds the openhands adapter reference and verification docs, updates the configuration, architecture, and runtime-backend docs, and adds `tests/fm-openhands-harness.test.sh` and a live signals e2e test. It also updates existing harness-list tests and adds `.omc/` to `.gitignore`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix round does exactly what was asked: it removes the already-working bypass, so readiness now means only the empty-composer placeholder and the brief pointer is always sent and submitted once. The new regression test runs the real spawn script, and it would fail against the old code (the stale `ESC: pause` would skip the pointer and leave pointer.log empty). Findings from earlier rounds that were ignored are not re-reported.

## Testing

I drove the real product at 1dc460a in a throwaway lab: a private tmux socket, a throwaway FM_HOME and project, and a throwaway treehouse pool. The live openhands spawn on Fireworks DeepSeek 4.1 Flash returned rc=0. The pane shows the brief pointer submitted and the turn running (`Working … ESC: pause`), and the worker wrote the requested LIVE_PROOF_R4.txt and a scout report. A single Escape paused the turn and left the process running; `/exit` then ended it. A live spawn with no API key refused before any pane was created. The opt-in live signals e2e test and the deterministic harness suite both passed. The stale-`ESC: pause` guard is covered only by the deterministic fake-tmux test, so it is recorded as untested live. My first attempt seeded the lab with a non-Fireworks key by mistake and failed authentication. It still showed the pointer typed and submitted, and it is recorded as a setup error, not a product failure. The lab has been torn down.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 4 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Delegating a scout to Fireworks DeepSeek 4.1 Flash via `fm-spawn.sh --harness openhands` starts the TUI, submits the brief, and the worker completes it (proof file written) | ✅ pass | live | round3-live-spawn-at-target-PASSES.txt: rc=0, LLM_MODEL=fireworks_ai/accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4p1-flash, pane shows '> Read the brief at …/launch-brief.md' then 'Working (0s • ESC: pause)',… |
| The generated openhands launch line runs through the shell without the round-1 `env: 'set'` failure (openhands process starts with --override-with-envs --always-approve --exit-without-confirmation) | ✅ pass | live | round3-live-spawn-at-target-PASSES.txt: process tree treehouse → bash → openhands, with the expected argv |
| Spawned worker can be steered: one Escape pauses the turn without killing it, and /exit ends the process | ✅ pass | live | round3-live-spawn-at-target-PASSES.txt: 'Pausing conversation', alive after Escape=yes, alive after submitted /exit=no; also round3-live-signals-e2e.txt |
| Adversarial: spawning openhands with no LLM_API_KEY refuses before any pane is created | ✅ pass | live | round3-live-missing-key-refuses.txt: 'error: openhands requires LLM_API_KEY …', rc=1, tmux windows before=2 after=2 |
| Adversarial: a stale 'ESC: pause' in the capture does not skip brief delivery (the pointer is always sent after the composer placeholder) | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result: only the deterministic fake-tmux test covers this (round3-harness-suite.txt passed it). There is no settle after the ready signal, no retry and no check that the composer emptied. kimi and rovo, which the comment names as the shape being followed, use fm_backend_send_text_submit with retries and a composer-state check. The composer lib now recognises the openhands placeholder (FM_COMPOSER_IDLE_RE_DEFAULT), so that helper can handle this TUI too. The live e2e test that proved this path waits 0.4s after the placeholder appears before typing; spawn does not. Failure case: Textual draws the placeholder before the Input widget is focused, so the keystrokes or the Enter are dropped. The composer then sits idle, openhands_wait_for_working times out after about 30s, and the spawn fails and kills the endpoint. The failure is closed, not silent, but it makes the DeepSeek route flaky. Fix: send the pointer through fm_backend_send_text_submit (with retries), as kimi and rovo do, or at least add the settle delay the live test used.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:5080` - Unrequired component. openhands_pane_is_ready (line 3915) treats a pane that is already busy as ready, and the spawn skips sending the pointer when the pane already classifies as working. The launch no longer carries -f/--task, so a new openhands process can never have a turn in flight before the pointer is sent; the comment itself says 'somehow'. The intent (the brief must actually be processed) does not need this branch. It is also exactly where the reported failure could come back: a stale or false `ESC: pause` in the last 12 non-blank lines of the capture makes the spawn skip delivery, and wait_for_working then succeeds at once. Result: the spawn reports success while the worker sits idle at its composer. Fix: remove the bypass so readiness means the placeholder only and the pointer is always sent.
- ⚠️ `tests/fm-openhands-harness.test.sh:241` - The fake tmux switches to `busy` as soon as the pointer text is typed with send-keys -l, not when Enter arrives. So the regression test cannot catch the bug this change fixes (text left in the composer and never submitted): if the spawn's Enter step were deleted, test_openhands_launch_carries_the_brief_with_env_model_and_autonomy would still pass. Fix: have the fake record the typed pointer and switch to busy only on a later `send-keys ... Enter`, so the test fails without the submit.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:3946` - openhands_spawn_fail writes a plain `printf 'failed: %s\n'` status line. The sibling spawn-fail helpers (kimi_spawn_fail, rovo_spawn_fail, agy_spawn_fail) write it through status_stamp_line, which adds the `[at=<epoch>]` stamp. title: feat(bin): add agy turn-end hook behind a one-time captain consent
body:
## Intent

Add a one-time captain opt-in before firstmate writes the agy turn-end hook into the captain's global agy settings.

The captain's words, 2026-09-21 10:41 IST: "then let us go wth your recommendation of the one-time opt-in".

He chose that after asking what the installer actually writes and whether it would affect his Mac. He was told, and it is true, that it edits one file, adds or replaces one key, leaves the rest intact, and that when the hook fires it only touches a turn-end marker and a small busy-state record inside firstmate's own directory with no network access and no deletion. His concern was settled on the facts. What he chose to fix is the CONSENT problem, not a damage problem.

He explicitly rejected two alternatives: leaving it silent as it is today, and asking on every spawn.

## What Changed

- Add `bin/fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh`, which writes one firstmate-owned `firstmate-turn-end` key into the global `~/.gemini/config/hooks.json` and installs its hook script plus a private per-task token registry under `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/`; `fm-spawn.sh` probes `agy --version` against a 1.2.6 floor, mints the per-task token it exports to the launched process, and arms agy's busy record from that hook instead of the rendered tail.
- Gate the install on a one-time consent file `config/agy-turnend-hook` (`allow`, `deny`, absent means ask once): a recorded `deny` retracts an earlier install and session-start bootstrap sweeps the same withdrawal, any refusal drops that spawn to the retained rendered-tail idle read rather than failing, and the item inherits into local secondmate homes only, excluded from the remote transfer set by `FM_LOCAL_ONLY_INHERITABLE_CONFIG`.
- Close agy's busy record on a manual interrupt through both `fm-control.sh` and `fm-send.sh --key Escape`, because agy's Stop hook does not fire on one, and retire only the task's own token at teardown while leaving the shared hook key installed for other live agy tasks.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: This round is two deletions and a log-prefix move, each verified against the diff, its owners, and a test assertion that discriminates against the pre-fix behavior; the only residue is one stale comment that contradicts the assertion beneath it.

## Testing

I drove the consent gate end to end as an operator would: the real installer, the real session-start bootstrap and the real installed hook script, each against a scratch machine with HOME redirected, and separately ran the targeted suite tests/fm-agy-harness.test.sh (50 cases, all green). Ten live scenarios covering the unasked refusal, the allow install, the never-ask-again property, the deny retraction, the live-token withdrawal, bad consent values, the store guards under allow, the session-start withdrawal, the local-only inheritance and a real hook firing produced 48 assertions with zero failures. The one firing I drove wrote only task-1.turn-ended and task-1.busy-state inside firstmate's own state directory and added nothing new to agy's tree, which is exactly what the captain was told he was consenting to. One scenario is untested: a real agy spawn in an unasked home. The suite exercises that path against a fake agy binary and a fake terminal backend, which is not the live product, so I am not claiming a live result for it. No visual artifact was captured because this change has no rendered surface - its whole output is CLI stderr and session-start text, which the transcript reproduces verbatim. The operator's real machine was verified clean before and after: ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json did not exist and no fm-turn-end.* files existed in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/ at either point. One cosmetic note not worth a finding: the deny refusal always says "any key an earlier consent installed has been removed", including in a home where nothing was ever installed. The worktree is clean and all scratch labs were removed.
