<summary>⚠️ **Review** - 1 info</summary>

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:4111` - The spawn arms a busy generation and seeds state=busy source=fm-spawn for every managed agy launch whose hook install succeeded, but nothing checks that the running agy actually has the hook surface. The repo's own prior record asserts it does not on the version it was verified against: the pre-change comment in bin/fm-busy-lib.sh said "agy 1.2.0 exposes no hook surface at all", and docs/verification/agy.md still lists Version as agy 1.2.0/1.2.1 with the hook surface established only on 1.2.6. Concrete sequence on a host still at 1.2.0: the captain records allow; fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh writes the firstmate-turn-end key; fm-spawn.sh:4111 arms BUSY_GEN and seeds the record; agy never reads hooks.json, so neither PreInvocation nor Stop ever fires. fm_busy_record_read then returns that seeded record for the whole task life and fm_busy_classify (bin/fm-busy-lib.sh:922-933) answers busy fm-spawn, never reaching the rendered-tail arm at line 951 that carried agy detection before this change. state/<id>.turn-ended is never touched, so the supervisor gets no turn-end signal and the crewmate reads busy until BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS (3600s) makes fm-watch treat it as a wedge suspect. The change is otherwise careful never to arm when nothing can clear (raw launch, refused install both skip the arm); a stale agy build is the same case and is the one that is unguarded. The remedy, not the defect, needs authorization: it means adding a capability or version probe, or confirming one hook firing before trusting the record, which extends the change beyond its stated scope.
- ⚠️ `docs/configuration.md:398` - config/agy-turnend-hook is deliberately left out of FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG (bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:71), and the stated rationale is that "consent is to touch one specific machine's home directory and a remote secondmate runs against a different one". That rationale does not hold for a LOCAL secondmate, which is a real launch shape (docs/architecture.md:65 reads "every endpoint-recorded local secondmate home's durable wake queue"). A local secondmate runs under the same uid and therefore the same ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json as the primary, but gets its own config/ directory. Concrete sequence: the captain records allow in the primary home and an agy crewmate installs the hook; a local secondmate home then spawns its own agy crewmate, its installer finds no consent file, refuses, and the spawn degrades to the rendered-tail read with no busy arm and no turn-end signal - for a hook that is already installed and working on that exact machine. The captain is then asked a second time for a write he already authorised, or, if that home cannot reach him, agy crewmates under it stay permanently degraded. The remedy needs authorization either way: inherit the file into local homes, or restate the scope in the docs as per-home and accept the repeat ask.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh:115` - A recorded deny refuses future installs but never removes a firstmate-turn-end key an earlier allow already wrote, and nothing else calls remove: teardown deliberately skips it (bin/fm-teardown.sh:1252-1254) and fm-spawn only ever calls install. Concrete sequence: the captain writes allow, one agy crewmate spawns and the key lands in ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json; he later changes his mind and writes deny; every subsequent spawn degrades as intended, but the key stays in the shared store and keeps running two synchronous subprocesses per turn in his own agy sessions and the Antigravity IDE for good. docs/configuration.md:391 reads "deny refuses it, and is equally durable", which a captain could reasonably read as retraction rather than as refusal of further writes. The remedy - making a recorded deny run the existing remove action, or documenting that revoking means running fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh remove by hand - changes product behavior, so it needs the author's call.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:2219` - The [ "$KIND" != secondmate ] half of the install predicate can never be false. bin/fm-spawn.sh:2140-2143 already exits non-zero when KIND is secondmate and HARNESS is agy, every HARNESS assignment happens at or before line 2119, and this line only runs inside the agy) arm of the case at 2196. The guard is dead and the comment above it describes the raw-launch predicate as the real one; dropping it leaves the install condition matching the busy arm at 4111 and the token mint at 4465 exactly, which is what the comment claims it does.

🔧 Fix applied.
3 issues (2 warnings, 1 info) still open:

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:72` - Adding `agy-turnend-hook` to FM_INHERITABLE_CONFIG makes it primary-authoritative, and `propagate_inheritable_config` mirrors primary ABSENCE by deleting the destination (bin/fm-config-inherit-lib.sh:573, allowed because config/ is gitignored). Concrete sequence: the primary home has no config/agy-turnend-hook; a LOCAL secondmate home spawns an agy crewmate, the installer refuses and names that home's own file (`CONSENT_FILE=$FM_HOME/config/agy-turnend-hook`, bin/fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh:59,144), so the answer is recorded there as `allow`; the next bootstrap or `bin/fm-config-push.sh` convergence sees no primary source and runs `rm -f` on the secondmate's copy; the next agy spawn in that home refuses again and re-issues ASK THE CAPTAIN ONCE. That repeats once per convergence cycle, which is the repeated ask the intent set out to remove ("one-time opt-in", with "asking on every spawn" explicitly rejected). The mirror image is also live: after the captain records `deny` in the primary, a local secondmate home still holding `allow` reinstalls the key on its next agy spawn until convergence catches up, so the retraction is not effective at the moment it is recorded. The fix round's own test `test_agy_consent_is_inherited_locally_and_never_remotely` asserts the deletion as correct, so it is part of the claim rather than independent proof. The remedy needs authorization because both options change behavior: exempt this item from absence-mirroring (new sub-category semantics, the way FM_SESSION_SCOPED_INHERITABLE_CONFIG carves out live convergence), or direct the ask to the primary home and say so in docs/configuration.md and the installer's refusal text.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh:136` - The retraction is reachable only from `install`, and `install` is called from exactly one place: the managed-launch arm in bin/fm-spawn.sh:2283, which is skipped for a raw launch and never reached when the version probe fails or when agy is not on PATH. Teardown deliberately never calls remove (bin/fm-teardown.sh:1252-1254). So the most likely withdrawal sequence leaves the key installed for good: the captain writes `deny` precisely because he no longer wants firstmate touching his agy, therefore no further managed agy spawn happens in that home, therefore `firstmate-turn-end` stays in ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json and keeps running two synchronous subprocesses per turn in his own agy sessions and the Antigravity IDE - the exact harm the retraction was added to end. docs/configuration.md:393-394 is accurate about the mechanism ("The next install in a home that reads `deny` removes the ... key") but the consent section never tells the captain that an immediate withdrawal exists as `bin/fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh remove`, which is ungated and safe when no key is present. Smallest honest remedy is a documentation line naming that command in the consent section; making `deny` retract eagerly (at bootstrap or config convergence) would extend the change with new machinery, so the choice is the author's.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-spawn.sh:1864` - `agy_version_at_least`'s header states "any prerelease or build suffix is stripped first" and line 1838 does `candidate=${candidate%%[-+]*}`, but that strip can never run from its only caller: the awk extractor at line 1864 requires a whole whitespace-separated field to match `^v?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)+$`, so a token such as `1.3.0-rc.1` or `1.2.8+build7` is not selected at all and `version` comes back empty. The result is the "printed no recognisable version" branch, i.e. a build that does carry the hook surface silently runs unarmed on the weaker rendered-tail read (with a warning on the spawn path, so it is not wholly silent). The same line 1841 guard `case "$candidate" in ''|*[!0-9.]*) return 1` is unreachable for the same reason. I ran the real binary on this host: `agy --version` prints `1.2.7` on stdout and the awk line parses it to `1.2.7`, so nothing is broken today - but docs/verification/agy.md, which owns how every agy fact was established, records no observed `agy --version` output even though the whole arming decision now depends on its format. Fix by widening the field match to accept a trailing `-`/`+` suffix so the documented strip becomes live (or by deleting the strip and the dead guard), and record the observed `agy --version` string in the verification doc.

🔧 Fix applied.
3 warnings still open:

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh:184` - The one-time consent question is narrower than what a consented install actually writes, and the withdrawal is narrower than the install. The ASK text at bin/fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh:184 asks only whether firstmate may add its own 'firstmate-turn-end' key to ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json, but the consented install (lines 214-304) also creates ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/ and ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/fm-turn-end.d/ (mode 0700) and writes the executable ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/fm-turn-end.sh (mode 0700, ~1.9 KB) into the captain's home. The deny retraction and the manual `remove` delete only the JSON key: I ran install then a deny-retraction against a scratch HOME and confirmed the key was removed and exit was 1, while fm-turn-end.sh and fm-turn-end.d/ were still present afterwards. So a captain who answers the question as asked consents to less than is written, and a captain who withdraws still has firstmate's executable and registry directory in his agy tree. Two facts size the remedy: rollback_install (line 97) already knows how to delete the hook script, and the sibling Kimi installer's remove "removes Firstmate's hook files" per docs/configuration.md:367, so the fuller withdrawal has precedent. The remedy is the author's call because it either widens the consent wording the captain reads or changes `remove`'s documented "only that key" semantics.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:1393` - The eager bootstrap retraction runs in every home, including a local secondmate acting on an inherited copy, so a stale deny can strip the key out from under the primary's live agy crewmates on the same machine. agy_turnend_consent_retract is called unconditionally at bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:1473 inside the local-phase block; unlike startup_memory_budget_setup (line 1376) it has no secondmate-home early return, and the comment at lines 1391-1392 makes that deliberate. Concrete sequence: the primary records deny; a local secondmate converges that copy; the captain changes his mind and records allow in the primary; the primary spawns an agy crewmate, which installs the key and seeds a busy record; the secondmate then runs its own full session-start bootstrap before the primary's next convergence sweep or bin/fm-config-push.sh reaches it, still reads deny, and removes firstmate-turn-end from the one shared ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json. The live crewmate's seeded record now has no PreInvocation or Stop to close it and the pane reads busy until BUSY_TURN_MAX_SECS (3600s default) ages it out - exactly the wedge the new 1.2.6 version floor was added to prevent, produced without any error. Smallest remedy: skip the retraction when fm_secondmate_parent_record_parse yields route=local, because the primary on that same machine runs the identical sweep and owns the answer; a remote secondmate is its own machine and must keep retracting. This needs the author's authorization because the current breadth is a deliberate stated choice. Note that test_agy_bootstrap_retracts_a_recorded_deny only exercises a primary home, so it cannot witness this.
- ⚠️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:1402` - The new AGY_TURNEND_HOOK: bootstrap line is not registered in any of the three places this repo declares bootstrap's output contract: the line inventory in bin/fm-bootstrap.sh's own header (lines 8-25), the bootstrap-diagnostics trigger list in AGENTS.md:582, and .agents/skills/bootstrap-diagnostics/SKILL.md, which states explicitly that "The line formats themselves are owned by bin/fm-bootstrap.sh's header". The failure variant is actionable and names a command to run. Concrete path: the captain records deny while ~/.gemini/config/hooks.json is no longer a JSON object (or node is no longer installed), so fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh remove refuses; bootstrap then prints "AGY_TURNEND_HOOK: ... could not be removed from <store> - run bin/fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh remove" at every session start, and because the prefix appears in no trigger list, nothing tells the agent that line is actionable or how to handle it, so the withdrawn consent stays un-retracted indefinitely while the line reads as unknown noise. Fix by adding the prefix to the header inventory, to the AGENTS.md:582 list, and a handling bullet to the bootstrap-diagnostics playbook.

🔧 Fix applied.
3 issues (1 warning, 2 infos) still open:

- ⚠️ `bin/fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh:126` - The withdrawal's third arm reaches past firstmate's own footprint into agy's directory and prints a false reason when it cannot. remove_hook_files rmdirs $CLI_DIR (~/.gemini/antigravity-cli) and, when that fails, reports "still holds files firstmate did not write". I reproduced the wrong label: after a consented install, a live token in fm-turn-end.d, and a deny retraction, the command printed BOTH the correct registry line AND "'<home>/.gemini/antigravity-cli' still holds files firstmate did not write, so it was left in place" - while the only thing in that directory was the registry firstmate DID write. On a real machine the label is wrong permanently rather than occasionally: ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli is agy's own directory, holding the trustedWorkspaces settings.json that bin/fm-agy-trust.sh writes (docs/verification/agy.md:58) and agy's brain/, so the rmdir always fails and that line fires on every remove forever, sending an operator hunting for foreign files that are not there. The remedy is removal, not repair: the round-3 instruction directed the withdrawal to take back "firstmate's hook script and the fm-turn-end.d registry directory" and named neither antigravity-cli/ nor a message about it; the fix round added this arm on its own, and docs/configuration.md:397-399 documents only the key, the hook files and the token folder, so no doc changes with it. Drop bin/fm-agy-turnend-hook.sh:126-129 and the matching "the emptied antigravity-cli directory survived the withdrawal" assertion at tests/fm-agy-harness.test.sh:1852. This is also this round's Simplification finding: the CLI_DIR arm is the one component 07f80ca introduced that no intent requirement needs.
- ℹ️ `.agents/skills/harness-adapters/references/harness/agy.md:26` - The Hooks row still ends "a recorded `deny` takes the key back out", which was true before 07f80ca widened the withdrawal and is now incomplete: a deny also deletes ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/fm-turn-end.sh and the fm-turn-end.d registry. The same fix round updated docs/configuration.md:369 and AGENTS.md's config/agy-turnend-hook line to say "the key and hook files" but missed this row. An agent reading the adapter reference to answer what a deny costs the captain gets an understated answer about writes into his own home. Extend the row to name the hook files the way the two updated owners already do.
- ℹ️ `bin/fm-bootstrap.sh:1420` - The success variant of the new bootstrap line is emitted under AGY_TURNEND_HOOK:, a prefix this change simultaneously registered as actionable in AGENTS.md:582 and in the bootstrap-diagnostics skill description, while the repo's own convention for a session-start fact that needs no action is the BOOTSTRAP_INFO: prefix that both owners explicitly exclude from a skill load (AGENTS.md:582: "silence and other `BOOTSTRAP_INFO:` facts need no load"). The playbook the change added then has to walk that back in prose (.agents/skills/bootstrap-diagnostics/SKILL.md:41: "The `withdrew ...` variant is informational only and needs no action"). Concrete sequence: the captain records deny, the next session start withdraws the hook cleanly, prints "AGY_TURNEND_HOOK: ... withdrew firstmate's agy turn-end hook and its files", and the agent loads the diagnostics skill only to be told there is nothing to do. Emitting the success as BOOTSTRAP_INFO: and keeping only the "could not be withdrawn" variant under AGY_TURNEND_HOOK: would keep the trigger list honest; that is an output-contract decision the author just made deliberately in three registered places, so it is the author's call rather than a mechanical correction.

🔧 Fix applied.
1 info still open:

- ℹ️ `tests/fm-agy-harness.test.sh:1854` - The inline comment above the second withdrawal case still reads "With the last token gone the folder goes too, and so does its parent." That was accurate at 07f80ca, when remove_hook_files rmdir'd $CLI_DIR. The fix round deleted that arm and inverted the assertion two lines below it, so the comment now states the exact opposite of what the code asserts: line 1858 fails the test if ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli was deleted. The block comment above the function was updated in the same round ("agy's own directory holding them is left alone") but this one was missed, leaving the file carrying both claims. Concrete consequence: a maintainer reading the comment as the statement of intent for the case directly beneath it would reintroduce the rmdir of agy's own directory, which is the arm the captain authorised removing precisely because it can never succeed on a real machine and prints a permanently false "still holds files firstmate did not write" reason. Correct the comment to say the registry folder goes and agy's own directory stays, matching the assertion and the function's block comment.
</details>

title: fix(bin): exclude a remote mate's own parent channel from self-home scans
body:
## What Changed

- Added `fm_parent_channel_outbound_status` in `bin/fm-parent-channel-lib.sh` and a lazily sourced `status_scan_parent_channel_exclude` in `bin/fm-classify-lib.sh` that resolve the outbound parent-channel path only for remote-mate homes; the four fleet-wide status scans (whole-file fold, incremental fold, presentation snapshot, unread surface) now skip that resolved path, while main homes and local mates keep treating a same-named `parent-replies.status` as an ordinary task log.
- Wired the same resolved-path exclusion into the watcher's signal scan and heartbeat fail-safe backstop (`bin/fm-watch.sh`) and the away-mode daemon's heartbeat catch-all in `bin/fm-supervise-daemon.sh` housekeeping, so a remote mate's mirrored channel lines no longer spin spurious wakes or a phantom `parent-replies` task.
- Added `tests/fm-parent-channel-scan-exclusion.test.sh` (registered in `bin/fm-test-run.sh`) covering the exclusion predicates, the folds, and both heartbeat backstops against real remote-mate, main-home, and local-mate fixtures plus an end-to-end `fm-wake-drain.sh` run, and documented the rule in `docs/secondmate-parent-channel.md`.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is a small, mechanical, fail-open exclusion behind one shared home-shape-aware helper with behavioral tests over real remote/main/local fixtures; the only residual finding is a minor test-teardown temp-dir leak.

## Testing

Ran the new tests/fm-parent-channel-scan-exclusion.test.sh (14 checks, pass; a regression variant run against the base commit fails there, proving the suite covers the reported bug), then drove every scenario live against the real product binaries: the actual watcher process stayed quiet on remote-channel appends while still waking on genuine tasks, the actual heartbeat backstop absorbed a channel-only heartbeat and still fired on a real task (the base-commit watcher under identical drives phantom-waked both ways), the actual away-mode daemon's catch-all scan produced no phantom escalation or phantom task tracking while still escalating real blockers, and the actual wake drain rendered no channel content across remote-mate, main-home, and local-mate fixtures while dropping stale channel records. Adjacent suites that own the touched functions (fm-daemon, fm-wake-queue, fm-wake-drain-unread-status, fm-watcher-lock, fm-wake-drain-open-decisions-cursor) all pass. Evidence transcripts and rendered drain output are in the evidence directory; worktree left clean.

title: feat(spawn): bind launches to exact reviewed heads
body:
## Intent

Add a fail-closed `--expected-head` launch contract for fresh Treehouse workers and a targeted `--codex-native-provider` guard for native ChatGPT-backed Codex launches required by Sterna Harness V2.

## Exact candidate

- Base: `da9607d7bb945e499fd70d4bf548edb37247d0cc`
- Head: `bae092afbffeff3166676137d1a0176f307be29a`
- Fork branch: `FictionalHayes/firstmate:feat/exact-spawn-sha`

## Guarantees

- Origin-authorized exact SHA convergence.
- Expected-commit custody scanning for bytes, modes, index state, ignored files, and recursive submodules.
- Final `HEAD == expected` and cleanliness comparison immediately before worker launch.
- Both same-tree and changed-tree checkout races fail closed without launching a worker.
- Pinned Git, Claude, and Codex executables for exact-head launches.
- Literal sanitized worker environment built by the authorizing Firstmate process.
- Ambient Git configuration, `core.fsmonitor`, hooks, replacement objects, grafts, namespace, filter, index-flag, and clean-checkout defenses.
- API credentials and endpoint overrides omitted from native Claude and Codex workers.
- Durable guarded relaunch posture and pre-stop validation.
- No provider framework, API-key fallback, merge, or deployment.

## Threat model

The change fails closed against repository input, arbitrary refs, ordinary harness-controlled worktree races, dirty state, ambient Git/configuration, and provider environment drift. Arbitrary malicious same-UID host compromise capable of rewriting user-owned execution or credential state during execution is outside this V2 boundary.

## Validation

At exact head `bae092afbffeff3166676137d1a0176f307be29a`, the complete `fm-spawn-pool-base-freshen`, `fm-spawn-codex-native-provider`, `fm-control-relaunch`, and `fm-spawn-dispatch-profile` suites passed. Pinned ShellCheck 0.11.0, Bash syntax, and diff checks passed. The direct `core.fsmonitor` marker and hostile pane-daemon HOME/PATH/API-key regressions passed for Claude and Codex.

The three broader repository failures `fm-afk-return`, `fm-backlog-atomicity`, and `fm-calm-claude-mod` reproduce identically on the exact base and are classified as inherited: an existing AFK assertion, missing GNU `timeout` on macOS, and Bash 3.2 lacking `${var@Q}`.

GitHub currently reports no configured checks for this PR at the exact head. Maintainer approval and merge remain required. No live model or metered API call was made.

title: test(spawn): cover launch command delivery through pane transport
body:
## Intent

Approve a bounded Firstmate launch-command-delivery fix. A guarded Nungu API CI retry truncated the command before Claude started. Existing work must remain preserved; do not use an unchanged retry or bypass the selected worker runtime.

## What Changed
- Add `tests/fm-spawn-launch-delivery.test.sh`, a new suite asserting that spawn launch commands reach the pane's executable interface intact: a long single-quoted raw harness command (with mixed quoting and ~1800 chars of padding) must parse and execute in the destination shell with its full payload, including the trailing suffix, preserved.
- Cover the claude launch path: the delivered command must reach the pane, keep `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, route the brief through destination-shell command substitution, and preserve the generated `launch-brief.md` path.
- Register the new suite in `bin/fm-test-run.sh` and add trap-based cleanup (EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP/QUIT) that removes staged `/tmp/fm-launch-delivery-*` case directories.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change adds only a regression test suite and a one-line test-family registration over an already-merged production fix, follows the repo's established spawn-fixture patterns, and incorporates all previously accepted review fixes, leaving no reachable defect path in shipped code.

## Testing

Drove the launch-command-delivery contract live end-to-end through a real bin/fm-spawn.sh launch into an isolated Herdr lab session: a long quoted raw launch with literal command-substitution text reached the destination shell unchanged and executed, and a fresh claude worker launched through the staged source-file transport and reached processing (verified as the pane's foreground harness via herdr pane process-info). Evidence transcripts, staged launch files, and process info were preserved to the evidence directory; the lab session was torn down, the scratch treehouse pool removed, and the default Herdr session was never touched. The change's regression suite was also run through bin/fm-test-run.sh, but that execution is recorded as untested rather than a live pass because the prior payload did not establish a live product result for it.

ROOT=~/.no-mistakes/worktrees/558623ebb989/01M33ZXEVXY45A98PE3BWY7NPJ
LAB_HELPER=$ROOT/bin/fm-herdr-lab.sh
OUT_DIR=~/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M33ZXEVXY45A98PE3BWY7NPJ

fail() { echo "FAIL: $*" >&2; cleanup; exit 1; }
note() { echo "== $*"; }

# --- isolated lab session ----------------------------------------------------
unset HERDR_ENV HERDR_PANE_ID HERDR_TAB_ID HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID HERDR_SOCKET_PATH HERDR_SESSION

# Firstmate's documented test-harness escape hatch: this validation drives the
# real fm-spawn from a no-mistakes gate worktree (bin/fm-gate-refuse-lib.sh).
export FM_GATE_REFUSE_BYPASS=1
SESSION=$("$LAB_HELPER" name launch-delivery) || fail "could not name lab session"
TMP_ROOT=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/fm-launch-live.XXXXXX") || fail "mktemp"

WORKTREES=()
CLEANED=0
cleanup() {
  local wt
  [ "$CLEANED" = 1 ] && return 0
  CLEANED=1
  for wt in ${WORKTREES[@]+"${WORKTREES[@]}"}; do
    [ -n "$wt" ] && treehouse return --force "$wt" >/dev/null 2>&1
  done
  rm -rf -- /tmp/fm-launch-live-* 2>/dev/null
  "$LAB_HELPER" teardown "$SESSION" || echo "WARN: lab teardown reported failure" >&2
  rm -rf "$TMP_ROOT"
  return 0
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

note "provision lab session $SESSION (provision owns prepare + fleet tripwire)"
"$LAB_HELPER" provision "$SESSION" || fail "provision failed"
lab() { "$LAB_HELPER" run "$SESSION" "$@"; }

# --- throwaway scratch world -------------------------------------------------
FMHOME=$TMP_ROOT/home
PROJ=$TMP_ROOT/project
mkdir -p "$FMHOME/state" "$FMHOME/config" "$FMHOME/data" "$FMHOME/projects"
touch "$FMHOME/state/.last-watcher-beat"
mkdir -p "$PROJ"
git -C "$PROJ" init -q
printf '# scratch\n' > "$PROJ/README.md"
git -C "$PROJ" add README.md
git -C "$PROJ" -c user.name='Live Validation' -c user.email='live@example.invalid' commit -qm initial
TASK_A=launch-live-raw-a1
TASK_B=launch-live-claude-b1
for id in "$TASK_A" "$TASK_B"; do
  mkdir -p "$FMHOME/data/$id"
  cat > "$FMHOME/data/$id/brief.md" <<EOF
# Task
## Captain's intent
Disposable live validation of launch-command delivery for $id. Do nothing and remain idle.

## Firstmate spec
This brief exists only so the launch transport has a real file to stage.
EOF
done

spawn() { # <id> <launch...>
  local id=$1
  shift
  env -u HERDR_ENV -u HERDR_PANE_ID -u HERDR_SOCKET_PATH -u HERDR_TAB_ID -u HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID \
    HERDR_SESSION="$SESSION" FM_SPAWN_NO_GUARD=1 \
    FM_HOME="$FMHOME" FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE="$ROOT" \
    "$ROOT/bin/fm-spawn.sh" "$id" "$@" 2>&1
}

meta_field() { grep "^$2=" "$FMHOME/state/$1.meta" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | cut -d= -f2-; }

pane_read() { # <pane-id>
  lab pane read "$1" --source recent --lines 200 2>/dev/null
}

# --- Scenario A: long quoted raw launch through a real Herdr pane -------------
note "Scenario A: long quoted raw launch with literal command-substitution text"
MARKER_A=$TMP_ROOT/marker-a.txt
PAD=$(python3 -c "print('A'*1800)")
PAYLOAD="prefix 'single quoted' \"double quoted\" literal command substitution \$(printf should-not-run) $PAD suffix-after-long-padding"
PAYLOAD_Q=$(python3 -c 'import shlex,sys; print(shlex.quote(sys.argv[1]))' "$PAYLOAD")
MARKER_Q=$(python3 -c 'import shlex,sys; print(shlex.quote(sys.argv[1]))' "$MARKER_A")
RAW="/bin/sh -c $(python3 -c 'import shlex,sys; print(shlex.quote(sys.argv[1]))' "printf '%s\\n' $PAYLOAD_Q > $MARKER_Q")"

SPAWN_A_OUT=$TMP_ROOT/spawn-a.out
spawn "$TASK_A" "$PROJ" --mode no-mistakes --yolo off --harness "$RAW" --backend herdr >"$SPAWN_A_OUT" 2>&1 \
  || fail "scenario A spawn failed: $(cat "$SPAWN_A_OUT")"
WORKTREES+=("$(meta_field "$TASK_A" worktree)")
echo "-- spawn A transcript:"; cat "$SPAWN_A_OUT"

PANE_A=$(meta_field "$TASK_A" herdr_pane_id)
[ -n "$PANE_A" ] || fail "no herdr_pane_id recorded for $TASK_A: $(cat "$FMHOME/state/$TASK_A.meta" 2>/dev/null)"
note "task A pane: $PANE_A"

DEADLINE=$(( $(date +%s) + 90 ))
while [ ! -s "$MARKER_A" ] && [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$DEADLINE" ]; do sleep 2; done
[ -s "$MARKER_A" ] || { pane_read "$PANE_A" > "$OUT_DIR/live-lab-scenario-a-pane-timeout.txt" || true; fail "marker never written; launch command did not execute in the pane"; }
DELIVERED=$(cat "$MARKER_A")
[ "$DELIVERED" = "$PAYLOAD" ] || fail "delivered payload differs from the intended launch payload"
case "$DELIVERED" in
  *'$(printf should-not-run)'*) : ;;
  *) fail "literal command-substitution text did not survive as literal text" ;;
esac
note "marker content matches payload byte-for-byte; substitution stayed literal"

pane_read "$PANE_A" > "$TMP_ROOT/pane-a.txt" || fail "pane read failed"
STAGED_A=$(ls -d /tmp/fm-"$TASK_A"+* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$STAGED_A" ] || fail "no staged launch namespace /tmp/fm-$TASK_A+*"
STAGED_A_FILE=$(find "$STAGED_A" -name 'launch*' -type f 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$STAGED_A_FILE" ] || fail "no staged launch file under $STAGED_A"
cat "$STAGED_A_FILE" > "$OUT_DIR/live-lab-scenario-a-staged-launch.txt"
case "$(cat "$STAGED_A_FILE")" in
  *'suffix-after-long-padding'*) : ;;
  *) fail "staged launch lost the long-command suffix; transport truncated it" ;;
esac
LIT_SUB='$(printf should-not-run)'
case "$(cat "$STAGED_A_FILE")" in
  *"$LIT_SUB"*) : ;;
  *) fail "staged launch lost the literal command-substitution text" ;;
esac
if grep -q "^\. '.*launch" "$TMP_ROOT/pane-a.txt"; then
  note "pane received the staged short source line (not a typed long literal)"
  grep "^\. '.*launch" "$TMP_ROOT/pane-a.txt" | head -1 > "$TMP_ROOT/pane-a-source-line.txt" || true
else
  note "NOTE: staged source line not visible in recent capture (may have scrolled)"
fi
cp "$TMP_ROOT/pane-a.txt" "$OUT_DIR/live-lab-scenario-a-pane.txt"
note "Scenario A PASS"

# --- Scenario B: claude launch delivered via staged source file ---------------
note "Scenario B: claude worker starts fresh through the staged source and reaches processing"
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR_B=$TMP_ROOT/claude-config
mkdir -p "$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR_B"
SPAWN_B_OUT=$TMP_ROOT/spawn-b.out
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR_B" \
  spawn "$TASK_B" "$PROJ" --mode no-mistakes --yolo off claude --backend herdr >"$SPAWN_B_OUT" 2>&1 \
  || fail "scenario B spawn failed: $(cat "$SPAWN_B_OUT")"
WORKTREES+=("$(meta_field "$TASK_B" worktree)")
echo "-- spawn B transcript:"; cat "$SPAWN_B_OUT"

PANE_B=$(meta_field "$TASK_B" herdr_pane_id)
[ -n "$PANE_B" ] || fail "no herdr_pane_id recorded for $TASK_B"
note "task B pane: $PANE_B"

# The staged launch namespace is the on-disk source the pane sources; assert the
# complete claude command there (the exact bytes the destination shell reads).
STAGED=$(ls -d /tmp/fm-"$TASK_B"+* 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$STAGED" ] || fail "no staged launch namespace /tmp/fm-$TASK_B+*"
STAGED_LAUNCH=$(find "$STAGED" -name 'launch*' -type f 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$STAGED_LAUNCH" ] || fail "no staged launch file under $STAGED"
STAGED_CONTENT=$(cat "$STAGED_LAUNCH")
echo "$STAGED_CONTENT" > "$OUT_DIR/live-lab-scenario-b-staged-launch.txt"
case "$STAGED_CONTENT" in
  *'claude --dangerously-skip-permissions'*) : ;;
  *) fail "staged launch is missing the claude command" ;;
esac
case "$STAGED_CONTENT" in
  *"$FMHOME/data/$TASK_B/launch-brief.md"*) : ;;
  *) fail "staged launch lost the brief path" ;;
esac
LIT_CMDSUB='$('
case "$STAGED_CONTENT" in
  *"$LIT_CMDSUB"*) : ;;  # claude brief is read through command substitution
  *) fail "staged launch lost the command-substitution brief read" ;;
esac
note "staged launch carries the complete claude command, brief path, and brief command-substitution"

# Reached processing: poll the real pane's OS-level foreground process until a
# verified harness (claude) is running in it, then record the pane's own view.
proc_json=''
DEADLINE=$(( $(date +%s) + 90 ))
while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$DEADLINE" ]; do
  proc_json=$(lab pane process-info --pane "$PANE_B" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if printf '%s' "$proc_json" | jq -e '
    .result.type == "pane_process_info"
    and ([.result.process_info.foreground_processes[]?
          | ((.argv // [])[0] // .argv0 // "" )] | map(test("claude")) | any)
  ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 2
done
printf '%s' "$proc_json" | jq . > "$OUT_DIR/live-lab-scenario-b-process-info.json" 2>/dev/null \
  || printf '%s' "$proc_json" > "$OUT_DIR/live-lab-scenario-b-process-info.json"
printf '%s' "$proc_json" | jq -e '
  .result.type == "pane_process_info"
  and ([.result.process_info.foreground_processes[]?
        | ((.argv // [])[0] // .argv0 // "" )] | map(test("claude")) | any)
' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  || fail "claude worker never showed as the pane's foreground harness (process-info: $(printf '%s' "$proc_json" | head -c 400))"
note "claude verified as the lab pane's foreground harness (reached processing)"

lab agent get "$PANE_B" 2>/dev/null | jq . > "$OUT_DIR/live-lab-scenario-b-agent-state.json" 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 3   # let the claude TUI paint before the pane capture
pane_read "$PANE_B" > "$TMP_ROOT/pane-b.txt" || fail "pane B read failed"
cp "$TMP_ROOT/pane-b.txt" "$OUT_DIR/live-lab-scenario-b-pane.txt"
if grep -q "^\. '.*launch" "$TMP_ROOT/pane-b.txt"; then
  note "pane B shows the staged source line"
fi
note "pane B capture (first 25 lines):"
head -25 "$TMP_ROOT/pane-b.txt"
note "Scenario B PASS (delivery contract proven against the real pane; worker reached processing)"

note "ALL LIVE SCENARIOS PASSED"
cleanup
exit 0

title: fix(spawn): pass muse max effort through unchanged instead of remapping to ultra
body:
### What this does
Passes muse `max` reasoning effort through unchanged as `--reasoning-effort max` instead of remapping it to `ultra`. Retains `ultra` as an option for models that support it.

### Why it is needed
The previous mapping remapped `max` -> `ultra`, written when muse 0.1.0 did not have a `max` level. muse 1.3.0 supports both `max` and `ultra`. However, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` does not support `ultra` and silently degrades `ultra` to `xhigh` instead of failing, causing worker sessions requesting `max` effort to run a tier lower at `xhigh`. This was verified via the effective level reported in the worker pane footer while `effort=max` was recorded in metadata.

### Verification
- `bash -n bin/fm-spawn.sh` clean.

title: fix(teardown): honor symlinked Treehouse roots
body:
### What this does
Teardown now resolves physical paths when comparing a worktree path against Treehouse pool registry entries, ensuring that symlinked Treehouse roots are properly recognized and returned to the pool.

### Why it is needed
When Treehouse roots or worktree parent directories are symlinked, string comparison between the worktree path and the registry entry failed to match. As a result, teardown could not identify the slot as a Treehouse pool slot, skipping clean slot release and leading to orphaned or unreturned pool slots.

### Verification
- `bash -n bin/fm-teardown.sh` clean.
- Unit test in `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` (`teardown returns a slot whose recorded path and Treehouse registry path differ only by a symlink`) passes alongside the existing teardown regression tests.

title: fix(bin): let a clone's firstmate.deployBranch override the stale forge default
body:
## Summary

`bin/fm-spawn.sh` ran `git remote set-head origin --auto` on every pooled-worktree spawn, resolving the FORGE default branch and rewriting the clone-shared `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`. For a repo whose real deploy branch is not the forge default, this had two effects: `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh` permanently compared against the wrong branch and reported STUCK forever, and the spawn's own base resolution prepared the pooled worktree on the stale branch. On `ecstatic-starfish-prod`, whose forge default `main` is eight months stale while the real deploy branch is `prod`, a previously merged migration file went missing from the captain's working copy because of this.

This adds `firstmate.deployBranch`, an explicit per-clone git config key naming a project's real deploy branch, and makes every place that resolves a project's base branch honor it:

- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` (pooled worktree base) - skips `git remote set-head` entirely when the key is set, since that call rewrites a clone-shared ref other tools still trust.
- `bin/fm-fleet-sync.sh` (sync comparison base)
- `bin/fm-review-diff.sh` (review diff base)
- `bin/fm-merge-local.sh` (local-only fast-forward target)
- `bin/fm-teardown.sh` (content-in-default landed-work fallback and the local-only unmerged-commits check)
- `bin/fm-ff-lib.sh` and `bin/fm-tangle-lib.sh` (firstmate's own primary-checkout/secondmate-home base resolution)

All six/seven resolvers now delegate to one shared `fm_default_branch()` in `bin/fm-deploy-branch-lib.sh` (resolution order: `firstmate.deployBranch` -> `origin/HEAD` -> local `main`/`master`), replacing six near-identical private copies. An unset key leaves every site's behavior unchanged. A key naming a branch that does not resolve is never silently ignored: every caller's existing refusal now names the key and value as the source, without asserting a cause (branch absence) the code never actually established - a fetch failure can also mean the branch exists but origin is unreachable, and the message says so.

**Limitation, stated plainly:** merging this alone changes no clone. The key must be set per clone (`.agents/skills/project-management/SKILL.md` now documents this as an explicit add/clone step: confirm the branch exists on origin, set the key, and check that branch out in the clone). A clone re-created later without following that step silently loses the setting and the original fault returns.

Verified against the safety-critical question of whether a misconfigured key could make `fm-teardown.sh`'s landed-work checks over-report work as landed (it cannot: both checks require exact equality - byte-identical final tree content, or literal commit-object reachability - properties that don't weaken based on which branch name is fed in), and against the live `ecstatic-starfish-prod`/`ecstatic-contractor-console`/`windows-direct-events-app` clones, which already have the key set.

## Test plan
- [x] `bin/fm-lint.sh` (shellcheck + actionlint) clean
- [x] `tests/fm-spawn-pool-base-freshen.test.sh`, `tests/fm-fleet-sync.test.sh`, `tests/fm-review-diff.test.sh`, `tests/fm-teardown.test.sh` pass, including new regression coverage for: the configured branch overriding the stale forge default without moving `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`; the unset-key fallback being unchanged; a misconfigured key naming a branch absent from origin failing loudly; a misconfigured key naming a real-but-wrong branch never causing teardown to report unlanded work as landed; an unreachable origin never producing a false absence claim.
- [x] Full no-mistakes pipeline (review, test, document, lint) green on this branch

title: fix(bin): recognize the GitHub Copilot CLI as a session-lock harness
body:
## What
Adds `copilot` (the GitHub Copilot CLI's process name) to the session-lock
harness identity in `bin/fm-session-lock-lib.sh` (`FM_HARNESS_RE` /
`FM_HARNESS_NAMES`), anchored exactly like `pi`/`omp` — the bare word only,
so unrelated paths/args containing "copilot" are never mistaken for the
harness.

## Why
Running Firstmate under the GitHub Copilot CLI left every session unable
to verify fleet-lock ownership (`bin/fm-lock.sh` reports "error: cannot
locate harness process in ancestry"), forcing permanent read-only mode: no
spawn, steer, merge, drain, or supervision repair possible.

## Scope
This is a narrow session-lock identity fix only. It intentionally does
**not** add `copilot` to the crew-dispatch harness list in `AGENTS.md` /
`bin/fm-harness.sh`, which would require full harness-adapters
verification (launch flags, trust-dialog handling, busy-state and
turn-end extensions) that the Copilot CLI has not gone through yet as a
spawn target.

## Testing
Ran `tests/fm-session-lock-ancestry.test.sh` (all cases pass, including a
new `test_copilot_anchored_name_detects_as_harness` case verifying the
anchored match and that substrings like `copilothelper`/`gh-copilot` are
correctly rejected).
